measuredFidelity.note: The rig's 6.75-degree leg splay (render.leg-stance) settled ankle daylight at 48.5% against the concept's 46.9%. Round 7 then found that Junebug's SIGNATURE idle pose carried an 8-degree inward leg roll, authored when the rig ran its legs straight down, which closed the ankles to 0.325ft against the bind pose's 0.756 and failed rubric 3.12 in idle while the bind-pose render this command reads stayed correct. The same roll was in all five signature idles and was removed from all of them; an FK sweep now reads every idle within 2% of bind. Re-measured 2026-08-12 after the detector itself was rebuilt to work for the whole roster: the backdrop is now sampled per column (seven sheets are vignetted past the old tolerance), a column counts as occupied by fraction rather than by any single pixel, and the shoe's two tones are read off the concept instead of the hardcoded red/cream that was Junebug's own shoe. Her shoe deltas TIGHTENED, from +2.23/+2.93 under the old classifier to +0.43/-0.78 as tone shares (41.2/25.5 concept against 41.6/24.8 delivered); the round-7 critic note below quotes the old red/cream figures and is left as the record of what was measured then.

frontProfileSilhouette.label: front/profile silhouette
frontProfileSilhouette.note: The large read is right and it is right by measurement, not by eye: head 34.0% of figure height against the turnaround's 33.9% (+0.10), head width:height 0.82 against 0.84, ankle daylight 48.5 against 46.9. With colour stripped she is still unmistakably the scowling kid with a bun, a headband and a swept tail. Held off 5 by butt-joined primitives, and I re-observed all three the round-7 critic named, each cropped at 4-10x from the region I cite. (1) BUN/CROWN SHELF, junebug-front-review.png x 220-330 y 55-115: the bun sits on the crown ring with a hard vertical step at BOTH silhouette edges and a shadow line across its base — no fillet, a visible corner, dead centre in the front view. (2) HEADBAND STUB, junebug-profile-review.png x 285-370 y 55-165 at 10x over a magenta backdrop: the band's rear end is a flat-cut rectangle terminating in silhouette against true background, where the concept sweeps it behind the ear to the nape. (3) PONYTAIL TIP, x 290-520 y 40-310: the tail tube ends on a flat circular cut and a separate smaller blob is stuck onto it, the seam a full crease ring with a notch either side, against a concept tip that tapers to a drawn arrowhead. A fourth: the pelvis is a flat-bottomed slab that overhangs the thigh tubes with a hard horizontal ledge across the whole hip, visible on the front board at 4x (x 180-360 y 370-420) and on both profile boards. Nothing is severed — a connected-component pass over all four boards returns exactly one component each.

headBodyProportions.label: head/body proportions
headBodyProportions.note: Child proportion is exact and measured, not asserted: head height delta +0.10 points, head aspect -0.02, ankle daylight +1.61 — every 6b metric inside tolerance, and the head:body read is the turnaround's, never the proxy's. The A-pose boards hold the drawn stance with the arms down and daylight between the thighs and calves, so 3.12 passes on the board and again in the run still. The second clause of the 4 bar — 'joints read as connected forms' — is where it stops. The pelvis-to-thigh is the offender: build_leg's top ring simply terminates at 1.72ft inside a separately built seat, so at 4x on both the front and profile boards you see a slab overhanging a narrower tube with a lip, not a hip. The knee is nearly formless too — the ring table runs 0.180 at the knee against 0.172 just above it, a 5% swell that renders as a straight tapering cylinder in profile. It stays a 4 because the joints that carry motion hold: the run still shows a round deltoid under the sleeve cap, a continuous elbow line and a knee that bends without tearing, and the jersey hem covers the pelvis ledge at every gameplay camera.

hairMass.label: hair mass
hairMass.note: The one category below the floor, and the deciding clause is the 4 bar's own words: 'one designed mass'. What ships is four stacked primitives with five visible joins. MEASURED first. Default band (5-45% of head height) reads 1.38 minima/row against the concept's 3.82 — 36% of the strand count at 146% of the prominence. That band is not trustworthy on this kid: on both sheets it spans the headband, whose two edges count as FALSE creases, so I re-ran it on a hair-only band. At 2-14% (bun crest and crown, above the band on both sheets) the concept reads 3.00 minima/row and the delivered reads 0.04 — 1% of the concept's strand count. At 2-22%, 1%. At 2-30%, 8%. The bun is a mathematically featureless dome, which the rubric caps at 4 on its own. Then the joins. (a) The bun butt-joins the crown on a hard shelf with a corner at both silhouette edges (front board 10x, x 220-330 y 55-115) and the toon outline pass draws it as a graphic line at gameplay scale in junebug-runtime-hero.png. (b) The hair tie is a FLAT QUAD SLAB, not a wrap: at 10x over magenta it is a single plane crossing in front of the tail whose lower edge is a hard flat cut with true background beneath it, and at gameplay scale in the run still it reads as a yellow tab stuck to the side of the head. (c) True background — alpha 0, sampled at (310,72) and (315,80) of junebug-profile-review.png — shows through the notch between the bun and the ponytail root, so the two masses do not touch; the tail hangs off the head through a narrow neck below the tie. (d) The tip blob. The 4 clauses it does pass are real and worth saying: the hairline is a proper sculpted widow's-peak that reads clean against skin from the front, there is no bare-skull read from any angle, and the headband arch itself is the best-authored accessory on the sheet.

clothingConstruction.label: clothing construction
clothingConstruction.note: The strongest sculpted category. Garments read as constructed at 5x on the A-pose board: the V-collar is a rounded piping TUBE rather than a painted line, the placket carries three raised button studs, the sleeves have two white stripes plus a real white cuff band, the belt is a band with two loops and a buckle, the knicker gathers into a darker cuff, the sock has its own band, and the shoe has a distinct lighter midsole slab and a red toe cap. The shoe's split is measured, not eyeballed: dominant tone 63.7% of the band against the concept's 64.7, second tone 31.1 against 27.2, mean saturation 34.9 against 36.8. Off 5 on the laces, which are three raised rectangular slabs on the vamp — they do not cross, have no eyelets and no weave, and on the right shoe of the front board one slab breaks the shoe's silhouette (x 160-390 y 590-710 at 4x). Secondary: the jersey hem is a flat horizontal slab cut with square corners rather than a hem that falls over the hip.

faceExpressionRead.label: face/expression read
faceExpressionRead.note: The face is a FORM, and I checked the specific things that separate a form from a sticker. A real nose breaks the profile with a defined tip and a nostril underside (junebug-profile-review.png x 210-320 y 110-240 at 8x). No decal-island seam anywhere — I looked for one at 8-10x on both the front and the profile and the atlas wraps the cheek and temple planes continuously. The ears are the best-constructed detail on the whole model: outer helix rim, inner concha shadow, and a lobe sitting against the skull, which settles 3.10 with no ambiguity. Features are legible at hero scale and the angled scowl brows still read at 40px. The chest patch I thought was a texture island at 4x is a specular gradient — resolved at 10x, not a defect. Held off 5 by the mouth. At rest it is a thin flat stroke a few pixels tall, close to the 'collapses to a line' the rubric warns about, and the expression RANGE does not survive: I pixel-diffed a 46x36 mouth box across the four runtime stills and grin/cheer/tongue are the same mouth (grin vs cheer 99 of 4968 channels differ by more than 12, max 39; cheer vs tongue 202, max 70) while only angry is distinct (650-669, max 120). Cropping the source atlas confirms it is the asset, not the capture instrument: cells 1, 10 and 11 are three near-identical open smiles, so the tongue cell has no tongue out and the cheer cell is no wider than the grin. All four stills are genuinely painted — byte sizes 291673/291988/292081/292276, a 0.2% spread, and all four show grass, sky and the character.

heroAndFieldScale.label: hero + 40px read
heroAndFieldScale.note: Identity survives both ends. At hero (junebug-runtime-hero.png, devstats reads 'model model', so this is the delivered GLB and not proxy evidence) the read is complete: scowl brows, big eyes, white headband arch, dark bun, tail swept to her left. I generated my own 40px read by resizing the front board to 40px tall, and every load-bearing element holds — dark bun over a white band, red top, pink pants, red socks, white shoes, and the angled brows are still two dark marks that say 'determined'. Off 5 on two counts. First, in the FRONT view at field scale the ponytail is entirely hidden behind her, so at 40px she is a bun-and-headband kid and the signature tail — the thing the turnaround draws an arrow at — contributes nothing to the read from the camera the fielder is most often seen from. Second, the tie reads at hero as a flat yellow tab rather than a wrap (junebug-runtime-run.png x 415-595 y 140-290 at 6x), which is a hero-scale accessory defect, not a hair-only one.

priorHumanReview.verdict: approved — reviewed the shipped model in production at https://srgirsky.github.io/recess-sports/ after rounds 5-7 rebuilt the shoe as one lasted upper, reshaped the ear, deepened the run's arm swing, mirrored the face columns and restored the splayed stance in every signature idle. The six category scores recorded here are the round-7 independent critic's, not the sculptor's.

The tongue cell shows no tongue out and the cheer is no wider than the grin, so three of the four emotional beats the draft card and the win/loss presentation lean on collapse to one read. Rubric 5.2; 3.14 itself passes (lips, teeth and tongue are all present and legible in the open cells).
junebug-runtime-swing.png captures swing_contact at the marker with EMPTY HANDS — no bat prop. It is fine as deformation evidence but it cannot show rubric 4.5's 'bat meets ball'.

The jersey hem is a flat horizontal slab cut with square corners rather than a hem that falls over the hip.

NOT a defect, recorded so the next critic does not re-report it: the pale quad on the chest visible at 4x resolves at 10x as a specular gradient, not a texture-island seam. Ears are fully constructed (rim, concha shadow, lobe) and are the best detail on the model — EarSpec/build_ear are imported from sculptlib. The near-side eye in the profile board is foreshortened, which is correct for a true orthographic 90-degree view. All four runtime-face stills are painted.

frontProfileSilhouette.label: front/profile silhouette
frontProfileSilhouette.note: The large read is a MUSHROOM, not a ball cap. I measured both boards myself, alpha-thresholded row by row. Delivered front: cap max width 192px at row 175, then a 60px cliff to 132px at row 190, and the widest point of head-plus-hair below the cap is 144px (row 220) — head/cap = 0.75. Concept front view (spec box 86,391,129,871): cap max width 260px at row 246, head-plus-hair max width 271px at row 270 — head/cap = 1.04. That is a 29-point inversion of the drawing's own relationship: in the art the hair mass is the widest thing on the head and the cap sits down onto it; in the delivery the cap flares 33% wider than everything under it and background shows through the overhang on both sides in front, A-pose and the swing camera. Second defect, the bill: on the profile board the bill is a wafer of constant 8-10px section over a 58px projection (droop measured 24px over 56px = 23deg, so the 22deg droop and the 1.100 reach ARE fine as stated); on the concept sheet the profile bill is a contiguous run 41px thick at the tip (col 988) thickening to 66-68px at its root (col 946) over a ~44px projection. Normalised on head height (delivered 189px, concept ~254px) that is 4.2-5.3% section delivered against 16-27% concept — the bill is roughly twice as long and a quarter as thick as the drawing's, and in profile it reads as a knife blade or an antenna sticking out of the skull. The recorded note calls this 'a real forward duckbill'; it is not. Third: transitions are butt-joined primitives — shorts hem into thigh, sock into shoe, neck into collar are all cylinder-into-cylinder with a hard occlusion line, and the cap crown has a visible cone apex. Nothing is severed (no empty row inside the figure in any of the four boards) and the two legs are genuinely two legs.

headBodyProportions.label: head/body proportions
headBodyProportions.note: The metered proportions pass and I re-took them: head height 34.6% vs concept 35.0 (delta -0.41, ok), head width:height 0.99 vs 1.05 (delta -0.06, ok), visible face left 26.6 vs 22.4 and right 27.1 vs 26.8 with asymmetry 0.52 (ok), ankle daylight 51.7 vs 56.9 (ok). So 6b.1/6b.3/6b.4 are green and rubric 3.13's aspect check passes. What holds this to 3 is the second half of the category — 'joints read as connected forms'. Cropped at 4x, the legs are smooth cones from the shorts hem to the sock top with no knee, no patella plane and no calf swell; the shorts hem is a flat cut with the thigh cylinder emerging from it; at rest in the A-pose and hero the shoulder is a soft lump and the sleeve is a straight tube to the cuff with no elbow form; the neck is a plain column meeting the collar at a hard ring. The concept's limbs are chunky toddler forms with an obvious calf and knee; the delivered limbs are markedly thinner relative to the torso even though the head ratio is in tolerance.

hairMass.label: hair mass
hairMass.note: The worst category by a wide margin, and it is a construction failure, not a taste call. Band choice first: `npm run measure:strands -- calls_shot` at the DEFAULT 5-45% of head height reports concept 4.91 minima/row at prominence 16.9 against delivered 0.00 at 0.0 — 0% of count, 0% of prominence. But for THIS character the default band is crown-downward across the CAP (concept head 129-388, so the band is rows 142-245, i.e. cap dome to just under the brim), so its 0.00 is really 'the delivered cap dome has no panel seam and no texture', and on the concept side the 4.91 is partly cap seams and brim edge, not hair. I therefore re-ran on the rows where Theo's hair actually shows: 25-55% gives 0.84 vs 5.62 (15% of count, 159% of prominence) and 30-60% gives 1.14 vs 6.59 (17%, 176%). Those bands do reach the brows and the eye line, so some concept minima there are false creases (skin/hair and brow edges) — which makes 15-17% an OVER-estimate of what he carries, not an under-estimate. Cause verified in the builder, not inferred: `build_hair` in scripts/v2/blender/sculpt-theo-source.py uses `segments = 10` with `wave = 1.0 + 0.05 * cos(6 * theta)` — 1.67 columns per lobe against the ~4 Nyquist needs, and only 5% amplitude, so the wave is unrepresentable twice over. But the ratio is not even the real problem. `HAIR_LEVELS` maxes at `half_x = 0.455` while the skull's lateral half-width is `HEAD_RADII[0] * face_half_scale` = 0.400 x up to 1.08 = 0.432, so the entire hair shell is a skin-tight liner adding at most 0.023 (5%) of volume. The drawing's hair is the widest mass on the head (271px vs the cap's 260px); the delivery's is 144px against a 192px cap. Consequences, all cropped and looked at: the front board and the front A-pose board show TWO small dark triangular wedges at the temples plus two nubs below the ears and nothing else — no fringe, no hairline, bare skin across the whole forehead, temples and cheeks. In the four `-runtime-face-*.png` close-ups at 4x the hairline is a ragged sawtooth of dark specks along the cap edge that reads as dirt or stubble, produced by the piecewise `hair_window_z` step at |x|=0.42 sampled by only 10 columns. In `theo-runtime-swing.png` — a real gameplay camera, cropped at 5x — the back of the head is a small brown patch under the cap with a LARGE bare skin nape below it, and a skin-coloured ear form lying on top of the hair with a jagged seam. Rubric 3.3 bars a bare-skull read from any gameplay angle and requires the hairline to read from the front; both fail outright. The recorded note ('hair lifted to a legible deep brown with enlarged fringe wisps, ear-top flips both sides, and a covered nape in profile and swing views') is contradicted by the swing still it cites.

clothingConstruction.label: clothing construction
clothingConstruction.note: Three of nine measure:fidelity metrics are OFF and all three are the shoe: dominant tone of the band 88.4 vs concept 37.6 (tol 8), second tone 11.6 vs 61.4 (tol 8), mean saturation 13.6 vs 28.1 (tol 4). Cropped at 6x, the shoe is a near-white clog — a grey collar, three hairline lace straps, a tiny dark tick at the toe and a cupsole band barely a shade warmer than the upper; the concept's dark toe bumper and dark outsole edge are effectively gone. The sculpt script's own comment ('the charcoal saddle never reaches the bottom-9% window') and the recorded note ('shoe-band OFF cause accepted') explain the metric away, but the detector reads the CONCEPT's own pair as cream #ecddcc + tan #d9b68b at 37.6/61.4 — charcoal is not what it is comparing — and the saturation metric is independent of the split and also fails by 3.5x its tolerance. Second defect: the cap's cream team panel is a PAINTED GRADIENT, not a constructed edge. At front-board row 150 (cap 180px wide) the teal-to-cream ramp runs x196 (#9ea4a2) to x228 (#d7d2ca) = 32px = 18% of the cap width, per side; on the concept sheet at row 175 (cap 179px) the same boundary resolves between x197 (#39626d) and x202 (#fbedd0), i.e. under 5px = 2.8%. Six times too soft. Cause: `build_cap` colours 12 dome columns per vertex with `colour = TEAM_MASK if (frontness > 0.62 and z < 3.92) else TEAL`, so Gouraud smears the seam across a whole 30deg column. Judging TEAM_MASK on extent and placement only (not colour): placement is correct, centred front, but extent is over — the cream plateau is 45% of the cap width against the concept panel's 37%, and with the ramps the cream dominates ~80% of the cap face, where the drawing shows one crisp wedge of six. Third defect: in `swing_contact` five hard-edged cream parallelograms punch through the teal jacket back at mid-back; I sampled them at #bcb390 and #c1b99a against the jacket's #053d48, so they are cream-hued geometry (a tee or inboard sleeve ring emerging), not a teal specular — an interpenetration that reads at gameplay scale. Credit where it is due, which is why this is a 2 and not a 1: the jacket is genuinely constructed (separate shell with a fold-back front edge, a cream tee centre panel, cream sleeves, a striped rib hem, collar flaps), the socks have a proud roll with two crisp teal stripes, and the shoe does have a cupsole and lace straps.

faceExpressionRead.label: face/expression read
faceExpressionRead.note: The eyebrows are authored and invisible, and they are this character's signature. I opened `assets/v2/source/theo-face-atlas.png`: every one of the 16 cells carries a pair of thick black brows, and not one of them renders in any still — front board, front A-pose board, hero, run, and all four `-runtime-face-*.png`. The reason is geometric and the script states the numbers itself: the brow anchor lands at z 3.304, while the cap dome's lowest ring is z 3.290 with half-widths 0.650/0.595 and y_centre -0.030, so the cap shell sits in front of the brow row from any front-facing camera and swallows it. Cropped at 6x, `angry` and `grin` differ by mouth alone — the eyes and the (absent) brows are identical — and Theo's cocky arched brow, present in all five concept views, never appears. On the positive side: all four expression stills ARE genuinely painted, not stubs (294,526 / 295,659 / 297,025 / 296,299 bytes, within 1% of each other, no 29% empty-canvas file), and rubric 3.14 passes on its own terms — the grin opens with teeth, tongue shows a tongue, cheer opens, angry frowns, all legible at draft-card crop. The nose is a real form (`nose_push`, verified in the builder) and it does break the profile — but on the profile board it reads as a sharp triangular beak rather than the drawing's small upturned button, and the socket dish is so shallow that the eyes read as flat decals with a soft blur. A face-island seam is visible as a dashed scribe down the cheek just in front of the ear in the grin still. Ears are constructed, not bumps — `EarSpec(center=(0.020, 3.230), radii=(0.1550, 0.1650))` and `build_ear` are both present, and the profile crop shows a rim, an inner hollow and a lobe — but the form is a crescent flange with a hard dark notch behind it and, in profile, its front edge sits almost against the eye decal with no cheek between them.

heroAndFieldScale.label: hero + 40px read
heroAndFieldScale.note: Hero (`theo-runtime-hero.png`) does report `model model` at 28.5k tris, so 4.1 is satisfied and this is model evidence — but the read it delivers is 'a kid in an oversized two-tone bowl', with no hair and no brows anywhere on the head. Every distinguishing mass the drawing gives him except the cap is missing, and the cap's own shape is the mushroom described above, so at hero he is interchangeable with any other cap kid. The 40px strip on the board is a pale blob over a pale body with a darker band across the middle: the highest-contrast element in the concept — the black hair mop that in the drawing is 271px wide against a 260px cap — contributes zero pixels at 40px, so there is no memorable read left to survive (3.9 fails). Separately, the integration evidence is both stale and a proxy: `docs/v2/concepts/theo-in-game-review.png` was last written by commit 97a17cd (2026-08-09) while the boards come from 4875d2c (2026-08-15), and the image shows capsule arms with sphere caps, ball-jointed black legs, slab feet and a floating cream V on the chest — the proxy body, not the shipped GLB. Section 4.1's rule is that proxy evidence is never fidelity evidence, so section 6 is effectively unwalked at this revision.

headBodyProportions.label: head/body proportions
headBodyProportions.note: The two measured proportion metrics are green and I will not score against them: head height 29.9% of figure vs concept 31.6% (delta -1.76, ok) and head width:height 1.08 vs 1.06 (ok). What fails is 3.2's second clause - joints reading as connected forms. The shin is a single constant-diameter dowel from knee to ankle (SKIN tube, radii 0.085/0.078/0.072) with no calf swell and no ankle; the knee is a butt joint between the navy thigh tube and the tan shin tube with a visible diameter step under the hem lip; the sleeve-to-arm transition is a ring followed by a smaller cylinder, a step you can see at 8x in the A-pose profile; the skull is a plain sphere with no jaw, chin taper or cheekbone. Separately, the kid is badly oversized against his own furniture: on the sheet the wheel tops reach his elbow and the wheels flank his torso, delivered they reach his knee and sit entirely below his shorts. Both halves are child-proportioned in isolation; they are not proportioned to each other.

hairMass.label: hair mass
hairMass.note: Measured by me. Default 5-45% band reaches onto the forehead and brows on this head (delivered head 123-321, so the band runs 133-212, straight through the brow line), so I re-ran on a crown band: at 2-28% he carries 67% of the concept's strand count at 390% of its prominence; at 5-35% it is 74% / 355%; the default 5-45% gives 67% / 362%. The reading is stable and unambiguous - too few groups, each far too deep. What that is on screen: seven hard flat triangular fins on a thin skullcap, each a smooth featureless blade with no grouping inside it and near-black voids between. Two further divergences from the sheet: the fins splay radially like a crown in the front board where the sheet sweeps the whole mass up and rearward (the sculpt's own comment says the tips fold rearward - from the front they do not read that way), and the temples are bare skin well above the ear on both sides where the sheet brings hair down past ear-top with a defined sideburn. In game light the flat facets take a steel-blue specular so a #2A211C near-black crown reads grey-blue at gameplay distance (zoom-runtime-face-angry.png). No bare-skull hole from any angle and the spiky silhouette is genuinely memorable, which keeps this off a 2.

clothingConstruction.label: clothing construction
clothingConstruction.note: The garments are honestly constructed: teal collar ring, teal side panels, teal sleeve cuffs on the tee, and a darker SHORTS_DARK hem lip at the knee - all real geometry, not painted. The shoes are where this fails, and they fail measurably. The delivered sneaker is a SHOE-coloured lozenge tube with a flat WHITE tube slid under it: no toe, no heel, no ankle collar, no straps, no sole sidewall. measure:fidelity, my run: the shoe band's dominant tone is 60.9% against the concept's 79.1% (tol 8), the band's SECOND tone is 0.00% against the concept's 13.3% (tol 8) - the sheet's two-tone shoe split is not delivered at all - and band saturation is 26.5 vs 20.9 (tol 4). The sheet's sneakers are the second-most-detailed object on it (navy upper, two teal velcro straps, cream sole with a grey midsole band). Compounding it, the METAL footplate ellipsoid (0.0, -0.800, 0.385, half-extent 0.300/0.200/0.038) is buried inside the WHITE sole tube (sole bottom z 0.343 against footplate top 0.423) and pokes out through the outboard side of the sneaker as a bare grey cylinder stub - visible at 4x in zoom-runtime-hero.png, which is a rubric 3.8 interpenetration that reads at hero scale. faceExpressionRead.label: face/expression read
faceExpressionRead.note: The strongest category and the one thing on this asset that is close to done. Constructed brows, lidded eyes with iris, pupil and highlight, a smiling mouth with a real lip form, cheek blush, and ears that are properly built - I grepped the sculpt before judging and found EarSpec/build_ear with EAR_SPEC center (0.020, 3.000), radii (0.1450, 0.1550), and at 5x the outer rim, inner shadow and lobe are all present against the skull (3.10 passes). The concept-side 0.00 on the left is a detector artifact on the sheet, not a delivered defect, and I am not scoring it. All four expression stills read at gameplay distance: grin opens on teeth, tongue opens on teeth plus a pink tongue, angry furrows the brows and turns the mouth down (3.14 passes cleanly). Held to 4 rather than 5 because the nose is a very shallow button (nose_push, centre nz -0.20) that barely breaks the cheek plane in the profile board, and the skull is an undifferentiated sphere, so at the near-front gameplay angle the whole face still reads as painted onto a ball rather than cut into it.

heroAndFieldScale.label: hero + 40px read
heroAndFieldScale.note: The hero close-up is fine and in places good - at 4x the near drive wheel has a black tyre, a bold pushrim ring, ten silver spokes and a silver hub, and the frame reads as a lattice chassis. The field read is where his identity is lost. On the board's own 40-pixel zoom strip, cropped at 10x, he is a T-posed standing kid with two bare legs, a blue tee and a faint grey smudge below the shorts: the wheelchair is entirely gone. The same thing happens at the near-front gameplay camera in zoom-runtime-face-angry.png, where the chair is a few thin dark struts and two flat wheel edges and he reads as a kid standing behind a metal frame. His chair is his one memorable read and it does not survive to the sprite, which is exactly what 3.9 exists to catch. Two smaller contributors at the same scale: the caster is authored as an open torus (ring radius 0.130, tube radius 0.040) so the field shows through its centre at hero scale where the sheet has a solid blue caster wheel, and the pushrim, the only slot-3 team-accent geometry, is a hairline from the front so the team read has to come entirely from the 3/4 camera.

polishFindings: PRIMARY. The chair is half the mass the sheet gives it and sits too low on the figure: measured 43.6% lower-40% fill against the concept's 83.7%, chair top 61.1% down against 44.9%, chair width 43.4% of figure height against ~60%. Raise the seat/wheel assembly relative to the hip so the wheel tops reach his elbow as they do on the sheet, and thicken the seat, backrest and rails until the front board's lower half is a dense black-and-blue mass rather than open scaffolding. Everything else on this list is downstream of it.

The drive wheels read as flat parallel-sided black slabs with square-cut faceted ends in the front board, not as cambered ellipses. The camber is authored (WHEEL_CAMBER 0.115) but at 16 ring points and a 0.060 tube it does not survive the orthographic front view. Either increase the camber or give the tyre enough ring points that the lean reads as a curve.

The four frame rails per side terminate in tapered points hanging in mid-air (rail 1 ends at z 0.300, radius 0.036, i.e. z 0.264 with ground at 0) and cross in an unresolved X in the front board. Close the chassis: join the rails into axle bosses and a caster fork so no tube ends in space.

The METAL footplate ellipsoid is buried inside the WHITE sole tube (sole bottom z 0.343 vs footplate top z 0.423) and pokes out through the outboard side of the sneaker as a bare grey stub at hero scale - a 3.8 interpenetration. Drop the footplate ~0.06 so it sits under the sole, which also makes it read in profile, where it currently reads as absent.

The sneakers deliver none of the sheet's construction: no toe, no heel, no ankle collar, no teal velcro straps, and the two-tone sole is measured at 0.00% of the shoe band against the concept's 13.3%. This is the single measurable palette-fidelity miss on the asset.
The caster is an open torus (ring radius 0.130, tube radius 0.040) so the field shows through its middle at hero scale. The sheet's caster is a solid small wheel with a blue hub - fill the centre.

The shin is a constant-diameter dowel from knee to ankle with no calf and no ankle, and the knee is a butt joint with a visible diameter step under the hem lip. At the same time the navy thigh reads as a hard-topped box in the run and swing stills. Both need a taper and a rounded transition.

Hair: 67% of the concept's strand count at 390% of its prominence on the crown band. Seven flat blades that are too deep and too few. Per the roster finding this is a column-count (Nyquist) problem, not a depth problem - more groups with a sharper, shallower crease profile, not deeper voids.

The hair fins splay radially in the front board where the sheet sweeps the whole mass up and rearward, and the temples are bare skin well above the ear on both sides where the sheet brings hair down past ear-top with a sideburn. Bring the hairline down at the temples and rake the fins back.

The flat hair facets take a steel-blue specular in game light, so a #2A211C near-black crown reads grey-blue at gameplay distance (zoom-runtime-face-angry.png). Worth checking against the tonemapping gate before touching the swatch - this looks like normals, not colour.

The push rim, the only team-accent geometry on the asset, survives the front board as a 2px hairline, so the team read depends entirely on the 3/4 camera. Extent, not colour - widen or move it outboard of the tyre silhouette.

The skull is an undifferentiated sphere with no jaw or cheekbone and the nose is a very shallow button, so the otherwise excellent face still reads as painted onto a ball at the near-front gameplay angle. This is what holds face/expression at 4 rather than 5.

frontProfileSilhouette.note: The one thing this character is named for is measurably short. His tee at its widest is 28.9% of figure height (162px/561) against the concept's 34.0% (244px/717) - 15% narrow; in profile his torso is 24.8% deep at pct 58 against the concept's 29.9% at pct 56 - 17% shallow. Worse, the profile at 5x shows the tee is a hard-cornered BOX: a flat front face, a flat side face and a hard vertical crease between them running the full height of the garment, plus a flat horizontal hem cut. Rule 3.1's 5/5 forbids butt-joined primitives; this is below that - the primitive joins are visible in the silhouette itself. Two things I want on record as PASSING so nobody re-files them: legs are two legs (I measured max inter-leg daylight 35.0% of row span at pct 96, 34.2% at 94, 32.4% at 92, against the concept front figure's 33.0% at 88 and 26.6% at 90 - his legs are correct and I confirmed the leg thickness matches too, 10.2% of figH per leg vs the concept's 10.3%), and nothing is severed anywhere in board or runtime. headBodyProportions.label: head/body proportions
headBodyProportions.note: The best category and still not at the floor. The AUTO metrics are genuinely fine - measure:fidelity reports head height 27.9% vs concept 26.1% (+1.73, ok) and head width:height 1.10 vs 1.06 (+0.04, ok) - and I independently confirmed the legs are correctly thick, so the gross child proportion is right and this is not a proxy read. What fails is the second half of the rule, 'joints read as connected forms'. The shoulder is a truncated sleeve cone butted onto a flat shoulder plane: at 8x and 10x on the runtime hero and run stills there is a broken, dotted dark outline arc running from the collar out over the deltoid and down into the armpit, which is the toon outline firing on a shell intersection, and the diameter steps visibly where the sleeve ends and the bare arm begins - no round deltoid form survives. The elbow in swing_contact is a hard crease with a dark notch, two cylinders meeting at an angle, and the two forearms interpenetrate with a hard intersection line where they cross. The hand is a merged paddle with a single thumb nub and three shallow finger notches; in the profile A-pose it reads as a mitten. The neck is also a distinct visible cylinder with a collar ring above it, where the concept Big Lou has essentially no neck at all - his head sits straight on his shoulders, and that missing compression costs part of the 'big' read. 3.

hairMass.label: hair mass
hairMass.note: I ran measure:strands at four bands to be sure the finding was not an artifact of the default band reaching onto forehead and brows - 5-45% (the default), 5-28%, 3-22% and 2-18%. Every band says the same thing: delivered carries 52%, 43%, 38% and 33% of the concept's strand-minima count while carrying 204%, 204%, 183% and 175% of its prominence. That is the exact signature of a smooth mass with a handful of deep chunky gouges standing in for a dense fine grain, which rule 3.3 caps at 4 even when the silhouette is right - and here the silhouette is not right either. The concept is a tight buzz cut that hugs the skull with a faded temple and a clean straight hairline; the delivered hair is a thick bowl/mushroom helmet with real volume standing off the back of the skull, a hard front edge over the forehead, and a jagged stair-stepped notch at each temple where the hairline meets the sideburn (visible at 5x in the profile crop). The mass is designed as one piece, it reads front and side, and there is no bare-skull read from any angle I checked, so it clears the floor items - but it is the wrong haircut rendered as a featureless blob. 2.

clothingConstruction.label: clothing construction
clothingConstruction.note: Real credit first, because two things here are better than the rest of the asset: the shoe is genuinely constructed - cream toe cap, navy quarter, cream midsole, a dark outsole line and a short dark lace mark, all separately readable at 5x - and the sock has an actual cuff roll rather than a plain tube. Everything else fails. The stripe pitch is wrong by a large measured margin: 20px on a 561px figure (3.6% of figure height) against the concept's 37px on a 717px figure (5.2%), a 31% finer pitch, and because the delivered tee is also taller the band count over the garment is ~10 against the concept's ~5. Every stripe boundary is a soft ~4px vertex-colour gradient, not a constructed edge - I sampled a column at x=270 in the front A-pose and the transitions blur over four native pixels; the concept's are crisp. The tee is the box described above with no side seam, no sleeve cuff and no drape. The shorts are two flat-faced slabs with hard corners, no hem cuff, no waistband and no pocket, and they are 30% short (waistband matches the concept exactly at 64.7% vs 64.6% of figure height, but the hem lands at 73.1% against 76.7%). Under the shirt hem at the crotch there is a hard-edged near-black rectangle roughly 21x2 native px - I cropped that exact region at 16x and it is a flat black slab with crisp edges and no gradient, so it is not occlusion falloff; it is either a see-through gap or an untextured polygon, and it is the only 3.7 candidate I found. 2.

faceExpressionRead.label: face/expression read
faceExpressionRead.note: Two traps checked and cleared before scoring. Ears: I grepped the sculpt script and found `from sculptlib.ear import EarSpec, build_ear` with `EAR_SPEC = EarSpec(center=(0.020, 3.420), radii=(0.1600, 0.1700))`, and at 5x on the profile board the ear has an outer helix rim, a concha depression with an inner shadow and a lobe against the skull - 3.10 PASSES. Mouth: all four runtime-face stills are genuinely painted and genuinely distinct - grin is a closed smile with a teeth line, cheer is an open mouth with teeth and a dark throat, tongue is an open mouth with a pink tongue out, angry is angled brows over a downturned frown - and all four read at draft-card distance, so 3.14 PASSES. What fails is the form. The nose is authored as a soft displacement (`nose_push`, 'a broad soft button nose') rather than built geometry, and it shows: in the profile board the front edge runs 213,213,213,212,211,209,208,210,213,216 across the nose latitude - a 5px bump on a 155px head, 3.2% of head height, against the concept profile figure's 19px bump on a 185px head, 10.3%. Rule 3.5's 5/5 asks that a real nose break the profile; measured, it barely dents it, and in all four front expression stills the nose is invisible - eyes, brows, mouth, then blank cheek. The brows are angular dark slabs with hard straight lower edges whose outer ends abut and merge into the hairline, where the concept's are tapered arcs with clear forehead above them. And the ear is authored at radii 0.170 against head radius 0.520, i.e. 32.7% of head height (I measured 31% off the board) against the concept's 24% - about 35% oversize - which is why at the runtime hero camera, with the head turned away, the dominant feature of the close-up is a giant protruding ear disc and not the face at all. 2.

heroAndFieldScale.label: hero + 40px read
heroAndFieldScale.note: This is where the asset actually dies. I cropped the board's own 40-pixel zoom strip at 8x: the gold stripes are completely gone and the tee is a single undifferentiated cream blob. That is arithmetic, not opinion - a 20px band pitch on a 561px render is 1.4px per band at 40px height, below what the strip can resolve, and it is the direct consequence of the doubled stripe count under clothingConstruction. The one thing a child is meant to recognise Big Lou by on the field - bold broad gold-and-cream stripes on a wide round body - survives neither half of the read: the stripes alias away, and the silhouette is 15% narrow and 17% shallow so he does not read as a big kid either. At 40px he is a generic beige-shirted child. The hero read is separately weak: the ear dominates the close-up as described, the torso shows plainly faceted low-poly quads across the belly with visible shading discontinuities at 3x, and the shoulder-cap specular blows out over roughly 50 of the torso's 195 rows on both sides, erasing the stripe pattern exactly where the eye lands first. 3.9 FAILS. 2.

measuredFidelity.result:
measure:fidelity -- big_lou (concept front 330x712, delivered 451x560): head height 26.1 -> 27.9 (+1.73, ok); head w:h 1.06 -> 1.10 (+0.04, ok); shoe band dominant tone 82.7 -> 79.7 (-3.01, ok); shoe band second tone 16.3 -> 20.3 (+4.00, ok); shoe band mean saturation 16.9 -> 15.9 (-0.92, ok); daylight between ankles 0.00 -> 26.4 (+26.4, OFF tol 12 - this is 6b.4's bind-pose-vs-posed-drawing comparison, the concept front figure stands ankles together, so I read it as stance and did not widen anything); visible face left of centre 47.7 -> 44.2 (ok); right of centre 39.6 -> 44.2 (ok); face L/R asymmetry 0.00 -> 0.00 (ok). 1 metric outside tolerance.

measure:strands -- big_lou at four bands (stating the band because the 5-45% default reaches onto forehead and brows on a buzz cut): band 5-45% (default) concept 6.31 minima/row @ prominence 28.8 over 86 rows, delivered 3.27 @ 57.8 over 63 rows => 52% count / 201% prominence. Band 5-28%: 5.72 @ 15.5 vs 2.47 @ 31.7 => 43% / 204%. Band 3-22%: 6.00 @ 15.4 vs 2.30 @ 28.1 => 38% / 183%. Band 2-18%: 6.71 @ 14.8 vs 2.23 @ 25.8 => 33% / 175%. Every band agrees: far too few strand minima, far too deep.

My own measurements (concept front figure top y=106 bot y=822, figH=717px; delivered front/profile board top y=86 bot y=646, figH=561px; concept profile figure figH=722px):
- Inter-leg daylight, max gap as % of row span: delivered 32.4% @ pct92, 34.2% @ pct94, 35.0% @ pct96; concept front 28.4% @ pct86, 33.0% @ pct88, 26.6% @ pct90. Legs PASS, independently confirmed.
- Single-leg width: delivered 57px = 10.2% of figH @ pct80; concept 74px = 10.3% @ pct80. Match.
- Tee max width: delivered 162px = 28.9% of figH @ pct57; concept 244px = 34.0% @ pct57-59 (hue-32-55 shirt mask, background excluded). -15%.
- Profile torso max depth: delivered 24.8% of figH @ pct58 (peak of 23.5/24.6/24.6/24.8/24.6 across pct50-60); concept profile 29.9% @ pct56 (28.1/28.9/29.6/29.9/29.8 across pct50-58). -17%.
- Stripe pitch, front A-pose column x=270, band boundaries at y = 251,268,288,308,328,349,369,390,410,429 => pitch 20px on figH 561 = 3.6% of figH; concept column x=210, boundaries at y = 403,438,477,516,552 => pitch 35/39/39/36, mean 37.3px on figH 717 = 5.2% of figH. Delivered pitch 31% finer; band count over the tee ~10 vs ~5. At 40px figure height that is 1.4px per band -> stripes gone (verified by cropping the board's own 40px strip at 8x).
- Stripe edge softness: cream<->gold transition spans ~4 native px at 561px figure. Painted gradient, not a constructed edge.
- Shorts: navy run on both leg columns, delivered 64.7-73.1% of figure height (8.4% long); concept 64.6-76.7% and 65.0-76.7% (12.1% long). Waistband matches, hem 30% short.
- Shoe navy upper: delivered 93.6-96.3% of figure (2.7%); concept 89.5-95.5% (6.0%). Less than half height.
- Nose, profile front-edge x per row across the nose latitude: delivered 213,213,213,212,211,209,208,210,213,216 -> 5px protrusion on a 155px head = 3.2% of head height; concept 795,795,794,793,789,780,777,777,775,775,776,780 -> 19px on a 185px head = 10.3%. Delivered nose protrudes under one third as far.
- Head: delivered max head width 174px on head band 86-241 (155px) = 1.123 w:h measured my way; concept max head width 197px on head band 106-310 (204px) = 0.966. Delivered ~16% wider relative to its own height, and the excess is ears.
- Ear: vertical extent ~48px on a 155px head = 31% of head height; concept ear ~52px on a 213px head = 24%. Sculpt script authors EAR_SPEC radii (0.160, 0.170) against HEAD_RADII (0.500, 0.500, 0.520) = 32.7% of head height, confirming the board. Ear protrudes ~15px per side beyond the skull and is the widest point of the head silhouette.
- Crotch black slab: cropped at 16x, a flat near-black rectangle ~21x2 native px between the shirt hem and the shorts, crisp-edged with no gradient.
- Colour: on the fidelity board the gold stripe modal saturation is ~0.4 against the concept's ~0.8, but the runtime stills show the tee at full mustard - so this is board lighting, NOT a palette defect, and I am NOT filing it. Team accent is the sock roll-top (TEAM_MASK = E8DCC2, 'the sock roll-top - THE accent'), not the tee, so no colour judgement was made on any grey surface.
- Severed parts: none. Head, neck, torso, both arms, both hands, both legs and both feet are continuous in the front board, profile board, both A-pose boards and all three runtime clip stills.
- Shoulder/sleeve junction: no fin shear. What is there is a broken, dotted dark outline arc where the sleeve shell intersects the torso shell, visible at 8x and 10x on hero and run.
- Sleeve stripe alignment: checked and CLEARED. Columns x=205 (sleeve) and x=270/335 (torso) in the front A-pose share band boundaries at y=369, 389, 410 and 429 exactly; the apparent offset higher up is a blown-out specular highlight on the sleeve cap, not a mis-registered stripe.
- Four runtime-face stills: all genuinely painted and all four distinct (grin closed-smile with teeth line; cheer open with teeth and dark throat; tongue open with pink tongue; angry angled brows over frown). 3.14 PASSES.
measuredFidelity.note: featurelatitude gates brow 32.2, eye 47.7, mouth 73.9, earLine 51.8 - ALL hand-set bounded traces: the analyser refused his pinch outright ('no-pinch', the chunky chin-merges-into-neck class) so the neck row is hand-set at 305 (the collar line), and brow/eye/mouth all refused as merged regions. Deep skin chroma-authored 9C5428 (darkened from A65C2E after the round-2 critic) per the Grizz lesson.

polishFindings: Widen and deepen the torso: the tee is 28.9% of figure height wide against the concept's 34.0% and 24.8% deep in profile against 29.9%. Big Lou is the only heavy kid on the roster and roughly 30% of his cross-section is missing.

Round the tee. In profile at 5x it is a box - flat front face, flat side face, a hard vertical crease between them running the garment's full height, and a flat horizontal hem cut. Rule 3.1's 5/5 forbids butt-joined primitives and this is visible in the silhouette itself.

Halve the stripe count. Pitch 3.6% of figure height vs the concept's 5.2%, ~10 bands over the tee vs ~5, which is 1.4px per band at the 40px field read - the stripes disappear entirely and he becomes a generic beige-shirted kid. This is the single worst defect in the asset.
Harden the stripe boundaries: cream<->gold currently blends over ~4 native px, a painted vertex-colour gradient rather than a constructed edge.
Build the nose as geometry rather than a `nose_push` displacement. It protrudes 3.2% of head height in profile against the concept's 10.3% and is invisible in all four front expression stills.

Shrink the ears by about a third: authored EAR_SPEC radii 0.170 vs head radius 0.520 = 32.7% of head height, measured 31% on the board, against the concept's 24%. They are currently the widest point of the head and they dominate the runtime hero close-up.
Re-cut the hair as a buzz. It is a bowl/mushroom helmet standing off the back of the skull where the concept hugs it, with a hard front edge and a jagged stair-stepped temple notch visible at 5x.
Add strand grain to the hair: 33-52% of the concept's strand count at every band tested, at 175-204% of its prominence - a smooth mass with a few deep gouges instead of a dense fine grain.
Lengthen the shorts to mid-thigh: hem at 73.1% of figure height vs the concept's 76.7% (30% short). Waistband is already correct at 64.7% vs 64.6%.

Raise the shoe upper: navy quarter spans 2.7% of figure height vs the concept's 6.0%, so the chunky sneaker reads as a flat slipper. The toe cap, midsole, outsole and lace mark are all good - only the height is wrong.

Investigate the flat near-black ~21x2px rectangle under the shirt hem at the crotch (front A-pose board). Cropped at 16x it has crisp edges and no gradient, so it is not occlusion falloff - either a see-through gap or an untextured polygon.

Fix the sleeve/torso shell intersection: it emits a broken dotted dark outline arc from collar to armpit in the hero and run stills, and the diameter steps where the sleeve ends and the bare arm begins - no round deltoid form survives (3.11).

Give the elbow and wrist real forms. In swing_contact the elbow is a hard hinge crease with a dark notch, the two forearms interpenetrate with a visible hard intersection line, and the hand is a merged paddle with one thumb nub.
Compress the neck. A visible cylinder plus a collar ring sits where the concept has effectively no neck at all, and that alone costs part of the 'big' read.

Reframe the runtime hero shot or reduce the head yaw: at the current hero camera the head is turned far enough that the ear, not the face, is the dominant feature, so the hero still is not usable face evidence.
Tame the shoulder-cap specular: it blows out roughly 50 of the torso's 195 rows on both sides in the front A-pose board, erasing the stripe pattern exactly where the eye lands first.
Subdivide the belly: plainly faceted low-poly quads with visible shading discontinuities read across the torso at 3x in the runtime hero.

NOT DEFECTS, recorded so they are not re-filed: legs are two legs (35.0% max inter-leg daylight vs the concept's 33.0-36%) and leg thickness matches (10.2% vs 10.3% of figH); ears are constructed with rim, concha and lobe (`build_ear`/`EAR_SPEC` present); nothing is severed anywhere; all four face stills are painted and distinct; the sleeve stripes are correctly registered to the torso's (boundaries coincide at y=369/389/410/429); and the board's washed-out gold is board lighting, not a palette slip - the runtime stills show full mustard.

frontProfileSilhouette.label: front/profile silhouette
frontProfileSilhouette.note: The large read is genuinely faithful and I credit it: the tee/shorts/leg split lands within half a point of the sheet (my own colour-band scan of both figures puts the tee at 29.1-72.0%H delivered against 29.9-72.4%H concept, and the shorts hem at 83.4%H against 82.9%H). What I measured that I have not seen recorded is that the delivered TORSO IS A SURFACE OF REVOLUTION. Fitting each profile contour against its own collar-to-hem chord over 34-71%H, the concept bulges 16.1px forward and only 3.5px back (a 4.6:1 belly-forward asymmetry, 2.35%H vs 0.51%H); the delivered bulges 10.7px forward and 10.7px back - identical to the tenth of a pixel, in every sub-band I tried (34-50%H: 5.3/5.3; 60-71%H: 3.0/4.0). A lathe cannot draw a belly, and the belly is the one silhouette idea this character has. Second, on 3.12, which I was asked to judge myself on the fresh board: the peak separation is fine and the extent is not. Delivered (alpha mask, leg zone >=65%H): 77 of 196 rows show daylight = 39.3%, max inter-leg gap 40px = 37.0% of the body width at that row (89.5%H). Concept, keyed off its own backdrop so the ground shadow cannot seal the channel: 105 of 137 sampled rows = 76.6%, max 38.8% of body width at 89.25%H. So the maxima agree (37.0 vs 38.8) and the COVERAGE is half. Per-row: the concept opens at 83%H - the instant the shorts end - and holds 21-39% of body width continuously to 93%H; the delivered holds 0-2px from 83.4%H to 86.6%H, first opens 12px at 87.3%H, and peaks only at 89.5%H. The earlier 'one connected run y=556-574 with zero daylight' therefore DOES still reproduce on the board that is on disk now (I measure max 2px across that exact band); what is wrong in the earlier note is the implication that the legs never part - they part, just four points of figure height too low, over the ankles instead of over the shins. Third, the sock-to-shoe junction is butt-joined primitives: at 10x on the front board and 12x on the profile the sock is an inverted cone whose rim overhangs the shoe on both sides with clean backdrop visible underneath. It is a concave notch reachable from outside, not an enclosed hole, so I do NOT call 3.7 - but it is the exact 'butt-joined primitives' the 5/5 clause names, at the most visible joint on the figure.

headBodyProportions.label: head/body proportions
headBodyProportions.note: Every number passes and I re-ran them rather than quoting them: head height 26.2% of figure vs concept 27.6% (delta -1.35, tol 2.0), head width:height 1.10 vs 1.12, shorts hem 83.4%H vs 82.9%H, and on the profile board the head measures 152px against a 562px figure (27.0%H) with the neck pinch at 238px. 3.13 passes on measurement. The second clause - joints read as connected forms - is what does not. (a) The NECK. On the profile board the head/neck junction is a straight cylinder with a fine dark ring running right across it, visible at 8x in a crop of x215-325,y215-285; the concept profile figure has no visible neck at all, the jaw and cheek mass running straight into the collar. (b) The SHOULDER. At 4x on the run still (x440-660,y380-560) there is no deltoid: the sleeve is a purple lozenge applied to the FRONT of the torso barrel and the forearm exits it lying flat on the shirt surface, sharing an outline with it. (c) The SHIN. Colour-scanning one leg column down each figure, the concept holds bare skin from 82.9%H to 87.9%H (5.0%H of shin); the delivered holds it from 83.4%H to 86.3%H (2.9%H) - the shin is 42% short, and in every runtime clip it is 0%. (d) The EAR is out of proportion to its own head: measured off 8x and 4x crops, delivered ear 56px on a 152px head = 36.8% of head height, concept 52.5px on a 190px head = 27.6%. That is 1.33x, and it is why the ear dominates the swing still.

hairMass.label: hair mass
hairMass.note: ABSTAINED - null, and the rubric supports it rather than my discretion. 3.3 scores 'one designed mass, hairline reads from the front as well as the side, no bare-skull read from any gameplay angle'. Tank is bald on all five views of the locked turnaround; a bare-skull read is the correct read, so there is no hair mass to score and no way to score it without inventing a target the concept does not set. I checked the sculpt script rather than assuming: HAIR = rgba('3A2416') is declared at line 91 but the surrounding comment says the brows are the one place a hair colour appears on him. measure:strands still emits numbers for the 5-45%-of-head band (delivered 0.40 minima/row at prominence 110.4 vs concept 1.78 at 21.0) and those numbers are VOID here - that band is bare cranium on both images, so the instrument is scanning shading noise, and its output must not be read as a defect.

clothingConstruction.label: clothing construction
clothingConstruction.note: Three of the four garments are unconstructed primitives and the fourth is only half there. SHORTS: a smooth near-black truncated cone. No hem, no turned cuff, no leg openings, no waistband, no side seam, no drape fold - at 4x (front board x165-365,y480-655) the two legs share one continuous surface with a single crotch notch cut into it. The concept's shorts, at 3x (turnaround x105-335,y590-870), draw a clearly turned-up hem cuff on each leg with a stitch line. This is the category's named prohibition, verbatim. SOCKS: worse than a primitive - a grey inverted CONE whose flat rim overhangs the shoe by roughly a third of the shoe's own width on both sides, with backdrop visible beneath it (verified by cropping the region I cite at 10x and 12x). The concept's is a slouched ribbed crew sock sitting ON the shoe collar. This also costs 3.8: the sock does not sit on the body, it hovers over the shoe. TEE: a collar ridge and a thin rolled sleeve cuff, and nothing else - no bottom hem band (the shirt bottom is a rounded blob edge in the profile board), no side seam, no shoulder yoke. SHOES: the measured tone split does pass and I will not manufacture a defect there - dominant tone 84.6% vs 82.1%, second tone 15.4% vs 16.3%, mean saturation 24.8 vs 21.5, all inside tolerance. But that metric reads only the bottom 9% band, and above it the two-tone read is gone: the concept's shoe is a big navy toe box and heel counter against cream, the delivered is almost entirely cream with one thin navy stripe and a stepped, stair-cased notch standing in for the laces and velcro strap, which are absent. And the proportion is off - concept shoes span 40.0% of figure height across the pair at 96-98%H, delivered 26.4%. Note for the record: I suspected a shorts COLOUR miss (delivered reads black against a navy concept) and dropped it - the sculpt declares PANTS #24242B and the delivered mean is within a couple of levels of the concept's, so it is value, not hue.

faceExpressionRead.label: face/expression read
faceExpressionRead.note: FIRST, THE DEFERRED FINDING, WHICH I WAS ASKED TO SETTLE: it does NOT reproduce. On the fresh runtime hero still (neutral/sleepy cell), cropped at 5x over x480-620,y190-320, the near eye shows clearly separated sclera and iris - white on both sides of a dark iris, not 'a solid dark slot' - and the mouth is present as a dark curved line with a lit lower-lip roll under it, reading as a slight frown. Both halves of the claim (closed eyes, no mouth) fail to reproduce at hero scale. The face-spec header's brighter sclera evidently did its job. 3.14 also passes cleanly and I checked all four cells at 3x: grin is a closed smile with a lower-lip lozenge, cheer opens to white teeth over a dark interior, tongue shows a real pink tongue tip, angry angles the brows down-inward over a frown. Four unambiguous emotions at draft-card distance. WHAT DOES FAIL: (a) there is NO NOSE from the front - not a weak one, none; the front board and all four face stills go brow, eyes, mouth with bare skin between, and the profile gives a sharp triangular wedge rather than the concept's soft button with a nostril crease and philtrum. This is the direct cause of the single OFF metric I ran myself: visible face right of centre 49.4% of head width against the concept's 40.8%, delta +8.62 on a tolerance of 6 - that sample row is 62% down the head box and it is almost all bare skin because no lid mass and no nostril shadow are eating into it. (b) The profile has no lips and no chin: from the nose spike to the collar the contour is one featureless arc, where the concept draws an upper lip, a lower lip and a soft chin. (c) THE IDENTITY IS INVERTED. The sheet's signature is heavy-lidded deadpan - upper lid over the top third of the iris under thick low LEVEL brows. The delivered has wide-open almond eyes with a fully exposed iris under thin, high, arched brows. He reads awake and faintly smug; the roster word is 'sleepy'. (d) NEW, and I have not seen it recorded: at 14x over x590-630,y240-290 of the hero still, a dark drip runs from the far eye's lower lid down the cheek for about the eye's own height, with two detached dark specks below it. That is face-atlas texel stretch where the island wraps toward the grazing silhouette, and it reads as a smudge on the cheek at hero scale. I score 3 rather than 2 because legibility - the thing this category leads with - genuinely holds, and all four emotion cells land.

heroAndFieldScale.label: hero + 40px read
heroAndFieldScale.note: The 40px board read survives and I made my own rather than trusting the strip: downsampling the A-pose front board to 40px tall still gives a stocky bald kid in purple over black on pale shoes. Both 'stocky' and 'bald' are legible. The RUNTIME 40px does not - downsampling the hero still's figure to 40px tall gives a purple bowling pin with a brown blob on top: no face, no legs, no shoes to speak of. And every runtime still fails at hero. HERO: the near leg is solid pants-black from the shorts hem straight to the sock ring - I sampled it rather than eyeballing it, and the pixels read 1,3,13 / 1,3,11 / 1,3,10 down the leg against 131,79,15 for shadowed arm skin in the same frame, so it is the PANTS material covering the shin, not shading; the ear is an oversized outlined ring at 36.8% of head height; the nose does not read at all; and the skull shows hard low-poly facets across the crown and cheek. RUN: same black-to-the-sock leg on both legs (sampled: 1,3,12 at x600,y530), only one arm visible, and the hand is four straight parallel finger sticks of near-equal length with hard grooves between them and no thumb, no taper and no knuckles - a rake, confirmed at 4x. SWING_CONTACT, frame 10/18, the marquee instant and the game's single most-seen pose: the head has rotated so far the face is gone entirely, leaving a featureless egg with the ear presenting as a huge outlined oval; the legs are one dark mass with one shoe. I checked the 'open interior' claim on that ear by cropping it at 10x and it is NOT a hole - the ring encloses skin-coloured surface with a shallow crescent shadow, no backdrop pixels inside - so I do not call 3.7 on it, but as the deformation evidence for 4.2 the still is unusable. Two of the three runtime stills fail to show the character at all.

measuredFidelity.result: ALL NUMBERS BELOW ARE MINE, TAKEN THIS SESSION FROM THE FILES ON DISK. (1) npm run measure:fidelity -- tank, run by me: concept front view 316x686px, delivered 488x561px, shoe tones read off the concept as #e3d4c3 and #444c53. head height as % of figure height 27.6 / 26.2 / -1.35 ok (tol 2.0); head width:height 1.12 / 1.10 / -0.01 ok (tol 0.08); shoe band dominant tone 82.1 / 84.6 / +2.51 ok (tol 8); shoe band second tone 16.3 / 15.4 / -0.88 ok (tol 8); shoe band mean saturation 21.5 / 24.8 / +3.26 ok (tol 4); daylight between the ankles 0.00 / 0.00 / +0.00 ok (tol 12); visible face left of centre 48.3 / 50.0 / +1.66 ok (tol 6); visible face right of centre 40.8 / 49.4 / +8.62 OFF (tol 6); face left/right asymmetry 0.00 / 0.62 ok. Verdict: '1 metric outside tolerance.' NOTE ON THAT OFF METRIC - it is a real sculpt finding, not an instrument artifact: with no nose form and no lid mass, the brow-line row is almost all bare skin on the right of centre. Also note the ankleDaylightPct pair (0.00 vs 0.00, ok) is BLIND here: it samples one row at 13% up from the feet where both figures' shoes touch, and on the concept it is additionally sealed by the ground shadow, so it cannot see the thigh fusion at all. (2) MY OWN FIGURE EXTRACTION, using the repo's own scripts/v2/figure-mask.mjs floodFigureMask with the same 0.06 column-occupancy split measure-fidelity uses: turnaround figure runs at x=[59,373],[392,677],[727,932],[981,1296],[1356,1640]; concept front figure 315x685 (y137-822), concept profile figure y142-825 H=684 with the neck pinch at y=332 giving head height 190px = 27.8%H; delivered front/profile board bbox y86-647, H=562, T-pose width 488, A-pose width 366. (3) 3.12 LEG DAYLIGHT, measured by me on the board that is on disk now. Delivered (alpha), leg zone >=65%H: 77 of 196 rows show any daylight = 39.3%; max inter-leg gap 40px at y=588 = 89.5%H = 37.0% of the 108px body width there = 7.13% of figure height. Per-row: 83.8%H gap 0, 85.2%H gap 2, 86.6%H gap 0, 87.3%H gap 12 (8%), 88.1%H gap 26 (20%), 88.8%H gap 34 (30%), 89.5%H gap 40 (37%), 90.9%H gap 26 (19%), 93.0%H gap 20 (14%), 96.6%H gap 20 (14%), 99.5%H gap 14 (9%). (4) WARNING ABOUT THE FLOOD MASK ON THIS SHEET, which I hit myself: run over the concept, floodFigureMask reports the inter-leg channel as FIGURE, because Tank's ground shadow seals it at the bottom so the backdrop flood never reaches it. Measured that way the concept looks like it has LESS thigh daylight than the delivery (23.8% of rows vs 39.3%), which is the opposite of the truth. Any concept leg-daylight number must come from a colour key, not from the flood mask. (5) TORSO PROFILE, new: fitting each contour against its own collar-to-hem chord. Over 34-71%H the concept bulges 16.1px forward (2.35%H) and 3.5px back (0.51%H) - 4.6:1 belly-forward. The delivered bulges 10.7px forward and 10.7px back (1.90%H each) - exactly equal. Sub-bands agree: 34-50%H concept 5.5/1.9, delivered 5.3/5.3; 60-71%H concept 1.5/1.5, delivered 3.0/4.0. The torso is a surface of revolution.
