At 40px that is two or three pixels; Tank effectively carries no team colour on the field. (11) 40PX READS, generated by me: A-pose board downsampled to 40px tall still reads stocky/bald/purple; the hero still's figure downsampled to 40px tall reads as a purple bowling pin with no face and no legs. (12) BINARY BOARD ITEMS AS I READ THEM ON THE FRESH EVIDENCE: 3.7 PASS - I cropped every region I would have cited at 4-14x and found no enclosed backdrop inside any silhouette; the sock overhang and the swing-still ear are a concave notch and a shaded dish respectively, not holes, and I decline the earlier 'hollow oval crater' call. 3.8 FAIL - the sock rim overhangs the shoe with backdrop visible beneath it on both legs. 3.9 WEAK PASS on the board, FAIL at runtime. 3.10 PARTIAL - rim, concha and tragus present, lobe absent, and 1.33x oversized. 3.11 FAIL - no deltoid, the sleeve is a pad applied to the front of the torso barrel, the forearm lies coplanar with the shirt, and the hand is a four-stick rake. 3.12 FAIL ON EXTENT, pass on peak, per (3). 3.13 PASS on measurement (1.10 vs 1.12). 3.14 PASS, all four cells. (13) NOT CLAIMED, checked and dropped: the shorts read black against a navy concept, but the sculpt declares PANTS #24242B and the delivered mean sits within a couple of levels of the concept's, so it is value under the board's tonemapping, not a hue defect. Likewise the shirt's lower saturation on the board tracks the skin's, so it is the render, not the vertex colours - check tonemapping.lint.test.js before anyone touches a swatch. (14) The A-pose renders at 50 degrees of abduction rather than the roster's 72; I did not score it, and I confirm it is doing its job - the sleeve clears the tee in both A-pose views.
measuredFidelity.note: Evidence and board re-captured fresh for the round-31 critic; hairMass abstains (bald).

polishFindings: THE WORST ONE: the torso is a surface of revolution, so Tank has no belly. Measured against each contour's own collar-to-hem chord over 34-71%H, the concept is 16.1px forward and 3.5px back; the delivered is 10.7px forward and 10.7px back - identical, in every sub-band. The character whose entire premise is that he is wide carries none of it in profile. Push the tee's forward radius and pull the back in; the depth envelope is already right, only its distribution about the spine is wrong.

Split the shins, not the ankles. The delivered legs are fused from the shorts hem (83.4%H) to 86.6%H with a maximum 2px of daylight, and only open at 87.3%H. The concept opens at 83%H the instant the shorts end and holds 21-39% of body width all the way to 93%H. The peak gap is already correct (37.0% vs 38.8%); it is the top four points of figure height that are welded. Move the hip pivots apart and narrow the thigh volumes - do not widen the stance, and do not touch a tolerance.

Rebuild the sock as a garment. It is currently an inverted cone whose rim overhangs the shoe on both sides with backdrop visible underneath (crop x190-280,y555-615 of the front board at 10x, and x232-328,y566-610 of the profile at 12x). Make it a slouched ribbed cylinder that sits ON the shoe collar, and give the shoe a heel counter for it to sit on. This one part costs 3.4 and 3.8 together and it is at the most-looked-at joint on the figure.

Give the shin back its length. Concept bare skin runs 82.9-87.9%H (5.0%H); delivered runs 83.4-86.3%H (2.9%H) - 42% short - and the shoe has taken the difference, at 10.0%H against the concept's 6.4%H. A shorter shoe and a longer shin fixes the proportion and the daylight at once.

Reweight the shorts so they stop becoming leggings. In both the run and the hero idle stills the PANTS material covers the whole leg to the sock ring - I sampled it (1,3,11 down the leg against 131,79,15 for shadowed arm skin in the same frame), so it is the material, not shading. The bind pose has 2.9%H of bare leg; motion has zero, and at gameplay distance he reads as a purple blob on a black triangle.

Build the nose as a form and it fixes the only OFF metric with it. There is no nose at all from the front - the four face stills and the front board go brow, eyes, mouth over bare skin - and the profile gives a sharp triangular wedge where the concept has a soft button with a nostril crease and a philtrum. visible-face-right-of-centre is 49.4% against 40.8% (tol 6) precisely because that row has no lid mass and no nostril shadow eating into it.

Add the lip and chin shelf. From the nose spike to the collar the delivered profile is one featureless arc; the concept draws an upper lip, a lower lip and a chin. This is the other half of why the profile head reads as an egg.

Restore the deadpan - this is the identity, not a polish. The sheet's signature is heavy upper lids over the top third of the iris under thick low LEVEL brows. The delivered has wide-open almond eyes with a fully exposed iris under thin high arched brows: awake and faintly smug, where the roster word is sleepy and the production packet says sleepy must not become dim. Note that the previously deferred claim about this face - that it reads as closed eyes and no mouth - does NOT reproduce on the fresh hero still: at 5x the sclera and iris are clearly separated and the mouth line with its lit lower lip is present. The face is legible; it is the wrong face.

Fix the face-atlas stretch at the head's grazing edge. At 14x over x590-630,y240-290 of the hero still a dark drip runs from the far eye's lower lid down the cheek, with two detached dark specks below it. The island is stretching where it wraps toward the silhouette. Not previously recorded.

Give the shoulder a deltoid. At 4x on the run still the sleeve is a purple lozenge applied to the FRONT of the torso barrel and the forearm exits it lying coplanar with the shirt, sharing its outline. There is no upper arm and no shoulder ball at any clip angle (3.11).

Reshape the hand. Four straight parallel finger sticks of near-equal length, hard grooves between them, no thumb visible, no taper, no knuckles - a rake. The concept draws a chubby mitt with sausage fingers.

Bring the ear back to scale and give it a lobe. Measured: 56px on a 152px head = 36.8% of head height, against the concept's 52.5px on a 190px head = 27.6% - 1.33x oversized, which is why it dominates the swing still. The rim, concha and tragus ARE built (sculptlib.ear is imported and I confirmed all three at 8x), but the rim closes into a continuous oval with no lobe, and 3.10 names the lobe.

Construct the shorts. A smooth truncated cone with no hem, no turned cuff, no leg openings, no waistband and no side seam, against a concept that draws a turned-up hem cuff with a stitch line on each leg. Same for the tee's missing bottom hem band, side seam and shoulder yoke.

Rebuild the shoe above the measured band. The tone split passes (84.6/15.4 vs 82.1/16.3) because it only reads the bottom 9%; above that the concept's navy toe box and heel counter are gone, replaced by cream with one thin stripe and a stair-cased notch standing in for laces and velcro. The pair also measures 26.4%H wide at 97%H against the concept's 41.5%H.

Shorten the neck and hide its seam. The delivered profile shows a straight cylinder with a fine dark ring across it where it meets the skull (8x, x215-325,y215-285); the concept profile figure has no visible neck at all.

Widen the team-accent surface. TEAM_MASK sits on exactly two vertex rows of the sock roll-top and measures 1.20% of the front silhouette (1078 of 89569 figure pixels) - two or three pixels at 40px. Tank carries no team colour on the field, which is a 2.4/6.6 problem even though it is not one of the six scores.

Reshoot the swing_contact deformation still. Frame 10/18 has the head rotated so far that the face is gone entirely and the legs are one dark mass, which makes it useless as 4.2 evidence whatever the model is doing. (I did crop that ear at 10x before repeating the earlier open-interior call, and I withdraw it: the ring encloses skin, not backdrop.)

Investigate the board saturation at the instrument, do not repaint. The shirt and the skin both drop by a similar factor between concept and board, so this is tonemapping, not vertex colour. Check tonemapping.lint.test.js before touching any swatch.

frontProfileSilhouette.label: front/profile silhouette
frontProfileSilhouette.note: The front large read is broadly right and the halo's SCALE is measurably dead-on: I measured hair-mass width / figure height at 0.392 delivered vs 0.392 on the concept front figure. Everything else about the outline is not. Delivered front hair carries 4 outward silhouette lobes over 178 rows (2.2 per 100 rows) against the concept's 15 over 206 rows (7.3 per 100) — 31% of the concept's rate — so the halo resolves as a rounded polygon with visible flat chords rather than a curl mass. Hair W:H is 1.062 delivered vs 1.202 concept, so she is under-wide and over-tall (hairH/figH 0.369 vs 0.327): a mushroom, not a halo. The profile is the weaker half. The head is a boxy faceted slab; front-contour relief across the face band is 43 px over 94 rows (46% of head-band height) vs the concept's 121 px over 179 rows (68%), so the whole front of the head reads flat-fronted where the concept's face projects clear of the hair. Two butt-joined primitives sit on the profile outline: the hood is a lumpy kidney lobe stuck behind the neck, and the kangaroo pocket steps 9 px forward in ONE row with square top and bottom. Rubric 3.1's 5 asks for organic transitions between forms; these are the opposite. Silhouette-only, with colour removed, she reads as a bob-cut helmet rather than a curly halo — that is the identity miss. 3.7 (no holes) I could not fault: I cropped the hood/neck junction and the pocket at 4x and found no see-through.

headBodyProportions.label: head/body proportions
headBodyProportions.note: The measured proportion work is the healthiest part of this asset and I am not going to invent a problem here. `measure:fidelity` reports head height 33.2% of figure vs the concept's 34.6% (delta -1.41, ok) and head width:height 1.18 vs 1.16 (delta +0.02, ok), so 3.13 passes and she is not a bobblehead and not a proxy. She reads as a child, not a shrunk adult. What holds her off 4 is the second half of the category — 'joints read as connected forms'. At 4x on the runtime torso the sleeve meets the torso along a hard crease line running neck-to-armpit with no deltoid mass over it, so the upper arm reads as a tube butt-joined into a bag; the same crop shows a pinch/collapse just under her left deltoid. The neck is a plain untapered cylinder between two flat planes, and the hands are undifferentiated mitts. Legs are two legs with clear daylight in bind, idle, run and the batting stance — 3.12 passes and I re-observed it rather than taking it on faith. Note the one metric outside tolerance is the ANKLE gap in the OTHER direction: 26.4 delivered vs 0.00 concept (tol 12), because the concept front figure stands with its feet touching and the delivered board is a bind pose. Per 6b.4 that is a 'look at the stance' note, not a licence to widen the tolerance.

hairMass.label: hair mass
hairMass.note: This is the blocker and it is not 'add strands' — it is that the articulation she has is the WRONG KIND, in three specific ways. (1) Frequency and depth are inverted. `measure:strands` (default band, 5-45% of head height — I state the band because that window does reach onto the forehead and brow, where skin/hair and brow edges can count as FALSE creases, which if anything INFLATES the delivered figure and makes the result below generous) reports 2.89 strand minima/row delivered vs the concept's 12.67 — 23% of the count — at 48.3 mean prominence vs 31.3, i.e. 154% of the concept's depth. She has roughly a quarter as many creases, each half again too deep. That is a faceted mass, not a curled one. (2) The creases run the wrong way. At 4x on `mimi-mash-runtime-hero.png` the clump modulation resolves into about three long vertical grooves running crown-to-hem down the full height of the mass — precisely the 'fluted column rather than clumped curls' failure the sculpt script's own comment at line 279 says the row-varying amplitude was added to prevent. On the current evidence it did not prevent it. The 16 -> 48 column change bought sampling headroom the shape is not using. (3) The SHAPE is a different haircut. The mass terminates in a blunt cut at jaw level with square corners (visible at 4x in the front board crop), and its inner edge overhangs the brow: at 12x on the tongue still the hair's front edge is a coarse polygonal staircase that cuts into the temple and clips the outer end of the eyebrow. The concept is a halo that starts BEHIND a fully exposed forehead and blooms outward; this is a helmet the face is set into. Consequences: ear geometry exists (EAR_SPEC line 138, `build_ear` line 669 — I grepped before saying anything about ears) but is 100% occluded in BOTH board views, where the concept's side view shows the whole ear clear of the hair, so 3.10 cannot be read off this board at all. And exposed skin over the head band in profile is 56.6% of head height vs the concept's 65.0%. Colour compounds it: lit hair on the board measures ~(120,74,52) against the concept's lit ~(50,28,14) — about twice as light — so a smooth mass also reads as light-brown plastic. The runtime toon ramp darkens it back toward the concept, which is why the hero still flatters her and the board does not.

clothingConstruction.label: clothing construction
clothingConstruction.note: Genuinely constructed below the knee, primitive above it. Credit where it is due, measured at 4x: the high-tops are real shoes — cream toe cap, rust upper, three lace grooves, a white midsole with a dark outsole line and dark eyelet marks — and `measure:fidelity` backs the split (dominant tone 63.3% vs the concept's 70.4%, second tone 11.9% vs 17.7%, mean saturation 29.5 vs 26.6, all inside tolerance, so the shoe is not grey and not flat). The jeans have a true rolled pale cuff with an underside lip, and the sleeve has a real scrunch step at the forearm. Above the waist it falls apart. The kangaroo pocket is a flat slab, not a stitched welt: measured on the profile A-pose board, torso depth is 41-44 px through y 320-375, then the front contour jumps 228 -> 220 between two adjacent rows and holds — a 9 px protrusion, 21% of body depth, with square 90-degree top and bottom edges and no seam blending it into the garment. The hood is worse. On the profile board it is a lumpy kidney-shaped lobe butt-joined behind the neck with a hard dark crease at the junction, and at the runtime front camera (4x) it resolves into two near-BLACK navy wedges flanking the neck on top of the red shoulders, reading as backpack straps or shadow holes rather than a red hood drape — the concept's hood is the same rust as the hoodie and lies flat across the back. The cream tee sliver is a hard-edged pale RECTANGLE bar sitting on the chest, not a tee neckline seen inside a collar. And the ribbed hem the script declares (line 342, 'ribbed hem') does not read as a rib on any board or runtime view — the hoodie just stops. TEAM_MASK is the pale grey-blue rolled jean cuff (line 70) and its EXTENT is correct and modest — cuff roll only; I am judging extent, not the raw grey on the board.

faceExpressionRead.label: face/expression read
faceExpressionRead.note: The only category that clears the floor, and I went looking for a reason to fail it. I first suspected a decal island — the runtime stills appeared to show a lighter rectangular face patch with stair-stepped edges. Cropped at 12x, that is NOT a UV seam: it is the boundary between skin and the dark hair overhang, and the skin surface is one continuous tone with no island edge. Cross-checked against Junebug and Grizz at the same camera to confirm the artifact is not a renderer-wide one; theirs are clean too, so there was nothing to file. On the board at 4x the face is genuinely well built: eyes with iris, pupil and highlight, sculpted dark brows, a soft nose with a rounded tip and a bridge break, a smiling mouth with real lip volume. The nose IS a form and does break the profile — I measured the local forward bulge in the face band at 2.58% of head-band height delivered vs 2.23% on the concept side view, so it is comparable, not flat. `measure:fidelity` puts visible face left of centre at 27.0% vs the concept's 23.4% and right at 28.4% vs 27.1%, with 1.35 left/right asymmetry — all in tolerance. 3.14 passes on the four expression stills: grin shows a tooth band, tongue shows an open mouth with a real pink tongue, and both read at draft-card distance, not only in close-up. Held at 4 rather than 5 by two things that are really the hair's fault landing on the face: the halo's angular front edge clips the outer end of the eyebrow at gameplay scale, and at the swing camera the mass hides the face entirely.

heroAndFieldScale.label: hero + 40px read
heroAndFieldScale.note: Identity survives both scales, but with a specific defect at the field scale rather than a general softness. At the runtime hero the read is the strongest evidence on this asset: the toon ramp darkens the halo close to the concept's value, and dark round mass + rust hoodie + blue jeans + rust high-tops is unmistakably her. The 40 px strip on the regenerated board still holds the halo/red/blue split, so 3.9's one memorable read survives. Two things keep it off 4. First, the memorable read is the halo's SHAPE, and the outline is already only 31% of the concept's lobe rate at full board resolution (4 lobes/178 rows vs 15/206) — by 40 px the curl read is gone entirely and she is a generic round dark hair mass, which is exactly the silhouette that has to carry her against every other dark-haired kid on the roster. Second, the near-black hood wedges at the neck (see clothing) survive to gameplay distance as two dark notches punched into the shoulders; at 40 px they read as damage to the silhouette rather than as a garment. 6.6 is fine — she does not vanish against grass or dirt in any of the three runtime stills. 4.1 confirmed green: the hero, run and swing stills all report `model model`, so this is fidelity evidence and not proxy evidence.

measuredFidelity.result: TOOLS RUN MYSELF. `npm run measure:fidelity -- mimi_mash` (concept front 291x722, delivered 451x566; shoe tones read off concept #faecd9 and #9b7c63): head height as % of figure 34.6 concept / 33.2 delivered / -1.41 ok; head width:height 1.16 / 1.18 / +0.02 ok; shoe band dominant tone 70.4 / 63.3 / -7.09 ok; shoe band second tone 17.7 / 11.9 / -5.72 ok; shoe band mean saturation 26.6 / 29.5 / +2.91 ok; DAYLIGHT BETWEEN ANKLES 0.00 / 26.4 / +26.4 OFF (tol 12) — delivered has MORE ankle gap than the concept, whose front figure stands feet touching; bind pose vs posed drawing, read as stance per 6b.4, do not widen; visible face left of centre 23.4 / 27.0 / +3.66 ok; visible face right of centre 27.1 / 28.4 / +1.23 ok; face L/R asymmetry 0.00 / 1.35 ok. 1 of 9 outside tolerance. `npm run measure:strands -- mimi_mash`, BAND = the default 5-45% of head height (caveat noted: that window reaches onto forehead and brows where skin/hair and brow edges count as FALSE creases, which inflates the DELIVERED figure, so the ratio below is generous to the asset): concept head rows 92-343, 12.67 strand minima/row, mean prominence 31.3 over 101 rows; delivered head rows 80-267, 2.89 minima/row, mean prominence 48.3 over 76 rows => 23% of the concept's strand count at 154% of its prominence. MY OWN MEASUREMENTS (sharp, flood-filled hair component on the regenerated boards): delivered front hair bbox 222x209 px, W:H 1.062, 24,493 px, bbox fill 0.528; concept front figure (turnaround crop x40 w320) hair bbox 291x242, W:H 1.202, 32,861 px, fill 0.467. Figure heights 567 delivered / 740 concept => hair width / figure height 0.392 vs 0.392 (SCALE IS CORRECT), hair height / figure height 0.369 vs 0.327 (13% over-tall). Silhouette lobe count (outward local maxima on both edges of the hair outline, 3-tap smoothed, top 85% of the mass): delivered 4 over 178 rows = 2.2 per 100 rows; concept 15 over 206 rows = 7.3 per 100 rows => 31% of the concept's outline articulation. Profile: exposed-skin rows over the head band 56.6% of head height delivered vs 65.0% concept. Profile front-contour relief over the FACE band 43 px / 94 rows = 46% of head-band height delivered vs 121 px / 179 rows = 68% concept; but the local nose bulge inside that band is 2.58% delivered vs 2.23% concept, so the nose is NOT the deficit — the whole head front is. Profile A-pose torso depth 41-44 px through y 320-375, then front contour steps 228->220 between two adjacent rows and holds through y 425 => kangaroo pocket protrudes 9 px = 21% of torso depth with square top/bottom edges. Hair colour, lit surface, sampled on the boards: delivered ~(108-142, 65-92, 47-70), concept ~(40-59, 23-33, 10-17) — delivered reads roughly 2x lighter (authored swatch HAIR = 5A2E12, script line 57, deliberately lightened 'to group strands under the ramp'). Hair bottom-edge local roughness: 1.02% of hair width delivered vs 0.95% concept — this metric did NOT separate them (the concept's lower hair boundary is occluded by the shoulders), so I am reporting it as inconclusive rather than as evidence for the blunt-cut read, which is an eye call off the 4x front crop. TRAPS OBSERVED: grepped the sculpt script before saying anything about ears (EarSpec line 33/138, build_ear line 669 — ears EXIST, they are occluded, not absent); cropped every hole/artifact claim at 4x or 12x before filing, which killed a false 'decal-island seam' finding (it is the hair edge, confirmed against Junebug and Grizz at the same camera); judged TEAM_MASK by extent only (pale grey-blue rolled jean cuff, line 70 — extent correct); did not file the foreshortened near-side eye in the 90-degree profile; leg fusion NOT re-filed, and I re-observed daylight in bind, idle, run and bat_stance myself. 4.1 green: hero/run/swing stills all report `model model`, tris 29.0k, draws 14.
measuredFidelity.note: featurelatitude gates brow 37.0, eye 50.0, mouth 65.3 (bounded crop traces - the analyser refused all three; its two competing mouth bands at 75.7/93.2 are the under-chin and collar shadows), earLine 49.4. The pre-convention proxy blend carried stray meshes (*_CurlHalo, Icosphere) that exported alongside the LODs and blew the 400KB budget until purged.

polishFindings: HAIR, THE KIND OF FAILURE: not 'too few strands' but 'too few, too deep, and running the wrong way'. 2.89 minima/row at 154% prominence vs the concept's 12.67 at 100% means the 48-column ring is spending its budget on a handful of deep facets instead of a dense field of shallow ones. At 4x on the runtime hero the modulation resolves as ~3 long vertical grooves running crown-to-hem — the 'fluted column' failure the script's own comment at line 279 claims the row-varying amplitude fixed. The repair is to break the flutes into ROW-OFFSET clump cells (stagger the lobe phase per row so no groove survives more than ~15% of the halo's height) and to cut a6/a10 amplitude so prominence drops from 48 toward 31 while the count rises — trading depth for frequency at constant tri budget.

HAIR, THE SHAPE IS A DIFFERENT HAIRCUT: the mass terminates in a blunt cut at jaw level with square corners and its inner edge overhangs the brow, so silhouette-only she reads as a bob helmet. The concept's halo starts behind a fully exposed forehead and blooms outward and backward. Raise the hairline off the brow, ragged the lower boundary into clump lobes instead of a straight chord, and push the mass rearward: profile exposed-skin is 56.6% of head height vs the concept's 65.0%, and hair W:H is 1.062 vs the concept's 1.202.

HAIR EDGE CLIPS THE BROW: at 12x on mimi-mash-runtime-face-tongue.png the halo's front edge is a coarse polygonal staircase cutting into the temple and truncating the outer end of the eyebrow. Whatever else changes, the face-framing edge needs enough segments (or enough clearance) that it never lands on a facial feature.

EARS EXIST BUT ARE 100% OCCLUDED in both board views (EAR_SPEC line 138, build_ear line 669). The concept's side view shows the whole ear clear of the hair. As delivered, board item 3.10 cannot be read off this board at all — the ear is not verifiable, which is a different problem from it being wrong.

HOOD IS A BUTT-JOINED LOBE: on the profile board it is a lumpy kidney shape stuck behind the neck with a hard dark crease at the junction; at the runtime front camera it resolves into two near-BLACK wedges flanking the neck on top of the red shoulders, reading as backpack straps or shadow holes. The concept's hood is the same rust as the hoodie and lies flat across the back. Fix the value first (it should not be near-black), then the attachment.

KANGAROO POCKET IS A SLAB, NOT A WELT: measured 9 px of forward protrusion = 21% of the 43 px torso depth, arriving in a single row with square 90-degree top and bottom edges. The concept's pocket is a soft welt with a stitch seam. Chamfer the top and bottom edges into the garment and cut the protrusion.

CREAM TEE SLIVER READS AS A NAME TAG: a hard-edged pale rectangle bar sitting flat on the chest below the neck, in every runtime front still. It should be a soft V of tee seen INSIDE the hoodie collar, not a decal bar on top of it.

RIBBED HEM DECLARED BUT NOT VISIBLE: the script declares a ribbed hem (line 342) and the concept shows a prominent one. No rib reads at the waist on any board or runtime view — the hoodie just stops. Same for the collar rib.

HAIR VALUE IS ~2x TOO LIGHT ON THE BOARD: lit surface ~(120,74,52) vs the concept's lit ~(50,28,14). Authored HAIR = 5A2E12 was deliberately lightened 'to group strands under the ramp' (line 57), but the board is the palette-fidelity surface (2.2) and there she reads light-brown plastic. The runtime ramp darkens it back, which is why the hero still flatters her — that gap between board and runtime is itself worth resolving so the board stops being the pessimistic view.

SHOULDER HAS NO DELTOID: at 4x on the runtime torso the sleeve meets the torso along a hard neck-to-armpit crease with no round mass over it, and there is a visible pinch/collapse just under her left deltoid. Relevant to 3.11 as well as 3.2.

ANKLE GAP IS THE ONE OFF METRIC and it is off the GENEROUS way (26.4 vs 0.00, tol 12) because the concept front figure stands with feet touching. Per 6b.4 this is a stance note. Do not widen the tolerance and do not close her legs to chase it — the 10-degree default adduction that closed every uncalibrated kid is exactly the repair that must not be reintroduced.

NOT A DEFECT, RECORDED SO THE NEXT REVIEWER DOES NOT RE-FILE IT: the apparent lighter rectangular 'face decal island' with stair-stepped edges in the runtime stills is the skin/hair boundary, not a UV seam. Confirmed at 12x and cross-checked against Junebug and Grizz at the same camera. The face surface is continuous and the nose measurably breaks the profile (2.58% vs the concept's 2.23%).

frontProfileSilhouette.label: front/profile silhouette
frontProfileSilhouette.note: The large read misses on the two shapes that ARE Grizz. (1) The afro: I measured the hair envelope on both sheets with the same dark-pixel row scan. Concept front figure is 340x684px; its hair mass is 279px wide at y258 and spans y128-420, aspect H:W 1.047 - a ball taller than it is wide, whose sides descend 33px BELOW the chin (chin y387). Delivered front-review figure is 560px tall; its hair mass is 228px wide at y176-186 and spans y86-240, aspect 0.675, and its sides stop 43px ABOVE the chin (chin y283). Width is right (40.7% of figure height vs the concept's 40.8%); height is 27.5% of figure against 42.7%. So the mass is 36% too short for its width and does not envelop the skull - a bowl set on top of the head rather than a halo around it. (2) The belly: the concept profile draws a pronounced forward belly bulge with the tee draping over it and a real chest-belly-hip curve; the delivered profile and A-pose are a straight-sided bell/smock with no belly, no waist, no weight. The chubbiest kid on the roster ships as a thin kid in an oversized shirt. (3) Ears absent (see clothing/face notes; grep-confirmed, not eyeballed). (4) The shoulder is a straight bevel with no deltoid roundness - cropped at 12x the sleeve/torso junction is a clean continuous taper (NO fin, NO shear, and I checked before writing this), but it is also a cone butt-joined to a box. What is right: stubby child blocking, garment layout, legs, and the profile nose. Flood fill on all four board views returns 0 enclosed background regions and exactly 1 figure component each - no holes, nothing severed.

headBodyProportions.label: head/body proportions
headBodyProportions.note: Honest and close, and the best of the six. measure:fidelity could not take the head metrics (the head/neck detector found no silhouette pinch) - that is correct for this kid, the concept draws him with no neck at all, and the delivered model reproduces that: the jaw sits straight on the shirt. So I took them by hand. Head height (crown y86 to chin y283) is 197px of a 560px figure = 35.2%, against the concept's 259/684 = 37.9% - 2.7 points short, and all of the shortfall is the flattened afro. Head width:height 228/197 = 1.157 against the concept's 279/259 = 1.077 - 7% wide, same cause. Not a bobblehead, child proportion not proxy proportion, body vertically continuous. Where it loses points is joints reading as connected forms: the upper arm is a plain plugged cylinder with no deltoid and no elbow swell (visible in the hero torso crop at 5x and in the run still), and the torso is a featureless slab, so the figure reads assembled rather than grown. Docking to 3 rather than 4 because the concept's defining mass distribution - heavy, low, round - is simply not in the volumes.

hairMass.label: hair mass
hairMass.note: His identity, and the worst category. measure:strands -- grizz, DEFAULT BAND 5-45% of head height, and on this kid that band is clean of the forehead/brow trap: it samples concept y128-245 where the hair runs to y420, and delivered y86-169 where the hair runs to y240, so both windows sit entirely inside hair and no skin or brow edge can be counted as a false crease. Result: concept 15.55 strand minima/row over 105 rows; delivered 1.61 over 75 rows - the model carries 10% of the concept's strand count at 113% of its prominence. Visually that is exactly what you see: a completely smooth, featureless dome. Rubric 3.3 caps a smooth featureless blob at 4 however correct its silhouette - and here the silhouette is ALSO wrong (aspect 0.675 vs 1.047, terminating at the eyebrow line instead of below the jaw, straight faceted polygon segments along the profile edge instead of a scalloped curl edge, and a visible cone-point apex at the crown). So it fails on both halves of the criterion. It is not inside-out - the profile and back reads are correctly oriented, the earlier winding bug is gone - and there is no bare-skull read from any gameplay angle, and the hairline reads from front and side. Colour: delivered mean (54,49,46) against the concept's (49,32,21); the value is right but saturation is 8 against 28, so it ships as neutral grey-black where the drawing is a warm brown-black. 2, not 1, because the mass exists, sits correctly and holds through run and swing.

clothingConstruction.label: clothing construction
clothingConstruction.note: Genuinely mixed, and better than the board's own 3/5 suggests in places. Constructed and correct: the sleeve carries a real cuff band with a fold (cropped at 12x - a proper hem, not a painted ring); the sock roll is a chunky slouched cuff with a rolled top lip, and its extent is right - a band above the shoe, not creeping up the shin, not spilling over the upper (judging extent only, TEAM_MASK grey on the board is expected); the shoe has laces with three bars, a toe cap, a midsole and a side eyelet. I measured the shoe-only colour split excluding the sock: delivered 20.9% navy / 51.1% cream against the concept's 26.8% / 60.0% - the navy:cream ratio is 0.41 vs 0.45, so the split is right and measure:fidelity's shoe band metrics all pass (81.5 vs 81.9, 18.5 vs 16.0, sat 18.5 vs 19.4). What fails: the tee has NO collar or neck rib - the shirt just ends in a raw opening under the jaw with a hard shadowed notch either side (cropped at 9x with contrast boosted; those notches are shadow, not holes - flood fill confirms 0 enclosed regions); the chest pocket is a flat embossed rectangle with no flap, no stitch line and no bottom edge, reading as a printed square rather than a pocket; the tee hem is a straight cut with no fabric thickness; and the shirt hangs so long that the navy shorts are reduced to a narrow band, where the concept shows a clear shorts block from hem to knee. 3.

faceExpressionRead.label: face/expression read
faceExpressionRead.note: The logged largest identity gap is STILL open, and it is the whole read. The concept draws heavy HALF-CLOSED lids - the upper lid covering the top ~45% of the eye, the iris cut off, a shallow lens-shaped aperture - over thick soft brows that taper DOWN and OUT. That is his personality: deadpan, unimpressed, sleepy. The model ships wide-open ovals with full white sclera and a complete round iris, under hard black angular wedges angled down toward the CENTRE. The emotion is inverted: the drawing is bored, the model is furious. And it never changes: I diffed the four runtime face stills row by row over the head crop and the ONLY band that moves is 24 rows at the mouth (y306-330, mean abs diff up to 16); the brow band diffs at <=1.7 and the eye band at <=3.7, i.e. noise. So grin, cheer, tongue and angry all wear the same glare, and a smiling Grizz still scowls. (Junebug's same test shows two separate moving bands, so this is not a universal atlas limit.) The nose is NOT absent - sculpt-grizz-source.py line 182 authors nose_push, and I measured it: in profile it breaks the face edge by 12px on a 559px figure (2.15%) against the concept's 18px on 666px (2.70%), so 80% of target, and the delivered lip protrusion (17px) sits in the same relationship to it as the concept's does. But it carries ZERO front read: at 9x with 2.2x contrast the mid-face is blank - no nostrils, no wings, no bridge value break - where the concept has a big round button with two clear nostril dimples. The board mouth is a thin scratch against the concept's full pout. Credit where due: the four runtime mouths ARE genuinely painted and distinct (closed grin with a teeth strip, open cheer with teeth and dark interior, a pink tongue out, a downturned frown), so 3.14 passes at card distance; the face is visible in the front board view; there is no decal-island seam. But the skull is visibly FACETED at hero - a polygonal patchwork of hard flat planes down the temple and cheek in every runtime still. 2.

heroAndFieldScale.label: hero + 40px read
heroAndFieldScale.note: Fails the half of this that matters most. At the 40px strip the afro collapses into a flat dark BOWL sitting on the crown with its lower edge cutting straight across at brow level - it reads as a bike helmet or a beret, not an afro. That is the direct consequence of the measured 0.675 hair aspect against the concept's 1.047, and it means 3.9's 'one memorable read' does not survive the field sprite. He is not invisible against grass or dirt and the brown tee / navy shorts / cream sock silhouette is clean and legible, so he is findable - just not identifiable as the kid with the giant afro. At hero the afro recovers most of its mass in 3/4 (the round read is there in the swing back view), but the face arriving as a faceted glare undoes it. One more measured deviation at this scale: on the same lighting basis - the shirt matches the concept within (3,4,8), so the board's light is comparable - the skin ships at mean (183,127,93) against the concept's (154,90,50), luma 138 vs 102. His skin is roughly 35% lighter and less saturated than the drawing, which at 40px and at draft-card size reads pale. For a Black character whose skin tone is a core identity trait, that is not a rounding error. 2.

polishFindings: THE AFRO IS A FLAT BOWL, NOT A BALL. Measured hair-mass aspect H:W is 0.675 against the concept front figure's 1.047, and the mass terminates 43px ABOVE the chin where the concept's descends 33px BELOW it. This one number is also what kills the 40px read, where the afro currently silhouettes as a bike helmet.

EARS ARE ABSENT AND THE CONCEPT DRAWS TWO BIG ONES. Grep-confirmed: no EarSpec, no build_ear in sculpt-grizz-source.py; the header at line 232 already records this as unfinished work. The concept front view shows large ears with rim, inner shadow and lobe standing clear of the afro at eye-to-mouth height, and the delivered board has bare cheek there. Binary rubric item 3.10, currently failing.

HALF-CLOSED LIDS ARE STILL MISSING - the largest identity gap, unchanged on this board. Wide-open ovals with full sclera plus hard black brow wedges angled down toward the centre turn the concept's bored deadpan into a permanent angry glare. This is one face-atlas cell edit away and it is worth more than any geometry change on this kid.

THE EYES AND BROWS ARE BYTE-STATIC ACROSS ALL FOUR EXPRESSIONS. Row-diff of the four runtime-face stills moves only a 24-row band at the mouth (y306-330); the brow and eye bands sit at noise. Grin, cheer and tongue all scowl. Junebug's atlas moves two bands, so the pipeline supports it.

THE NOSE HAS NO FRONT READ. It exists and profiles at 80% of the concept's protrusion, but at 9x with 2.2x contrast the delivered mid-face is blank - no nostrils, no wings, no bridge break. The concept's is a big round button with two clear nostril dimples. Needs a value break or nostril geometry, not more protrusion.

NO BELLY. The concept profile draws a pronounced forward belly with the tee draping over it; the delivered torso is a straight-sided smock in every view. Grizz's weight is half his silhouette and none of it is in the volumes.

THE SKULL IS VISIBLY FACETED AT HERO. Every runtime still shows a polygonal patchwork of hard flat planes across the temple and cheek. The board renders are smooth, so this is the runtime toon shading amplifying head normals - check smooth-shading / normal handling on the head mesh rather than resculpting it.

SKIN SHIPS ~35% TOO LIGHT. On the same lighting basis (the shirt matches the concept within (3,4,8)), delivered skin is (183,127,93) against the concept's (154,90,50), luma 138 vs 102. Worth re-deriving the authored skin swatch from the turnaround; palette.lint will keep gating it against whatever is authored, so the lint will not catch this.

THE TEE HAS NO COLLAR. The shirt ends in a raw opening under the jaw with a hard shadowed notch either side (shadow, not a hole - flood fill confirms 0 enclosed regions). A rib band would also soften the yoke saddle that currently dips between the two sleeve caps.

THE CHEST POCKET IS A DECAL. A flat embossed rectangle with no flap, no stitch line and no bottom edge. The sleeve cuff and the sock roll are both properly constructed, so this is the one garment detail out of step with the rest.

THE AFRO CROWN IS A CONE POINT. The profile silhouette shows straight faceted polygon segments and a pointed apex where the concept has a scalloped curl edge over a near-hemisphere. Per measure-strands' own header the fix is trading afro rows for columns at constant triangle cost, not more lobes or deeper creases.

NO DELTOID. The shoulder is a straight bevel from neck to sleeve hem - clean at 12x with no fin and no shear at the sleeve/torso junction, but also a cone butt-joined to a box, and it reads as a stiff hinged cylinder in the run still.

frontProfileSilhouette.label: front/profile silhouette
frontProfileSilhouette.note: The front read is acceptable, but the profile (sprout-profile-review.png / sprout-profile-apose-review.png) is a flat plank: the torso is a featureless lathe pod with no chest, belly or seat, and it terminates in a hard horizontal shelf at ~y560 from which a plain tapered leg tube emerges — the textbook butt-joined primitive the 5/4 language names. The head silhouette is broken by a dead-flat triangular nose fin (crop /tmp/nose-prof.png, ~x155-260 y380-450 of the source) and by a lumpy yellow collar knob floating at the chin (source ~x300-410 y280-330).

headBodyProportions.label: head/body proportions
headBodyProportions.note: There is no neck: measure:fidelity could not take 5 of its 9 metrics because the head/neck detector found no silhouette pinch. Measured by hand on sprout-front-review.png the minimum width between crown and shoulders is 104px against a 217px max head width (48%); on the turnaround the same pinch is 49px against 237px (21%). Head is also squatter than the drawing — delivered w:h ~1.10 (217/197px) vs the instrument's concept 0.97. Head->shoulder, hip->thigh and sleeve->forearm all butt-join rather than reading as connected forms.

hairMass.label: hair mass
hairMass.note: measure:strands: 2.42 minima/row delivered vs 8.72 concept = 28% of the concept's strand count. It is a smooth featureless dome, which the rubric caps at 4 on its own, and it also loses the identity: the turnaround's signature is a forward-swept spiky quiff with a crown peak, the delivered is a rounded mushroom cap (sprout-front-review.png y86-200). It swallows the forehead the sheet keeps clear, clips the character's left eyebrow to a stub (/tmp/f-head.png, brow at crop x420-520), and leaks an orange eyebrow fragment ONTO the hair (source ~x330 y188 front, ~x225 y185 profile).

clothingConstruction.label: clothing construction
clothingConstruction.note: Real construction is present at the extremities: rolled denim cuffs, shoes with a sole, toe cap, three lace stripes and a knot, and a scored bib pocket. The garment BOUNDARIES are painted, not constructed — sculpt-sprout-source.py's overalls_color() is explicit ('one surface, no second shell'), and a scanline across sprout-front-review.png y315-345 shows a 3-4px blended ramp between the tee yellow and the bib denim. In sprout-runtime-swing.png the tee reads as a yellow rectangle stamped on the bib (~x400-455 y440-580). The concept's brass overall buttons at both strap/bib junctions are absent, and sleeve->forearm is a colour change on one tube, not a cuff.

faceExpressionRead.label: face/expression read
faceExpressionRead.note: The mouth work is the strongest part — /tmp/face-cheer.png and /tmp/face-tongue.png show real teeth and a real tongue, and angry reads. But the face is a sticker on a ball: in pure profile the whole frontal eye (sclera + iris) is visible wrapped onto the side plane (/tmp/nose-prof.png, crop x250-360 y200-420), and the nose is a flat triangular wedge whose tip sits at eye centre height with no ball, bridge or nostril. sprout-runtime-face-grin.png is BLANK — no character rendered — so 3.14's four-still evidence set is incomplete.

heroAndFieldScale.label: hero + 40px read
heroAndFieldScale.note: The 40px strip on sprout-fidelity-review.png does carry a dark-cap kid in blue overalls, so identity survives small. The hero and gameplay 3/4 is where it breaks: sprout-runtime-hero.png (~x480-590 y300-370) reads as one oversized eye plus an orange spike, with the near ear a flat flesh paddle and no neck under it.

polishFindings: 3.10 HARD FAIL, CONFIRMED: the sculpt builds no ears at all, justified at sculpt-bubbles-source.py:18 and :156 as 'ears are never drawn (the curl curtains cover them in all five views): no EarSpec, like Grizz'. The turnaround's profile view (x 638-846) draws a large, fully constructed ear — helix rim, antihelix, concha shadow, tragus and a clear lobe — at roughly x 735-760, y 295-340, with the ringlets tucked BEHIND it, and it occupies about a third of the visible cheek. Bubbles is not Grizz; the Grizz precedent was copied without re-reading her sheet.

The stand-in for the missing ear is worse than nothing: a rectangular gouge with hard corners is cut into the hair shell at ear height (bubbles-profile-review.png x 280-297, y 220-268; both sides visible in bubbles-front-review.png at x ~170-185 and ~350-365). It renders as a black open hole at gameplay camera (bubbles-runtime-hero.png x 460-490 y 290-340; bubbles-runtime-run.png ~250,285) and reads as damage, not anatomy. This is also a 3.7 concern — a visible open interior in the profile silhouette.

The bow is on the wrong garment landmark. The sheet puts a cream ribbon bow at the RIGHT WAIST, over the skirt seam; the delivered bow is a white chevron blob on the centre chest, and in profile it reads as a cream-rimmed medallion at the collarbone that interpenetrates the hair mass (bubbles-profile-review.png ~262,300). 3.8.

The buttons are rectangles. The sheet draws two round cream buttons offset to her right chest on a diagonal; delivered are two white rectangular slabs stacked on the centre line (bubbles-front-review.png x 262-272, y 370-395), which at 40px read as a zipper pull, not buttons.

The dress has no waist. The sheet's dress is a fitted bodice with a clear seam and a gathered, asymmetrically-hemmed skirt; the delivered garment is one uninterrupted cone from armpit to hem in both front and profile. The 'skirt' and 'bodice' the script's comment at line 357 claims to make readable do not exist as separate forms in the render.

An unexplained dark maroon band appears under the hem and in both armpits (bubbles-front-review.png hem y ~462-470; armpits x ~300-360 and ~540-590, y ~285-305). It is not a colour on the sheet, which is one pink plus cream trim. Worth checking against palette.lint — it may be a baked shadow or an errant swatch on the underside faces.
A stray white square floats at the neckline with nothing to attach to (bubbles-front-review.png ~265,335) — an orphan quad or a mis-sited trim piece.
The pocket flap breaks the silhouette in profile (bubbles-profile-review.png ~205,352) — a detached white nub outside the dress edge. Interpenetration that reads at hero scale, 3.8.

Shoes lose all construction in motion. In bubbles-runtime-run.png the raised shoe (~490,560) is a cylindrical puck with a white rim — no toe cap, no lace, no sole/upper split — against a sheet that draws crossed laces, a distinct sole and a pink sole stripe. The static shoe fares better and the shoe-band tone metrics pass, so this is a form problem, not a colour one.

The hair curtain sits closer to the face than the sheet does and steals the cheeks: the delivered inner hair edge drops level with the chin on both sides, boxing the face into a narrow porthole, where the concept front view leaves the full cheeks and jaw open. Nothing is swallowed outright — eyes, brows, nose and freckles all clear — but the face reads narrower than the drawing's.

The topknot does not read as a curly bun. It is a smooth mushroom cap butt-joined onto a flat crown plateau over a cream torus (bubbles-front-review.png y 75-140); at hero it reads as a cork stopper or a muffin, and in the team-tinted hero still the scrunchie goes olive-yellow and reads as a rubber band. Genuine positives, for the record: the four expression stills clear 3.14 outright (real open mouth, real tongue, real frown); the socks are the one correctly-constructed garment (cream crew with the pink stripe, matching the sheet); leg daylight at thigh and calf is clean in bind and in run (3.12); the 40px read is distinctive; and every shoe-band colour metric is inside tolerance.

The recorded 4/4/4/4/4/4 in character-fidelity.json is not defensible against this evidence. measure:strands alone (10% of concept strand count) forecloses a 4 on hair mass, and 3.10 is a confirmed hard fail, so the asset cannot be candidate-complete at any score.

The delivered head is 12% shallower front-to-back than the drawing - the back hair mass under-carries the concept's volume, so the profile is a different head shape, not a polish gap. (2) THE BUN IS BUTT-JOINED, MEASURED: on the front A-pose the silhouette width jumps 78px -> 121px between rows 147 and 151 - a 43px ledge in four rows where the bun meets the crown. The concept sweeps curls continuously into the knot. (3) The bun is a visibly faceted 7-gon in both front and profile at 3-4x crop, and the shirt hem and shorts read as butt-joined prisms. (4) On the runtime run still the collar-to-shoulder wedge reaches the outline and bites a black notch out of the shoulder contour (cropped at 6x, region x490-640 y290-430 of bendy-bao-runtime-run.png). Crown (bun top) row 87; the silhouette narrows 114 -> 82 -> 72 -> 60px across rows 267-279, which is a clean jaw-into-neck pinch at row 279, giving head-plus-bun = 192/561 = 34.2% of figure height; against the authored 87-297 span it is 210/561 = 37.4%, and the concept's own declared band is 242/646 = 37.5%. Either way this is a chunky child head at roughly a third of the figure, matching the turnaround and not the proxy. Head width:height 78.1% vs concept 81.8%. Limbs are short, the shoes are chunky, the neck seats under the jaw, and the bind pose reads as connected forms. Two things keep it off 5: the T-pose and A-pose arms run slenderer than the concept's chunky forearms, and the shoulder joint stops reading as connected in motion - the run still opens a dark wedge with a bright backface sliver exactly at the collar-to-shoulder junction, so the joint that is fine in bind is not fine in the delivered clip.

hairMass.label: hair mass
hairMass.note: This is the category the ruler settles against the recorded 4. I ran measure:strands myself at three bands and state them all. DEFAULT 5-45%: delivered 1.54 minima/row at prominence 24.9 vs concept 6.48 at 17.4 = 24% of the concept's strand count. That default band reaches down onto the forehead and brows, where the skin/hair boundary and the painted brow edges are counted as FALSE creases, so it flatters the delivered figure. Re-run on the BUN AND CROWN ONLY: 2-28% band gives 0.86 vs 6.09 = 14% of the concept's count at 74% of its prominence; 5-30% band gives 0.88 vs 6.79 = 13% at 80%. Excluding the brows the delivered mass carries roughly one seventh of the drawn strand grouping, and unlike the roster pattern its prominence does not over-compensate (74-80%, i.e. the few creases that exist are also shallower than the drawing's). That is a smooth featureless mass, which the rubric caps at 4 by itself. It goes to 3 because the silhouette is ALSO wrong: profile head depth 70.5% vs the concept's 80.2%, a 43px-in-4-rows hard ledge where the bun butt-joins the crown, and a bun that crops as a faceted heptagon rather than a knot. Worse, in the delivered run and swing stills the mass reads as a round afro mop with a bump on top, not the tidy swept knot the sheet draws - the gameplay read of his signature hair is a different hairstyle. THE OLD BACKFACE-VOID BUG IS GENUINELY FIXED, verified by my own samples: front bun (85,73,64) against adjacent crown hair (85,71,60); profile bun (50,42,37); runtime bun (31,21,7) against side hair (23,13,0). Hair does not swallow the face: centre-column hairline sits at 38.6% of head height delivered vs 36.8% measured on the concept front figure (head centre x=217), a 1.8-point match, and brows, eyes and mouth are all clear of it.

Features are legible at hero scale and the face is visible in the front board view, so the 4 bar is met and I score it 4. It can never be 5, and both blockers are measured. (1) THE NOSE. From the front it is simply not there: an 8x crop of x220-330 y200-290 on bendy-bao-front-review.png shows unbroken cheek between the lens rims and the smile, no tip, no nostrils, no form shadow, and the same is true in all four runtime face stills. In profile I traced the front silhouette myself: the frontmost SKIN pixel is x=209 at rows 238-241 (the glasses rim owns x=213 at rows 199-235, so I stepped past it), against forehead skin at x=220 on row 196 - 11px of projection over a 210px head = 5.2%. The identical trace on the concept profile figure gives a nose peak of x=947 at rows 294-298 against a forehead of x=930 = 17px over a 242px head = 7.0%. The delivered nose is 74% of the drawn projection and reads as zero from the camera the game actually uses. (2) A visible decal-island seam runs temple-to-chin down the near cheek where the flattened face plane meets the round skull - clearest in the 6x run-still crop and present in every face still. Brows are flat black paint and the eyes are flat decals. ON THE RECORD'S LENS REQUIREMENT, checked and deliberately NOT filed as a defect: I grepped build_glasses in scripts/v2/blender/sculpt-bendy-bao-source.py and there is no lens-disc geometry at all - the builder emits two cyclic tubes, two temple arms and a bridge, with the comment 'Open rings - the atlas eyes read through them'. But the SKILL.md rule exists for sheets that FILL the rings with paper-cream shine, and a 5x crop of the concept face shows Bendy Bao's lenses are clear: skin, sclera, iris and highlight all read through at full opacity. Open rings are the drawing-correct construction for this kid, and the visible-face metric that would arbitrate was refused by the instrument, so no one should quote a number here either. THE TEMPLE-ARM REQUIREMENT IS MET: the arm bows outboard to side*0.470 in the builder, and it is visibly present in the render - a 10x crop of x240-310 y195-265 on the profile shows the dark wire crossing the cheek and terminating at the ear root, not buried inside the skull.

heroAndFieldScale.label: hero + 40px read

At 40px it does not hold up as a 4. The board's own zoom strip loses both glasses and stripes; what survives is a dark bump, a pale torso, dark shorts and tan shoes, which is a generic kid silhouette. Bendy Bao IS the glasses kid, and the one feature that names him is the first thing to go at field scale. Worse, the fallback identity carrier fails too: in the run and swing stills the hair mass reads as a round afro mop with a bump, not a swept top knot, so at gameplay distance he is competing with every other dark-haired kid on the roster rather than being read as the bespectacled one. The runtime tee measures a healthy 45.9 greenness amplitude at the torso centre, but the bands wash toward white on the lit side and contribute nothing below hero scale. Add the two runtime artifacts that are visible at exactly this distance - the torn shirt back in swing_contact and the black notch bitten out of the shoulder in run - and the field read is actively damaged rather than merely thin.

frontProfileSilhouette.label: front/profile silhouette
frontProfileSilhouette.note: The front board is recognisable; the PROFILE is not, and 3.1 scores both. Concept profile (turnaround panel 3, cropped 4x): an open face - forehead, a projecting button nose, philtrum, lips, chin, a clean jawline to the neck, and a large fully-exposed ear - with the mane swept behind it. Delivered profile: a featureless auburn egg. I measured the visible skin against the head silhouette in both with one detector: concept 91.5% of head width at its widest row (skin bbox 200x217 over a 200px head, 100%), delivered 46.4% (bbox 80x193 over a 153px head, 52.3%). Half the profile read is gone - no chin, no jaw, no mouth, no cheek, only a thin crescent along the leading edge with one eye and a nose tip. Profile head depth is 27.8% of figure height against the concept's 32.1%, so the skull is also ~13% shallow front-to-back (3.13). Transitions are not organic either: the mane is one ring loft that butt-joins the collar with no neck visible in profile at all, where the concept shows a clear neck between jaw and ringer collar. NOT severed and NOT holed - I flood-filled all four board renders: zero fully-empty rows inside the figure bbox in any view, zero enclosed background regions in profile, front-apose and profile-apose, and 2 regions totalling 6px (antialias) in front.

headBodyProportions.label: head/body proportions
headBodyProportions.note: Child proportion is broadly right in the A-pose front board and 1.4/featurelatitude are AUTO-green, so I make no bobblehead claim. The failure is 'joints read as connected forms'. Cropped at 8x, the hero arm is a plain tapering cone from shoulder to hand: no deltoid, no elbow, no wrist. It exits the sleeve as a hard step - the cream cuff ends and a visibly thinner skin tube begins, with a dark outline gap between arm and torso - and at 9x on the front board the hand is a flat paddle with three finger grooves and no thumb. The concept's toddler-chubby girth is absent; the recorded note concedes 'limbs read a notch slimmer' and then scores 4 anyway. Compounding it, the mane mass dominates the figure at gameplay angles: in the swing_contact still the head-plus-hair egg spans roughly 52% of the visible figure height from behind and swallows the shoulders and the whole bodice.

hairMass.label: hair mass
hairMass.note: Measured, and it fails in BOTH directions. Strand grouping: I ran measure:strands myself at the default 5-45% band and at four tighter bands to rule out fringe/brow contamination - 5-45%: 2.92 vs 5.86 minima/row = 50% of concept count at 251% prominence; 15-45%: 3.40 vs 5.84 = 58% at 233%; 10-40%: 47%; 20-60%: 46%; 5-30%: 37%. The deficit is band-independent, so it is not a detector artifact. The cause is confirmed in source: ring_loft_mane uses segments = 18 with clump = 1 + curl*sin(8*theta) - 2.25 columns per lobe, barely above Nyquist, so most of the clump is literally unrepresentable and the creases that survive are over-deep (2-2.5x prominence) instead of numerous. Volume: I measured the mane's max width on the A-pose board at 152px over a 550px figure = 27.6% of figure height (matching MANE_LEVELS max half_x 0.545 over a 3.92 figure = 27.8%, so the number is right), against the concept front panel's mane at the full 242px figure width over a 630px figure = 38.4%. The mane carries 72% of the concept's width. The rubric caps a smooth featureless blob at 4 'however correct its silhouette' - this silhouette is NOT correct: too narrow, faceted, with a blunt hard-cut bottom edge where the concept has scalloped S-wave tips. And it over-covers where it should not, erasing the profile face (see 3.1). Below the cap.

clothingConstruction.label: clothing construction
clothingConstruction.note: Real construction is present and I verified it at 8x rather than assuming: a crisp cream waistband with hard top and bottom edges (a constructed edge, not a painted gradient - I checked the transition specifically and it is a clean two-row step) carrying a genuinely sculpted five-point gold star, a cream ringer collar and cuffs, striped socks, a two-tone sole with a visible welt, and lace strokes. On colour I defer to the number: measure:fidelity puts the shoe band's dominant tone at 50.2 vs the concept's 51.9, the second tone at 49.8 vs 45.0 and mean saturation at 26.6 vs 25.9, all inside tolerance, so I make no shoe-split claim. What holds it at 3 is that the signature garment is unbuilt: the skirt is a smooth featureless cone with a flat straight hem where the concept's defining garment is a pleated A-line with visible vertical pleat folds and a scalloped hem. The laces are single 1-2px dark strokes with no eyelets, no tongue and no crossings (cropped at 14x - they read as stray dark specks), and the cream is a soft instep dome rather than the concept's stitched rubber toe cap.

faceExpressionRead.label: face/expression read
faceExpressionRead.note: Three defects, one of them an evidence failure. (1) dazzle-runtime-face-grin.png IS EMPTY - 82,133 bytes against 276,780 / 277,339 / 277,497 for angry / cheer / tongue, i.e. 29.6%, exactly the empty-frame signature. Opened, it is the DOM HUD on pure black: no field, no sky, no character - the WebGL canvas never drew. Cheer, angry and tongue are genuinely painted and their mouths do read at that distance (open mouth with teeth, a frown line, a tongue), but 3.14's four-still evidence is 3 of 4 and one expression is unverified. (2) The face is a DECAL ISLAND WITH A VISIBLE SEAM. Cropped at 6x from the runtime hero, the face plate is a distinctly lighter orange patch bounded by a hard polygonal edge running from the brow down the near cheek to the jaw, plus a straight vertical seam on the far cheek, and the brow is a floating dark bar whose end is cut flat on that boundary. Rubric 3.5 names 'no visible decal-island seam' as the test and this seam reads plainly at hero scale. (3) Expression is unreadable in profile: 46.4% visible skin at the widest head row vs the concept's 91.5%, with no mouth, no lips and no chin surfacing at all, so at every profile-ish gameplay angle the face has nothing to express with. To be fair to the asset and against its own recorded note: a nose DOES exist and DOES break the leading edge of the profile silhouette - that note is wrong in the asset's disfavour.

heroAndFieldScale.label: hero + 40px read
heroAndFieldScale.note: The 40px zoom strip does carry the one memorable read - brown mane over purple dress - and identity survives it. The hero close-up survives too, but only as a face peeking out of a wig, and it is where the seam (3.5) and the ear spike (3.10) are most visible, so the close-up actively costs the character. On the field: at 16x on the runtime hero the hands are the same warm orange as the infield dirt and effectively disappear into it, which is a 6.6 risk on a fielder. Held at 3 rather than lower because the silhouette is unmistakable at both ends of the range.

measuredFidelity.result: RUN MYSELF. measure:fidelity -- diva (concept front 242x630, delivered 452x549; shoe tones read off concept #f6ece1 and #f2cda3): shoe band dominant tone concept 51.9 / delivered 50.2 / delta -1.66 ok; second tone 45.0 / 49.8 / +4.74 ok; band mean saturation 25.9 / 26.6 / +0.73 ok; daylight between ankles 0.00 / 34.0 / +34.0 OFF (tol 12) - per 6b.4 read as stance, the concept panel has the ankles touching and the delivered bind pose stands wide, the legs are unambiguously two legs so 3.12 PASSES; five metrics NOT MEASURED (head height % of figure, head width:height, visible face left, visible face right, face L/R asymmetry) because the head/neck detector found no silhouette pinch between crown and shoulders - a fact about the drawing, not a pass.  measure:strands -- diva, BAND USED: I ran the default 5-45% AND four others precisely because the default can reach past the fringe onto forehead and brows where skin/hair and brow edges count as false creases. 5-45% (default, concept head rows 191-398, delivered 99-319): concept 5.86 minima/row at prominence 36.3 over 84 rows, delivered 2.92 at 91.0 over 89 rows => 50% of count, 251% of prominence. 15-45%: 5.84@42.0 vs 3.40@97.7 => 58% / 233%. 10-40%: 5.94@36.8 vs 2.79@82.3 => 47% / 224%. 20-60%: 7.44@47.9 vs 3.44@92.2 => 46% / 193%. 5-30%: 5.43@26.6 vs 2.04@53.8 => 37% / 202%. Band-independent; I report 15-45% as the cleanest (below the fringe, above the brow band at 37%).  MY OWN MEASUREMENTS (same detector both sides): mane max width, delivered A-pose board 152px over a 550px figure = 27.6% of figure height (cross-checked against MANE_LEVELS max half_x 0.545 over a 3.92 figure = 27.8%), concept front panel 242px over a 630px figure = 38.4% => the mane carries 72% of the concept's width. Profile visible skin at widest row: concept 183px over a 200px head silhouette = 91.5%, delivered 71px over a 153px head = 46.4%; skin bbox concept 200x217 (100.0% of head width), delivered 80x193 (52.3%). Profile head silhouette depth: concept 32.1% of figure height, delivered 27.8% (13% shallow). Severance/holes flood-fill on all four board renders: front y98..647 - 0 empty rows, 2 enclosed background regions totalling 6px (antialias); profile, front-apose, profile-apose - 0 empty rows, 0 enclosed regions. NOTHING IS SEVERED, 3.7 PASSES. Face-still byte sizes: grin 82,133 / angry 276,780 / cheer 277,339 / tongue 277,497 - grin is 29.6% of its siblings and is confirmed empty on inspection. Source values read, not assumed: ring_loft_mane segments = 18 with sin(8*theta) clump = 2.25 columns/lobe; EAR_SPEC center z 3.220 radii (0.125,0.150) with head span 3.99->2.68 => ear centre at 58.8% of head height; HEADBAND_ARC ends at z 3.440 = 42.0% of head height, tube radius 0.046.
measuredFidelity.note: Feature placement gated by featurelatitude: brow 37.25 vs traced 37.0, eye 54.1 vs 54.1, mouth 76.3 vs 76.1 through her declared 3.99-2.68 span (the spec refuses all three landmarks - the mane merges every band - so the targets are bounded traces). No earLine: the mane owns the width metrics; ears reviewed by eye.

polishFindings: THE 'NO earLine' CLAIM IS FALSE, and it is the load-bearing one. scripts/v2/turnaround-specs/dazzle.spec.json records landmarks.earLine = { value: 78.3, unit: pctOfHead, proudPctOfHead: 17.4, confidence: 'traced' } - the tracer found it and calls it traced, while brow, eye and mouth are the three it refused. The sheet plainly draws ears: cropped at 4x, the concept profile panel shows a large ear with an outer helix rim, an antihelix, a concha shadow and a lobe, sitting PROUD of the hair with the mane tucked behind it, and the same ear is visible in the three-quarter panel. Yet scripts/v2/featurelatitude.lint.test.js (diva entry, ~line 240) omits earLine on the stated ground that 'the widest row is the mane at 78.3%, hair on concept and delivery alike; her ears hide under the curtains' - the sculpt header repeats it at line 85. By that file's own comment at line 156, an entry without earLine SKIPS the ear check, so nothing gated the placement.

CONSEQUENCE, MEASURED: EAR_SPEC center z = 3.220 puts the ear centre at 58.8% of the 3.99->2.68 head - eye level, as the sculpt comment says - against the sheet's traced earLine of 78.3% (mouth level). The ear sits ~19.5 points of head height too HIGH, ungated.

3.10 FAIL (and 3.8 FAIL). The ear is NOT absent - I grepped and it is built: sculptlib.ear is imported at line 33, EAR_SPEC declared at line 137, build_ear called per side at line 620. It is BURIED and CLIPPING. In the profile board only two disconnected skin-coloured slivers surface through the mane (a small crescent and a tiny arrowhead, z 3.14-3.36, matching EAR_SPEC's z extent 3.07-3.37); in the runtime hero and run stills, cropped at 6x, it protrudes from the hair silhouette at the temple as a sharp pointed elf-ear spike. No rim, no inner shadow, no lobe against the skull from any angle - the exact 3.10 anti-pattern, arrived at from the opposite direction (not a bare ellipsoid bump but a shard of one).

NOT A DEFECT - I checked before reporting it. The pale cream annulus with a skin-toned, folded centre on the lower-rear head in dazzle-profile-review.png (original px x250-285, y284-317, i.e. z 2.36-2.60) initially reads as a button or a gouge. Cropped at 9x it is the near HAND plus its cream sleeve cuff, seen end-on down the T-pose arm pointing at the camera, exactly as a true 90-degree orthographic profile should show it. It is absent from the A-pose profile board, which confirms it. No artifact.

TEAM_MASK judged on EXTENT only, never colour (the headband is the declared team-accent surface - grey #D8D2C6 on the board, gold at runtime). Its extent is short: HEADBAND_ARC terminates at z 3.440 = 42.0% of head height, so the band stops on the crown above the eyes and never comes down beside the face. The concept draws a WIDE FLAT RIBBON that runs from the crown down past the temple to the top of the ear at ~78% of head height, roughly 2.5x the width of the delivered 0.046-radius round tube. Front-on this makes the delivered band read as a thick pale saddle across the crown rather than a hair ribbon.

Garment colour boundaries are CONSTRUCTED EDGES, not painted gradients - verified at 8x on the waistband, which steps cream-to-purple across two rows top and bottom with the sculpted gold star seated on it. The soft transitions elsewhere (sock stripe, skirt) are lighting, not colour ramps. This item passes and the round-1 'mushy gradient' repair held.

The skirt is a smooth cone with a flat hem - no pleats, no scalloped hem - against a concept whose signature garment is a pleated A-line. Same defect the recorded note concedes ('the colour-pleat wedges read only softly') while scoring 4.
Shoe laces are single 1-2px dark strokes with no eyelets, tongue or crossings; cropped at 14x they read as stray dark specks on the upper and vanish entirely at 40px.
Skin tone is very close to the infield dirt in the runtime stills; at 16x the hands are nearly indistinguishable from the ground. Worth a 6.6 check at gameplay camera.

swing_contact renders bat-less on the review page. I did not score it - the bat is likely a game-side attachment, not the GLB - but if the board is meant to be 4.5/4.2 evidence, a contact still with no bat cannot show a marker landing on 'bat meets ball'.
EVIDENCE MUST BE REGENERATED before any re-score: dazzle-runtime-face-grin.png is an empty frame and 3.14 cannot be assessed on four expressions until it is recaptured.

The recorded card asserts 'no nose breaking the hair-covered profile'. That is wrong in the asset's own disfavour - nose_push does build a real button nose and it does break the profile silhouette's leading edge. The profile's problem is the mane covering the jaw, not a missing nose; fixing the wrong thing would regress a feature that is already right.

frontProfileSilhouette.label: front/profile silhouette
frontProfileSilhouette.note: The gross read is right (egg dome, big round glasses, noodle neck, boxy striped tee, straight jeans, rolled cuffs) and the proportion metrics are green, but the two forms the sculpt script itself says 'carry the whole silhouette' both fail. (1) THE EARS DO NOT REACH THE OUTLINE. I measured the delivered front render (540x720, figure bbox y88-647): the head silhouette is widest at 162px at y187 - the DOME - and the ears break the outline only at rows 221-222, by 10px per side. At the traced ear line (57.9% of the 88->260 head band = y188) the right ear's outer edge is x342 while the skull edge is x349, so the ear is 7px INSIDE the outline and contributes nothing. The concept is the opposite: its head is widest AT THE EARS (229px at y252-262 vs 189px at y235 just above them), the ears exceed the skull for 60 rows (28.7% of head height) by 20px per side, and the repo's own trace records earLine proudPctOfHead 10.3 - delivered is 5.8% at the wrong latitude and 0% at the right one. Ears are BUILT (EarSpec/build_ear at line 541, radii 0.160/0.190) and in profile they do carry a rim and an inner concha shadow - this is a misbuilt, too-shallow, too-low ear, not a missing one. (2) THE PROFILE IS A FLAT WALL. In noodle-profile-review.png the entire face front from y153 to y200 sits on one dead-straight column at x=207 - that is the glasses ring seen edge-on with zero wrap - and the nose advances it to x=203 only at rows 200-211: 4px, 2.4% of the 165-row head band. The concept profile advances from x943 (lens line) to x959 (nose tip), 16px = 7.7% of its head band, three times as much. Credits: head depth/width 139/162 = 0.858 against the concept's 198/229 = 0.865, near-exact; NO severed rows in any of the four board renders (I ran a full row scan on front, profile, front-apose and profile-apose: zero rows with no figure pixels inside the bbox); legs are two legs. Held to 3 on the ear and the flat profile, plus the butt-joined shoulder wedge and the ankle 'napkin ring' called out below.

headBodyProportions.label: head/body proportions
headBodyProportions.note: The numbers are in tolerance and I re-took them: head height 29.0% vs concept 31.0% (delta -1.99, ok), head width:height 0.99 vs 1.04 (delta -0.05, ok). The child proportion and the signature over-long thin neck read correctly and the neck sits organically into the skull with no collar seam. What holds this at 3 is the second half of the rubric line - 'joints read as connected forms'. Both shoulders fail it, and they fail it where a player looks: in noodle-runtime-hero.png the far shoulder carries a hard-edged navy wedge roughly 20x25px at native scale, outlined by the rim shader so it reads as a TEAR in the tee, and the near sleeve cap is a butt-joined tube pushed into the torso with a crease instead of a deltoid. The same wedge is present and larger in noodle-runtime-run.png, where the far shoulder reads as a detached dark lump with its own outline floating off the torso. The hand at run is a stack of hard-edged bars separated by black outlines rather than a fist. Torso mass is also thin against the head: A-pose shoulder span 146px against a 162px head, and the T-pose torso below the armpit runs only 72-86px, so the head is 1.9x the torso's width.

hairMass.label: hair mass
hairMass.note: Abstained - null. NOODLE IS BALD; there is no hair mass to score and no hair surface is built (the script declares HAIR = #3A2A1C explicitly as an 'unused surface lane - he is bald; brows are atlas ink'). The bald negative space itself is intact in the board renders: one uninterrupted dome, no invented cap, no hairline seam, no hole. I did NOT run measure:strands, per the brief. One consequence of baldness belongs to other categories rather than here and is recorded there: because the crown is his own skin, the dome's faceting and its warmth shortfall land on the largest single surface he has.

clothingConstruction.label: clothing construction
clothingConstruction.note: Real construction is present and I verified the edges are constructed rather than painted: scanning down x=268 through the tee, every stripe boundary transitions in 1-2px (329->331, 348->350, 371->373, 392->394, 416->418) - these are vertex-colour edges, not gradients. Rolled jean cuffs exist on both legs, band y572-592 = 3.6% of figure height against the concept roll's 4.4%, correctly placed at the ankle on both legs (TEAM_MASK, judged on extent and placement only - the untinted grey on the board and the tinted olive at runtime are both expected). Wrist cuff band, cream cupsole and two cream lace straps are all built (straps=((-0.170,-0.122),(-0.060,-0.012)) in NOODLE_SHOE). Held at 3 for four things. (1) THE SHOE IS NOT A LACED LOW-TOP. Cropped at 6x front and 7x profile, the two authored straps render as flat cream stripes on the outer quarter; there is no throat, no eyelets, no tongue, no collar opening and no separately readable toe bumper. The concept shoe has four lace crossings, metal eyelets, a cream toe cap and a dark chevron; the delivery is a tan clog with racing stripes. The rubric names laces explicitly. (2) The dark navy wedge at both sleeve/torso junctions reads as a hole in the garment at hero and run scale (see headBodyProportions). (3) The jean cuff is a smooth ring WIDER than both the jean leg above it and the shoe below it, with a hard step at each end and no fold edge - a napkin ring, not a rolled hem. (4) Garment warmth is largely gone: the cream stripe delivers rgb(210,207,202), r-b = 8, against the concept's rgb(229,208,183), r-b = 46 - 17% of the concept's warmth - and the blue stripe delivers b-r = 19 against the concept's 36. Denim itself is fine, rgb(74,103,137) vs concept rgb(52,78,105).

faceExpressionRead.label: face/expression read
faceExpressionRead.note: Below the floor, and the cause is a mis-traced landmark that the gate then certified against itself. THE MOUTH IS ~9.5 POINTS OF HEAD HEIGHT TOO HIGH. The repo's own machine trace, scripts/v2/turnaround-specs/noodle.spec.json, records landmarks.mouth = { value: 78.9, row: 288, confidence: 'traced' }. My own luminance map of the concept confirms it exactly: the smile is the dark run at row 288, and rows 261-264 - which the sculpt script and featurelatitude.lint.test.js both cite as 'the small smile rows 262-270' - are his NOSTRILS (the nose bulb runs ~245-264). featurelatitude.lint.test.js's own header warns about precisely this failure mode ('...NOSTRIL not the lip line, so it reports the mouth 10 [points] high'); Noodle's hand-entered mouth: 69.4 is that mistake hard-coded, so the record's 'mouth 69.4/69.4 green' is the sculpt agreeing with its own error, not with the drawing. On the delivered render the mouth line is row 207 of the 88->260 head band = 69.2% - faithful to the wrong target. THE CONSEQUENCES ARE THE WHOLE CATEGORY. The smile sits directly under the lens rims with no philtrum, and the nose has nowhere left to live: in noodle-front-review.png, cropped at 8x across x230-310/y185-245, the region between the lenses is UNMODULATED SKIN - no bulb, no nostrils, no cast shadow, only a scatter of freckle dots - against the concept's large highlighted button nose with two dark nostril slits. nose_push IS built (line 128, 'centre nz -0.42'), so this is a nose too shallow and too low, not an absent one: in profile it is a 4px hard-edged wedge at rows 200-211, i.e. AT the mouth's own latitude, and it projects 2.4% of head height past the frame line where the concept's projects 7.7%. Eye-to-mouth spacing collapses to 11.4% of head height (iris centroid row 187.5, mouth row 207) against the concept's 25.3% (iris 233.5, mouth 288) - 45% of the drawing's - leaving the features crammed in a band under the glasses and the bottom quarter of the face blank. The measured visible-face shortfall follows: 35.6/35.6 against 45.4/44.0, OFF by 9.8 and 8.4 on a tolerance of 6, and at that sample row the delivered head is crossed by irises (11px and 9px), sclera and four frame crossings while the concept's same row is 88.6% clean skin. Expression: all four -runtime-face-*.png stills are genuinely painted and distinct (295-296 KB each, no undersized sibling - grin shows a teeth band, cheer an open O, tongue a pink tongue, angry a closed line), but in ALL FOUR the eyebrows are hidden behind the lens rims at the gameplay camera, so angry and neutral differ only by a flat mouth stroke and angry does not read as angry. At hero the near lens reads as a dark socket and the temple bar is the boldest mark on the face.

heroAndFieldScale.label: hero + 40px read
heroAndFieldScale.note: Identity survives at hero - bald dome plus big round glasses plus blue/cream stripes is unmistakable from front, three-quarter and behind - and that is what keeps this off a 2. Two things hold it well below approval. (1) THE DOME IS VISIBLY FACETED. Cropped at 4x from noodle-runtime-hero.png, the skull shows large flat polygon facets with hard shading breaks across the crown and occiput, and the same faceting is present in every runtime still (run, swing_contact, and all four face cells). On the one character whose crown is his own skin and his largest single surface, this is the first thing the eye lands on. (2) THE SKIN LOSES ITS WARMTH BAND, which his record says is load-bearing for him. I sampled the delivered board's upper dome at (250,110) 40x20: rgb(225,203,179), r-g = 22, sat 0.20, and 0% of that patch passes the project's own isSkin test (it fails sat > 0.22). The concept's dome at (195,150) 40x20 is rgb(253,208,154), r-g = 45, sat 0.39, 100% isSkin. Cheek: delivered r-g 29 / sat 0.31 against concept r-g 70 / sat 0.58.
