hairMass.label: hair mass
hairMass.note: It is one designed mass and the spikes are the identity, so it clears the floor of the category on read. It cannot go above 3. The cap is a perfectly smooth, featureless matte dome - rubric 3.3 caps that at 4 on its own - and the eleven spikes are clean unshaded cones with a hard rim where each meets the dome, no clump grouping, no strand carving anywhere on the cap. Cropped at 6x the hairline is a literal staircase: three axis-aligned rectangular hair blocks with 90-degree corners stepping across the forehead, and those blocks read at hero scale as two floating dark rectangles above the eyes in every runtime face still. measure:strands (default band, 5-45% of head height - I checked it does not reach the brows here because the fringe covers that zone entirely) gives 4.23 minima/row against the concept's 7.83, i.e. 54% of the strand count at 364% of the prominence: few, very deep separations. That is the signature of cones stuck in a helmet rather than the concept's overlapping locks.

clothingConstruction.label: clothing construction

(1) The shoulder-wedge coverage gap, cropped at 6x on the A-pose front: a dark navy triangular patch sits on each side of the collar filling the space the sleeve tube and torso fail to close, with straight edges that read as a pasted wedge; the collar's own top edge is a sawtooth zigzag of skin against navy, not a hem. (2) The shorts have no crotch and no waistband - the shirt hangs as a flat apron whose hem cuts straight across, background daylight starts immediately below it, and the two dark shorts tubes are butt-joined onto the shirt's sides with a hard diagonal corner notch at each hip. Credit where earned: sleeve cuffs are rolled bands, the collar is a real band, socks have a roll-top, and the shoe is genuinely built - navy upper, cream cupsole with a rim step, toe bumper, three cream lace stripes. But at 16x both shoes carry a dark diagonal seam sliver where the toe bumper meets the cupsole, symmetric on left and right, and it reads as a black tick at 1x on the board.

faceExpressionRead.label: face/expression read
faceExpressionRead.note: This is the worst thing on the model. There are NO EYEBROWS - not in the board front view, not in any of the four runtime expression cells. The concept's single strongest facial identity feature is a pair of thick angled black brows sitting on bare forehead skin, and the sculpt script traces them itself at rows 245-260 before refusing to build them ('the fringe merges them'). I judged that refusal against the sheet and it is circular. Column scans, same head band both sides: on the concept over the brow (x=205) the hairline ends at 53.3% of head height, the brow band runs 56.7-60.9%, the eye starts at 65.9%. On the delivered over the same feature (x=248, x=290) hair runs unbroken to 68.9% and the eye starts at 77.7%. The fringe hangs 15.6 points of head height lower than the drawing's and the face is pushed 12 points down with it, so the brow zone is buried by a hairline that was built too low - the fringe merges the brows because the fringe is wrong, not because the drawing lacks room. The cost is expression: 'angry' differs from neutral only in the mouth and reads mildly puzzled without brows to angle; 'cheer' and 'tongue' are all but identical, the tongue a two-pixel red speck inside the same open mouth. Mouths do carry lips and a teeth line, so 3.14 half-holds. The nose is a soft ridge with no nostril and does not break the profile.

heroAndFieldScale.label: hero + 40px read

The hero close-up is where he loses points, and the ear is the reason. At the 3/4 gameplay camera the ear is the largest single form on the head - a flat skin paddle running from the hairline past the jaw, wider in silhouette than the eye and the nose combined, with a thin rim ridge but no concha depth, no tragus, no lobe separation. Add the browless blank face at hero scale and the close-up is the weaker of the two reads.

hairMass.label: hair mass
hairMass.note: One designed mass and no bare-skull read from any angle — the buzz shell wraps the sides and back under the cap and the swing_contact rear view is covered. Two things hold it at 3. (a) The hairline is a hard low-poly boundary: at 9x the temple in moose-profile-review.png shows a literal rectilinear STAIRCASE where the hair edge meets the skull, plus a squared-off vertical rear silhouette — worse than a smooth blob, which the rubric already caps at 4. (b) measure:strands, my runs: default 5-45% band gives 0.42 vs 3.46 minima/row (12%) at 104% prominence, but that band is CAP for both images on a capped kid, so it is not a hair reading — it is reading the concept cap's panel seams and button against the delivered cap's featureless dome. Re-run tight on the cap, 5-42%: 0.20 vs 3.29 (6%). Re-run over the visible hair/sideburn zone, 40-62%: 3.68 vs 6.03 (61%); 45-75%: 5.05 vs 8.37 (60%); 55-85%: 4.50 vs 9.20 (49%) — and those low bands are contaminated by brows, eyes and the ear rim as false creases exactly as warned, so read 49-61% as an upper bound, not a score.

clothingConstruction.label: clothing construction
clothingConstruction.note: Real inventory, present and grepped in the sculpt script, not assumed: ribbed hem band (TORSO_LEVELS z1.470 proud, SHIRT_DARK), ribbed sleeve cuff (z1.300 SHIRT_DARK, proud — visible at 9x with five separated fingers below it), hood (HOOD_LEVELS, a real mass behind the neck in profile), kangaroo pocket, drawstrings, jogger elastic cuff (z0.428 PANTS_DARK proud), and a low-top with cupsole, toe bumper, sidewall stripes and a lace slot. What holds it at 3: the HOOD IS INVISIBLE FROM THE FRONT — the concept's thick hood ring frames the neck on both sides and the delivered front view shows a bare neck with nothing behind it; the DRAWSTRINGS are two flat rectangular slabs standing proud of a bare chest with no aglets and no collar to hang from (they read as two scratch marks at 4x); the hoodie hem ends in a hard 90-degree slab corner rather than a band wrapping the body; and a bare-skin ankle ring shows between the jogger cuff and the shoe (LEG_STATIONS z0.300/0.150 SKIN) where the concept cuffs the jogger straight into the shoe and the script's own comment says 'SOCK unused — joggers cuff into the shoes'. Above all the garments are draped on a torso 22-28% too narrow, so they read as a smock rather than a half-foot-deep kangaroo hoodie.

faceExpressionRead.label: face/expression read
faceExpressionRead.note: All four runtime-face stills are genuinely painted and DISTINCT — grin (closed teeth band), cheer (open mouth, upper teeth, red interior), tongue (teeth plus a pink tongue), angry (down-angled brows, closed frown) — and each is legible at draft-card distance, so 3.14 passes. The face itself is what fails. (a) NO NOSE READS FROM THE FRONT: nose_push exists in the script and a small nose does break the PROFILE silhouette, but in every front camera (board, hero, all four face stills) there is zero nose event — no tip highlight, no nostril, no shadow — on a kid whose sheet gives him a broad button nose with visible nostrils as a signature. (b) THE EARS ARE THE DEFECT. EAR_SPEC = EarSpec(center=(0.020,3.260), radii=(0.1700,0.1650)); across the 27 EAR_SPEC lines in scripts/v2/blender/sculpt-*-source.py Moose is the ONLY kid whose fore-aft radius is >= his vertical radius, i.e. the only circular ear on the roster. On the board I measure the profile ear at 50x55px on a 136px head = 36.8% wide by 40.4% tall, aspect 0.91, against the concept profile ear at 34x49px on a 162px head = 21.0% by 30.2%, aspect 0.69 — 1.34x oversized in height, 1.75x in depth, and round instead of oval. At 9x the construction is thin: a helix rim runs only down the FRONT edge with a shallow concha behind it, the rear two-thirds is a smooth featureless pad, and there is no tragus and no lobe separation, so 3.10 is a bare pass at best. From the front they read as earmuffs clamped on the face and they are the loudest thing on the head. (c) The brows are thin pointed slivers where the sheet draws thick soft brows, and the mouth is small on a wide face. (d) Board skin renders #bf7b46 against the sheet's #ab5b24 anchor and the hoodie renders #d9ac7a against #ed921c — the whole board is washed relative to the runtime stills, which do carry mustard; flagging as evidence hygiene, not scoring it. Near-side eye foreshortening in profile treated as EXPECTED, not filed.

heroAndFieldScale.label: hero + 40px read
heroAndFieldScale.note: Identity does not survive the shrink. At 40px (I downsampled the A-pose board to 40px tall myself and put it beside the concept front figure at the same height) the concept is unmistakably a stout, wide, round kid; the delivered is a slim kid in a tabard with a smooth dome on his head and two round blobs at ear height. The cap contributes NOTHING at 40px because it has no bill silhouette — it reads as a beanie or a helmet, where the concept's brim is a clear dark wedge off one side of the skull. So 3.9's 'one memorable read' is lost: what survives the shrink is the ears, and the ears are the wrong shape and 1.3-1.75x oversized. At hero the mustard hoodie and navy cap do carry the palette and the face is legible, and the runtime deformation is clean (run, swing_contact, idle all show continuous shoulders, elbows and knees, feet planted, no tearing, model model reported), which is the only reason this is a 2 and not a 1.

measuredFidelity.result: MY RUNS. npm run measure:fidelity -- moose (concept front 317x664, delivered 455x557): head height %fig 25.0 -> 24.4 (delta -0.58, ok); head width:height 1.11 -> 1.07 (-0.04, ok); shoe band dominant tone 83.1 -> 89.1 (+5.97, ok); shoe band second tone 13.7 -> 8.17 (-5.57, ok); shoe band mean saturation 22.6 -> 19.9 (-2.74, ok); daylight between ankles 0.00 -> 30.2 (+30.2, OFF tol 12); visible face left of centre 18.9 -> 39.0 (+20.1, OFF tol 6); visible face right of centre 27.6 -> 39.7 (+12.2, OFF tol 6); face L/R asymmetry 0.00 -> 0.68 (ok). 3 metrics outside tolerance; the two face-visibility misses are driven by the cap's missing brim leaving the whole brow line and temples bare skin, and the ankle-daylight miss is a bind-pose stance difference against a feet-together drawing (not widened, not re-filed as a leg defect). npm run measure:strands -- moose: default 5-45% band 0.42 vs 3.46 minima/row = 12% of concept count at 104% prominence; my re-runs at 5-42% (cap only, both) 0.20 vs 3.29 = 6%; 40-62% 3.68 vs 6.03 = 61%; 45-75% 5.05 vs 8.37 = 60%; 55-85% 4.50 vs 9.20 = 49% — the low bands include brows/eyes/ear rim as false creases. MY OWN PIXEL MEASUREMENTS, both images normalised to 4.0ft (concept 0.006024 ft/px, board 0.0071813 ft/px), arms-down in both. Front half-span concept/delivered by z(ft): 2.60 0.6747/0.4596 (-0.2151); 2.40 0.7831/0.5601 (-0.2230); 2.20 0.8735/0.6248 (-0.2487); 2.00 0.9337/0.6822 (-0.2515); 1.80 0.9518/0.7397 (-0.2121); 1.60 0.9307/0.7899 (-0.1408); 1.47 0.9518/0.8043 (-0.1475); 1.35 0.9307/0.8258 (-0.1049). Profile depth (ft) concept/delivered: z2.40 0.898/0.704; z2.00 0.997/0.790; z1.60 0.966/0.819; z1.47 0.868/0.833; z0.95 0.702/0.417. Leg check against the script's own record 'measured: front z=0.95 halfWidth=0.6295 tol=0.08': concept 0.6325 (agrees), delivered 0.4524 (-0.180ft = 2.25x tol); leg flesh per leg concept 0.593ft vs delivered 0.395ft (67%); inter-leg daylight at z0.95 concept 6.2% / delivered 12.7%, at z0.65 concept 13.8% / delivered 23.8%. On the board: profile bill x167-208 = 42px long = 31% of head height (matches the concept's 31%), vertical extent 4-6px (3.0-4.4% of head height) against the concept brim's ~30px (18%) because the concept brim CURVES DOWN; measured board droop 1.5px over 41px = 2.1 degrees. Front board: cap navy y90-150, max width 126px, and the bill row (y144-150) is also exactly 126px — the bill adds 0px to the front silhouette and every row has count==span (a solid dome, no brim wings past the face). Concept front cap: navy y181-272, max width 152px on a 185px head (82%), and rows 202-272 have span 108-152 with count only 5-109, i.e. the brim descends past the brow as two side wings with face between. Cap vertical coverage: concept 55.4% of head height, delivered 44.1%. EARS. Profile outline delivered 50x55px on a 136px head (36.8% x 40.4%, aspect 0.91); concept 34x49px on a 162px head (21.0% x 30.2%, aspect 0.69). EAR_SPEC radii (0.1700, 0.1650) — the only one of 27 roster EAR_SPECs with fore-aft >= vertical. Turnaround spec records earLine 74.5% of head, proud 12.7% of head width. INTEGRITY. A first pass using a colour-tolerance backdrop reported the shoes as separate islands; cropping the region at 6x and reading raw pixels showed the ankle band is OPAQUE (alpha 255) at RGB ~(7,10,16) — a near-black 3px ambient crease, not background. Reporting it as a polish finding, not a severance. 40px: A-pose board downsampled to 40px tall beside the concept front figure at the same height. Board colour: skin #bf7b46 vs sheet anchor #ab5b24, hoodie #d9ac7a vs sheet #ed921c; runtime stills do render mustard.
measuredFidelity.note: Feature placement gated by featurelatitude: brow 52.2 vs traced 52.0, eye 66.7 vs 66.7, mouth 87.1 vs 87.0, ear line at the traced 74.5, through his declared 3.99-3.00 span (the smallest head span on the roster).

polishFindings: HEADLINE: the body is 16-32% narrower than the drawing at every torso station and 15-22% shallower in profile; the shin is 41% shallower. 'Moose is the big one' is not in the delivered mesh. Widen TORSO_LEVELS (max half_x 0.480ft against a drawing that runs 0.82-0.95 half, per the script's own comment) and LEG_STATIONS before anything else.

The sculpt misses its own recorded measurement: 'measured: front z=0.95 halfWidth=0.6295 tol=0.08' above LEG_STATIONS. Delivered 0.4524ft — 2.25x outside its stated tolerance. Whatever gate is supposed to read that comment is not reading it.

CAP BILL, the roster's repeat defect, present here in the width form: brim half-widths 0.310/0.295/0.235ft are all inside the dome's 0.452ft, so the bill contributes 0px to the front silhouette (bill row and dome row both 126px). Widen the brim base past the dome and drop the tip: 0.010ft over 0.335ft is 1.71 degrees, flatter than the kid who was rejected at 2.4 degrees for reading as a beanie. The concept brim descends to 55.4% of head height and wraps the temples; this one stops at 44.1%.

EAR_SPEC radii (0.1700, 0.1650) is the only circular ear among 27 roster specs. Measured delivered ear 36.8% x 40.4% of head height (aspect 0.91) against the concept's 21.0% x 30.2% (aspect 0.69). Shrink it and make it taller than deep; it is currently the loudest feature on the head at hero AND at 40px.
Ear construction is thin for 3.10: helix rim only along the front edge, shallow concha, rear two-thirds a smooth pad, no tragus, no lobe separation. Verified at 9x, not eyeballed.

No nose reads from any front camera — board, hero, and all four face stills — though nose_push exists and the profile nose does break the silhouette. The sheet's broad button nose with nostrils is a signature; give it a tip highlight and nostril shading that survives the front ortho.

The concept gives Moose no neck (row span 23.9% of figure height at the 26% station); the delivered inserts a bare neck stalk (9.7% at the same station) and shows no hood from the front. Bring the hood collar roll forward so it frames the neck as the sheet does.
Drawstrings are two flat rectangular slabs standing proud of a bare chest, no aglets, hanging from nothing. At 4x they read as scratch marks.

Hair boundary at the temple is a rectilinear staircase in the profile board at 9x, and the rear hair silhouette is squared off. Both are polygon-resolution artifacts on the hair shell, not a mass problem.

Both ankles carry an opaque near-black crease at RGB ~(7,10,16), ~3px tall across the full ankle in the front board. It is not a hole (alpha 255, one connected component) but at 40px it detaches the shoe from the leg. Lift the AO or close the cuff-to-collar gap.

A bare-skin ankle ring shows between the jogger cuff and the shoe (LEG_STATIONS z0.300/0.150 SKIN) where the sheet cuffs the jogger into the shoe — the script's own comment says 'SOCK unused — joggers cuff into the shoes'.
The hoodie hem terminates in a hard 90-degree slab corner rather than a band wrapping the body; visible at 9x on the A-pose left hip.

TEAM_MASK extent is fine and correctly a badge, not a panel (half-width 0.105ft on a 0.452ft half-dome = 23% of cap width, front-centre) — but it is a plain hard-edged rectangle with no border or embroidery, so it reads as a sticky note on a curved dome. Judged on extent, not colour.

The board renders the whole figure washed against the sheet (skin #bf7b46 vs anchor #ab5b24, hoodie #d9ac7a vs #ed921c) while the runtime stills do carry mustard. Not scored, but the fidelity board is the colour evidence of record and it currently understates the palette.

GOOD, do not regress: all four runtime-face stills are genuinely painted and distinct and read at card size; no severance and no holes in any board view; no shoulder fin shear at the sleeve/torso junction in T-pose, A-pose, run or swing_contact; the cuff, hem, pocket, hood, jogger elastic and cupsole shoe are all really built; head height and head aspect both inside tolerance; leg daylight (3.12) re-measured and correct.

frontProfileSilhouette.label: front/profile silhouette
frontProfileSilhouette.note: Independent re-score 2026-08-16 (critic != sculptor). Front reads and survives desaturation, but the PROFILE does not match the turnaround at all: in penny-profile-review.png (head x~200-400, y~70-290) the hair swallows the whole face - only an eye sliver and a nose spike escape - where penny-turnaround.png's profile view (x 732-950) draws brow, eye, nose, lips, chin and jawline entirely clear of a temple hairline. Also short of the 5-clause by visible butt joints at sleeve/torso, strap/bib and neck/shoulders (penny-front-apose-review.png x 195-215, y 285-300).

headBodyProportions.label: head/body proportions
headBodyProportions.note: Independent re-score: child proportion broadly reads and head width:height measures 1.19 against the concept's 1.17, in tolerance; head height is the recorded -2.07 miss. Held at 3 by the clause's second half - joints read as CONNECTED forms - which fails: the arm leaves the sleeve as a uniform tube with no deltoid, the neck is a plain cylinder butt-joined into the shoulders, there is no knee break, and the hands are flat paddles with a thumb nub.

hairMass.label: hair mass
hairMass.note: Independent re-score, and the instrument settles it: measure:strands reads 0.42 minima/row against the concept's 15.46 - 3% of its strand count - at 324% of its prominence, i.e. no strand structure at all and what variation exists is shading facets three times too coarse. Below the 4 baseline too, because the hairline reads from NEITHER side: the hair meets the forehead as one smooth featureless arc (penny-front-review.png x 140-400, y 70-290) and cuts flat at the nape. The concept draws dozens of countable ringlets with a ragged lobed outline; her one memorable read has become a bowl cut.

clothingConstruction.label: clothing construction
clothingConstruction.note: Independent re-score, and the strongest category - a genuine 4. Two straps with brass buttons, a raised bib patch pocket, a pink ringer tee with a proud deeper-pink sleeve cuff, a separate proud rolled-denim ankle cuff carrying the declared recessTeamAccent, and shoes with a real midsole/outsole step and three raised lace bands. The waist now carries a constructed hem: a ring pair straddling the colour boundary with the denim waistband standing 0.010ft proud of the tee, replacing a 0.20ft painted gradient. Short of 5: hip pockets are flat recessed rectangles rather than outlined patch pockets, there is no topstitching where the concept's denim is defined by gold topstitch at every seam, and the sneaker's criss-cross laces with eyelets and side chevron are reduced to three straight bands.

faceExpressionRead.label: face/expression read
faceExpressionRead.note: Independent re-score: 3.14 IS satisfied - the four runtime expression stills open a real mouth with teeth, throat and tongue, readable at card distance - and a nose form does break the profile. But the 5-clause fails by name: the face reads as a lighter mask island set into a keyhole in the hair, with a hard boundary where a raised muzzle/cheek pad meets the face plate and a vertical ridge crease from the brows down the nose, and the nose is a hard triangular wedge rather than a rounded button. Worse for gameplay, at both 3/4 angles the game actually uses (penny-runtime-hero.png, penny-runtime-run.png, head x~415-610, y~165-320) the hair covers most of the face: one eye, no mouth.

heroAndFieldScale.label: hero + 40px read
heroAndFieldScale.note: Independent re-score: the 40px strip survives as 'brown-haired kid in blue overalls with cream shoes', but the hair blob at that size is indistinguishable from a bowl cut, so the read is generic rather than HERS. The hero half fails harder - the close-up is a hair blob with one visible eye and no mouth, which is not an identity.

measuredFidelity.result: Re-run 2026-08-16 after the waist-hem pass, by the independent critic rather than the sculptor. The SAME three metrics remain outside tolerance and no new one joined them: head height 32.8 vs 34.9 (-2.07), ankle daylight 12.7 vs 0.00, visible face left 34.7 vs 27.4 (+7.29). All three keep the causes recorded in the 2026-08-15 pass - the rig's roster-wide splay, and the concept sheet's own 6.5-point left/right lighting split (the Moose class) against an evenly-lit board. Head width:height 1.19 vs 1.17, shoe band 59.1/40.9 vs 63.1/35.9 with saturation 24.8 vs 27.0, face asymmetry 1.39 - all in tolerance. measure:strands (new instrument, PR #164) reads 0.42 strand minima/row against the concept's 15.46 at mean prominence 97.8 against 30.2: 3% of the concept's strand COUNT at 324% of its prominence. That is the hairMass 2, measured rather than eyeballed - there is no strand structure, and what surface variation exists is shading facets three times too coarse. Three eye-suspicions were checked and DISCARDED because the numbers refused them: shoe accent share (delivered 1659/5527 vs concept 4161/15179 - the same), hair bbox aspect (1.125 vs 1.105), and pink tee coverage (delivered 48.6% vs concept 39.4% - MORE pink, the opposite of the suspicion).
measuredFidelity.note: Feature placement gated by featurelatitude: brow 40.9 vs traced 40.9, eye 56.4 vs 56.4, mouth 73.6 vs 73.5 through her declared 3.99-2.60 span (the spec refuses all three - the curls merge every band). ⚠️ THE PREVIOUS 'no earLine' JUSTIFICATION WAS WRONG ABOUT THE DRAWING. It recorded that 'the bob owns the width rows and covers her ears in every view; none are built (Grizz precedent)'. Her turnaround's profile view (x 732-950) draws a fully constructed ear - outer helix rim, concha shadow, lobe - entirely clear of the hair, and draws the whole face clear of it too. Grizz's precedent does not transfer: HIS afro genuinely covers his ears in every view and his sheet builds none. Hers is a sculpt defect, not an absent feature, and it is now finding 3.

polishFindings: Sculpt real curl clumps into the hair - discrete ringlet lobes across crown, sides and back. Target the instrument: measure:strands wants ~15 minima/row at ~30 prominence against the current 0.42 at 97.8. A noise displacement raises prominence WITHOUT adding minima and is the wrong fix.

★ HIGHEST VALUE: pull the hair back off the face in profile and 3/4. The fringe overhangs past the brow and covers cheek, mouth and jaw; the concept sets the hairline at the TEMPLE with the mass springing back behind it. This one fix repairs silhouette, face read and hero read together.

Build ears and expose them - rubric 3.10 is currently failing outright. The concept profile draws a fully constructed ear (outer helix rim, concha shadow, lobe against the skull) sitting clear of the hair. The record's previous claim that her hair 'covers her ears in every view' is contradicted by the drawing.

Break up the hair faceting: straight silhouette segments and flat shading bands are visible at hero scale (penny-profile-apose-review.png x~370-400, y~140-250, and across the crown of the swing still). This is what drives the 324% prominence reading.

Kill the muzzle island seam - merge the raised cheek/mouth pad into the skull's planes so no boundary line flanks the mouth, and round the nose from a triangular wedge into a child's button that still breaks the profile.

Give the front a hairline: even with the mass pulled back the hair meets the forehead as a featureless arc. A fringe with a couple of curl clumps overlapping the forehead is what reads as hair from the front.
Build the shoulder - a deltoid mass so the arm does not leave the sleeve as a uniform cylinder, tapering toward the elbow so the elbow line reads (3.11).
Soften the remaining butt joints: sleeve->torso, strap->bib, neck->shoulders. These are what stand between the silhouette and its named 5-clause.
Bring the nape down - delivered hair ends at the nape leaving a bare neck column (penny-runtime-swing.png x~270-340, y~390-425); the concept's mass falls to the shoulder line and covers it.

Denim detail for the clothing 5: outline the hip pockets as patch pockets, add contrasting topstitch to the bib edge, side seams and pocket mouths, and give the sneaker real criss-cross laces with eyelets plus the side chevron.

Head height is 2.07pp short (32.8 vs 34.9) - recorded, but it sits at the tolerance edge and is part of why the 40px read feels generic. Worth reclaiming alongside the hair work rather than left as a permanent exception.

frontProfileSilhouette.label: front/profile silhouette
frontProfileSilhouette.note: Front reads: round glasses, open brown jacket over cream, blue jeans, dark hair. Profile does not. The hair in profile is an angular faceted SLAB -- a flat vertical back plane, a flat front plane, hard chamfered polygon corners at the crown -- reading as a cardboard box, not the turnaround's rounded, layered, swept mass. Verified at 8x on the-professor-profile-review.png and -profile-apose-review.png; the facets are 18-column ring-loft edges, not compression. Rubric 3.1's five asks for organic transitions and this ships the opposite: the sleeve terminates at the wrist in a bare diameter STEP (front-review.png x20-230 y265-335 at 4x) with no cuff form, a literal butt-joined primitive. The jacket in profile is a smooth cone that flares continuously from chest to a hard horizontal hem cut, with no waist -- the turnaround's cropped bomber silhouette is gone. NOT severed anywhere: neck, wrists and ankles are continuous in every crop I took. Legs are NOT fused -- 3.12 passes with clear daylight between thighs and calves in bind, A-pose and run (measured daylight 14.5 vs concept 0.00, and per 6b.4 that is the concept's legs-together DRAWING, not a sculpt fault). Ears pass 3.10 outright: the profile crop shows a genuine outer rim, an inner shadow and a lobe against the skull, not an ellipsoid bump.

headBodyProportions.label: head/body proportions
headBodyProportions.note: The strongest category and the only one I would sign. Measured myself: head height 31.1% of figure vs the concept's 32.3% (-1.19, ok); head width:height 1.04 vs 1.00 (+0.04, ok) so 3.13 passes and no bobblehead. Child proportion, not the proxy. Legs read as two legs. Shoulders hold a rounded deltoid through swing_contact and run rather than collapsing to a hinged cylinder, and the elbow line stays continuous in the run still. One deduction from 5: the wrist and the shoulder are diameter steps rather than connected forms -- the sleeve is a constant-radius cylinder shoulder-to-wrist with no taper and no elbow mass, so the joints read as joined tubes rather than connected forms, which is exactly what 3.2 asks about.

hairMass.label: hair mass
hairMass.note: I grepped the builder rather than inferring it, and the premise handed to me is understated. ring_loft_sweep is called exactly ONCE (sculpt-the-professor-source.py:619) and is the only hair geometry in the file -- no clump pass, no lobe pass, nothing. Inside it the ring is x = half_x*cos(theta), y = y_centre + half_y*sin(theta): a plain ELLIPSE per row, 18 columns, with ZERO lobe or crease modulation authored at all. There is no 6-lobe clump to be under-sampled; there is no clump. So the only minima measure:strands can find are the 18-facet polygon corners, and it reports 2.54 minima/row against the concept's 8.87 -- 29% of the count at 168% of prominence. I re-ran at 5-28% (30%) and 5-22% (27%) to strip the forehead and brow contamination the default 5-45% band can reach; the ratio does not move, so the shortfall is the hair, not the instrument. Rubric 3.3's own words -- 'a smooth featureless blob caps at 4 however correct its silhouette' -- put the ceiling at 4, and three further faults take it below: (1) the concept's asymmetric side-sweep is gone, SWEEP_BIAS 0.085 is imperceptible and the delivered mass reads as a symmetric mushroom bowl; (2) the hairline over the forehead is a jagged blocky STAIRCASE with a castellated rectangular step at centre, plainly visible at 8x and at hero scale (it is skin showing through, not background -- not a hole); (3) it swallows the face, see below.

clothingConstruction.label: clothing construction
clothingConstruction.note: Genuinely split. The shoes are the best-built thing on him and I will not mark them down: cream sole with a raised toe bumper, a taupe canvas upper, three cream lace stripes and an eyelet tab, over properly rolled cream jean cuffs -- constructed footwear, matching the turnaround's read. I also confirmed a collar exists in profile with a stitch line and a small collar point, and the open jacket's fold-back front edges do read. Per the record's warning I did NOT treat the shoe colour as a finding: all three shoe metrics came back ok (dominant tone -3.33, second tone +6.46, mean saturation -2.69), the drawn grey upper sits above the bottom-9% band the metric samples, and the delivered upper reads taupe rather than the concept's cooler grey only by eye. The jacket is where it fails. Against the turnaround: no zipper (the concept draws a full front zip with a pull), no pockets (the concept draws two prominent flap pockets with buttons on both front views), no ribbed cuff (a bare diameter step instead), no ribbed waist hem band, and no back yoke seam (visible in the concept's back view, absent in the swing_contact rear still). Roughly half the constructed detail on the SIGNATURE garment is missing, and without the waistband the jacket reads as a flaring labcoat rather than a cropped bomber.

faceExpressionRead.label: face/expression read
faceExpressionRead.note: The worst category, and it is measured. BOTH EYEBROWS ARE COMPLETELY BURIED UNDER THE FRINGE in every single delivered frame -- front board, A-pose, hero, run, and all four expression stills. They are authored (face-specs.mjs the_prof browY 21, browThick 4.6, browHalf 13) and the sculpt script itself calls his brows 'the boldest mark on a face', so this is an occlusion fault, not an omission. I measured it: scanning hair-tone coverage per row across the head, the CONCEPT opens forehead skin past 25% of head width at 30% of head height and is 43% hair / 54% skin by the traced brow latitude of 44.4%; the DELIVERED is still 87% hair at 40%, 62% hair at the 44.2% brow latitude, and does not open past 25% skin until 42.9%. The fringe descends about 13 percentage points of head height lower than the drawing's, over a brow line the sheet keeps clear. The consequences are not cosmetic: (a) at 12x a hair wedge with a hard straight chord cuts across the viewer-right lens and eats the outer half of that eye and part of the iris -- geometric interpenetration, not a shadow, which is a 3.8 failure at hero scale; (b) rubric 3.14 fails on one of four cells -- grin, cheer and tongue are properly built (upper teeth, an open dark interior with a lower-lip highlight, a pink tongue breaking the lip line, all four stills distinct by md5 and all ~280KB, none empty) but ANGRY is indistinguishable from neutral apart from a small downturned mouth oval, because the brow is the only carrier of anger on a toon face and his never renders; (c) the profile shows no eye, no brow and no mouth at all. This also explains both OFF metrics I ran: visible face left of centre 25.3% vs 11.9 (+13.4) and right 25.3% vs 14.2 (+11.1) -- the delivered brow row is bare skin where the concept's is brow ink. Credit where due: the nose DOES break the profile silhouette (verified at 8x, a distinct wedge -- 'no nose' would have been a false finding), the eyes and round frames read strongly head-on, and asymmetry measures 0.00.

heroAndFieldScale.label: hero + 40px read
heroAndFieldScale.note: At hero the review page confirms 'model model' (4.1 satisfied) and the round glasses plus the brown-over-cream torso carry him -- but the fringe throws the eye region into shadow at the gameplay 3/4 camera, so the eyes read as two dark smudges and the face has no brow to anchor it. At the 40px strip his one memorable mark, the round wire glasses, is sub-pixel and gone; what survives is dark blob hair, a brown/cream torso split and blue legs, which is a generic read rather than a specific one. 3.9 is therefore weak: he survives the hero close-up on the glasses and loses at 40px, and the rubric asks for both. Fielder visibility against grass and dirt is fine -- the dark hair and mid-brown jacket separate cleanly from both in the runtime stills.

polishFindings: THE HEADLINE: the fringe descends ~13 percentage points of head height below the concept's and buries BOTH eyebrows in every delivered frame. Measured: the delivered head row at the traced brow latitude (44.2%) is 62% hair where the concept's is 43%; skin does not open past 25% of head width until 42.9% against the concept's 30.1%. Angry is not angry. With the brows permanently covered, the angry cell differs from neutral only by a small downturned mouth oval and will read as 'confused' at draft-card distance. Rubric 3.14 fails on that one cell; grin, cheer and tongue are all correctly built with teeth, lip and tongue.

The hair carries ZERO authored strand grouping. ring_loft_sweep's ring is a bare ellipse with no lobe term -- there is nothing for measure:strands to find but the 18 polygon facets, which is why it sits at 27-30% of concept count across every band I tried. Adding lobes into the same 18 columns will not help (the instrument's own header records this); columns, or a sharpened crease profile, is the lever.

The hairline over the forehead is a jagged blocky staircase with a castellated rectangular step at centre -- the 18-column loft intersecting the skull front unsmoothed. Clearly visible at hero scale. Skin shows through, not background, so it is not a hole.
The concept's asymmetric side-sweep is lost; the delivered mass reads as a symmetric mushroom bowl. SWEEP_BIAS 0.085 is below the threshold of visibility on the board.

In profile the hair is a faceted angular SLAB -- flat back plane, flat front plane, hard chamfered crown corners. It reads as a box. This is the single largest gap between the delivered profile silhouette and the turnaround's.

The jacket is missing most of its construction: no zipper, no flap pockets (the concept draws two with buttons), no ribbed cuff (a bare sleeve-to-wrist diameter step instead), no ribbed waist hem, no back yoke seam. NOT findings, checked and cleared so they are not re-raised: nothing is severed (neck, wrists, ankles continuous); legs are not fused, 3.12 passes in bind, A-pose and run and the +14.5 ankle-daylight delta is the concept's legs-together drawing per 6b.4; ears are properly constructed with rim, inner shadow and lobe (3.10); a real nose breaks the profile silhouette; the shoe 'grey vs cream' question is instrument geometry, all three shoe metrics measure ok; all four expression stills are genuinely painted and distinct; the profile's near-side eye absence is partly the expected 90-degree foreshortening, though here it is total occlusion by hair rather than foreshortening; the glasses ring standing proud of the cheek in profile is a receding-brow geometry artefact, not floating accessory geometry.

frontProfileSilhouette.label: front/profile silhouette
frontProfileSilhouette.note: The body silhouette is right - bomber, cuffed jeans, low-tops all read with colour stripped. The cap is not. In profile the crown is a smooth hemisphere and the brim is a constant-thickness rectangular plank with a square tip, butt-joined at a hard corner; the sheet draws a six-panel dome with a button and seam arcs, and a thick tapering shelf whose sides roll down. From the front the brim collapses to an 8px strip on a ~160px head (5%) against the sheet's 22-33px on a 196px head (11-17%), so the front silhouette reads as a bowl hat with a rim, not a ballcap. Butt-jointed primitives are explicitly what 3.1 caps, and this is the clearest case on the board. 3, not 4, because the cap IS the character and its large read is wrong from the front.

headBodyProportions.label: head/body proportions
headBodyProportions.note: Measured, not eyeballed: head height 32.3% of figure against the concept's 33.1% (-0.82, ok) and head width:height 0.89 against 0.93 (-0.04, ok) - both inside tolerance, so 3.13 holds and this is the concept's head, not the proxy's. Joints read as connected forms: the shoulder stays a rounded deltoid where the arm drops in the A-pose, the elbow line is continuous through run and swing_contact, knees do not pinch. Neck-into-jacket is a plain cylinder junction and the torso is a single tapered tube rather than the sheet's slight chest/waist break, which is what keeps it off a 5.

hairMass.label: hair mass

That is up from the 20% recorded for him in the roster sweep and well clear of the 15% line the instrument's header marks as the point where the number stops being the target; band is upper-middle of the roster's 2-57% spread. Front board shows a genuinely designed hairline - scalloped fringe across the forehead with temple lobes falling over the ears - and no bare-skull read at any board or runtime angle. The profile is where it stops: one smooth featureless mass with a hard stepped cut at the sideburn. Grouping on one view, blob on the other, so 4.

clothingConstruction.label: clothing construction
clothingConstruction.note: Real construction is present and I checked the builder before saying anything was missing: the navy ribbed cuff reads as a distinct band at the wrist, the jeans carry a rolled light-blue cuff, the shoes have a two-tone cupsole, a toe bumper and lace strokes (shoe band metrics all in tolerance - dominant tone 65.1 vs 69.7, second 26.9 vs 28.4, saturation 23.5 vs 22.3). But the jacket's loudest sheet details do not survive. The collar rib is authored at z 2.575/2.600 yet reads on the board only as two black wedges at the shoulder tops - there is no band across the front of the neck. The hem rib is a hairline where the sheet makes it the jacket's strongest horizontal. Grepping sculpt-ace-source.py for 'zip' and 'pocket' returns nothing: the front zipper with its pull and the welt pockets, both prominent on all five sheet views, are genuinely not built. And at 12x the tee's top edge against the neck is a 1-2px sawtooth. Colour boundaries themselves are constructed - jacket/tee, cuff, jean roll and sole splits all land on geometry rings with a 1-2px ramp, not painted gradients.

faceExpressionRead.label: face/expression read

Held to 4 by the eyebrows, which are hard-edged flat quadrilaterals against the sheet's tapered brows, and by a nose that all but disappears in the front board render - a soft shadow where the sheet has a defined tip and nostrils.

heroAndFieldScale.label: hero + 40px read

frontProfileSilhouette.label: front/profile silhouette
frontProfileSilhouette.note: THE SEVERANCE IS A TRUE BREAK, NOT A NEAR-MISS AT A THIN WAIST. I re-scanned both bind-pose boards myself: row y=421 (60.6% from crown, 39.4% height) carries ZERO figure pixels across the entire body in rocket-rosa-front-review.png and rocket-rosa-profile-review.png. It is not a pinch — y=420 is the cream shirt hem spanning x224-315 (92px, one of the WIDEST points on the figure) and y=422 is the shorts spanning x217-322; 100% of that width vanishes for one row. Sampled alpha at y421 x230/250/270/290 = 2,4,4,4 (front) and 0,11,17,10 (profile): effectively transparent, ~2% coverage, real background. The A-pose boards report 'no empty rows' ONLY because the dropped arms bridge that scanline (front-apose y421 = [[165,185],[354,374]] — arm spans only, torso still gone). Cropped at 8x it is unmistakable: a clean horizontal slit of backdrop running the full hip width between the shirt slab and the shorts. It is masked at runtime by the toon ink outline, so it is a board/3.7 failure rather than a live-render one — but 3.7 is a board check and it fails. SECOND, INDEPENDENT HOLE at the same junction: y422-435 has a 6px see-through notch at x267-272 between the two shorts side-boxes, above the separate centre gusset — you see backdrop through the shorts crotch for 14 rows. Beyond the holes, the large read misses the turnaround: from the FRONT the character is a centred top-knot bun, not the sheet's high side ponytail; from BEHIND (swing_contact, the batting camera's own angle) cap and tail merge into one undifferentiated soft-serve cone with no tail read at all; in PROFILE the tail is a flat faceted sail with a hard spike at the top-back and a sharp V-chip where the crest tube butt-joins the fan (cropped at 12x — a construction corner, not a hair groove). And the stance is wrong: my own measure:fidelity run gives ankle daylight 54.2 delivered vs 0.00 concept, +54.2 against a tolerance of 12 — a wide splayed A where the sheet stands narrow.

headBodyProportions.label: head/body proportions
headBodyProportions.note: The measurable half is genuinely good and I will not punish it: my own measure:fidelity run gives head height 36.5% of figure vs the concept's 36.5% (delta +0.02) and head width:height 0.67 vs 0.69 (delta -0.02), both comfortably inside tolerance, so 3.13's face-aspect check passes and the child proportion is the turnaround's, not the proxy's. What fails is the second clause of 3.2 — 'joints read as connected forms'. The hip joint is not merely unconvincing, it is absent (see the y=421 finding). The shorts are three butt-joined boxes, a left panel, a right panel and a narrower centre gusset that sits lower and steps forward with hard ink-outlined seams down both sides; at the runtime hero camera it reads as a nappy flap, not a crotch. The sleeve hem to bare forearm is a hard step with no deltoid: the sleeve is a box and a thin tube emerges from it, so at idle and run the shoulder never rounds. In swing_contact the lead elbow reads as two cylinders meeting at a kink rather than a continuous elbow line (3.11 concern). Sock cuff to calf is a crisp constructed step, which is correct. So: proportions right, connections wrong.

hairMass.label: hair mass
hairMass.note: Measured by me, and tightening the band makes it WORSE, not better, so the default is not flattering it. Default band 5-45% of head height: delivered 0.99 strand minima/row, prominence 61.1 (81 rows) vs concept 6.16 and 19.6 (85 rows) = 16% of the concept's strand count at 312% of its prominence. I re-ran at 5-30%, which is pure crown well above the hairline (delivered brows sit at ~46% of head height, so the default does graze them): 0.53 vs 5.50 minima/row = 10% of concept count at 171% prominence. Honest number: 10-16%, i.e. a smooth faceted blob with a handful of very deep facet creases and no strand grouping whatever. Rubric 3.3 caps a featureless blob at 4; this one cannot reach 4 because the silhouette half fails too. (a) The signature is a HIGH SIDE PONYTAIL and from the front it is a centred top-knot: a hexagonal prism butt-joined to a dome with a visible ledge ring at the join. (b) From behind, cap and tail are one mass, so at the batting camera the ponytail does not exist. (c) HAIR SWALLOWS THE FACE. The turnaround keeps a full forehead of roughly one eye-height between brow and hairline; the delivered hairline is a hard horizontal edge sitting directly ON the eyebrows, and in rocket-rosa-runtime-face-angry.png the raised inner brow is partly overlapped by the hair mass. There is no forehead on this kid at any angle. (d) The profile crown is one flat polygon plane with hard unsmoothed facet boundaries.

clothingConstruction.label: clothing construction
clothingConstruction.note: Genuinely mixed, and the shoes are the best thing on the asset. Cropped at 8x, each sneaker has a cream midsole with a distinct darker outsole strip under it, a navy upper, a cream toe cap, three crisp cream stripes and a dark lace stroke — that is a constructed shoe, not a primitive volume, and my measure:fidelity run confirms the colour split is right (shoe dominant tone 67.4 vs concept 70.0, second tone 32.6 vs 28.6, band saturation 16.1 vs 19.7, all ok). The collar piping and sleeve piping are crisp loft-ring edges, not smears, and the sock cuff is a hard constructed edge. AGAINST that: the shorts are the worst-constructed garment on any board I have looked at — three butt-joined boxes with a see-through notch above the centre gusset, no waistband, no hem roll, and a gusset panel that reads at hero scale as a separate rectangular flap. The tee is a hard-cornered slab with a flat disc bottom and no hem at all, and it does not reach the shorts. ON THE PAINTED-VS-CONSTRUCTED QUESTION: mostly constructed edges (piping, stripes, sock cuff, shirt/shorts volumes are separate lofts), but two are painted gradients — the shoe's cream toe cap blends into the navy through a soft mottled blur with a raised bubble artefact in the middle of the cream, and the midsole/upper boundary is equally cloudy. The lace is a painted stroke, not geometry. TEAM_MASK EXTENT (judging extent, not colour, per the brief): the scrunchie is a ~40x8px orange sliver on the tail in the profile board plus a detached 3-4px orange island beside it, invisible from the front and invisible at 40px in all three views. That is too little accent surface for either team palette to read in game (2.4).

faceExpressionRead.label: face/expression read
faceExpressionRead.note: The four runtime-face stills are the asset's real strength and I checked them for the empty-file trap first: grin 285439, cheer 283363, tongue 283495, angry 283961 bytes — all within 1% of each other, none near the ~29% tell, and all four are visually distinct when cropped and tiled. 3.14 passes cleanly and is not close: grin is a closed smile with a teeth band, cheer opens to an upper teeth row over a dark red interior, tongue shows a real pink tongue below the teeth, angry is a down-turned frown with a modelled lower lip and inward-angled brows. That reads at draft-card distance. My measure:fidelity run also clears 6b.3: visible face left 49.3% vs concept 43.8%, right 47.9% vs 44.4%, asymmetry 1.43 — all ok, and 3.13's aspect ratio passes (0.67 vs 0.69). The nose is NOT absent — nose_push is in the sculpt script and the profile crop confirms geometry breaking the silhouette — but it breaks it as a sharp beak point rather than the sheet's soft button, and under the board's flat front light it produces no shading break at all, so the front board view reads as a noseless face. The near-side eye reading as a foreshortened grey sliver in the profile is EXPECTED at a true 90-degree ortho and I am not counting it. What holds this to 3 is 3.5's own 5-clause and the hero evidence: cropped at 6x from rocket-rosa-runtime-hero.png there is a hard, ink-outlined, dotted decal-island seam running down the face from the brow through the cheek where the flat face plane meets the skull, catching visibly different light on each side. 3.5 bars exactly that. Add the swallowed forehead, flat parallelogram brows and a skull with no cheekbone, jaw or chin plane, and the face is a sticker on an egg that happens to animate well.

heroAndFieldScale.label: hero and field scale
heroAndFieldScale.note: Split result. The hero 3/4 (rocket-rosa-runtime-hero.png) reads well — the ponytail is clearly a ponytail, the face lands, the white/navy/orange colours all separate against grass and dirt, the review page reports 'model model' (4.1 satisfied) at 27.7k tris, and run reads as a genuinely energetic sprint with clear daylight between the legs. I built my own 40px strip from the hero, front board and profile board and upscaled it: from PROFILE and 3/4 the tail mass survives and she reads as a girl with hair. From the FRONT she does not. At 40px front-on the top-knot collapses to an unreadable nub, the ears become the dominant shape, and she reads as a short-haired boy in a white tee — the same read as half the roster, with zero trace of the one thing that makes her Rocket. No orange is visible at 40px in any of the three views. Since the draft card portrait and the pitcher's on-screen presentation are both front-facing, that is a real 3.6/3.9 miss, not a technicality. One more motion note: the ponytail hangs dead vertical through the whole run cycle with no trail or whip, which for the character literally named Rocket is a wasted signature.

frontProfileSilhouette.label: front/profile silhouette
frontProfileSilhouette.note: Recognisable without colour (spiky crest + round glasses + overalls), but the front board misses his own sheet at both denim stations and the profile has no face in it. I re-derived the px/rig-unit scale from each image independently (delivered figure y73-647 = 575px over 3.99 units = 144.1 px/unit; concept front figure y121-810 = 690px = 172.9 px/unit) and validated it against the sheet: the concept's own pair-outer halves measure 0.5003 / 0.5118 / 0.5639 at z 1.10 / 0.80 / 0.46 against the declared 0.5007 / 0.5210 / 0.5673, so the ruler is good to ~2%. The DELIVERED halves at the same rig heights are 0.4025 / 0.3956 / 0.2846. That is -0.098 / -0.125 / -0.283 ft against a declared tol of 0.03 / 0.03 / 0.04 — 3.3x, 4.2x and 7x over. Yes, he is visibly spindly against his own drawing: the concept's pant leg is 86px wide per leg on a 690px figure (12.5% of figure height) and FLARES as it descends (0.500 -> 0.512 -> 0.564); the delivered leg is 57px on a 575px figure (9.9%) and TAPERS (0.403 -> 0.396). The direction of the silhouette is inverted — cricket's slim tapered pipe where the sheet draws a baggy denim column, and cropped at 4x side by side the difference reads immediately as a different, thinner kid. Compounding it, the pant hem lands mid-shin: measured on the front board the leg necks from 53px to 27px between y560 and y570 (-49% in 5 rows) and holds a bare 27-29px cream sock column for 34 rows (5.9% of figure height) before the shoe starts at y600. The concept never necks at all — 81, 81, 87, 82, 67px per leg from y700 straight into the sole. Profile is worse: scanning the frontmost foreground column row by row, the head's leading contour is x=217 CONSTANT from y192 to y246 (55px, 27% of head height) — that is the lens ring seen edge-on as a dead-flat vertical plate — and the skin behind it is x=223 constant from y190 to y245. There is no forward bulge anywhere: the nose does not break the profile. The back of the hair is a chain of straight chords with hard corners at 6x (crown-to-nape faceting), not an organic transition. No holes or open interiors found in either silhouette (3.7 passes).

headBodyProportions.label: head/body proportions
headBodyProportions.note: The head itself is right and I am not arguing with the numbers: measure:fidelity gives head height 35.5% of figure vs the concept's 36.9% (delta -1.42, ok) and head w:h 0.84 vs 0.86 (delta -0.02, ok), so 3.13 passes and he is not a bobblehead. What fails is the second half of the criterion — joints reading as connected forms — and the limb mass relative to the trunk. The legs are 20-24% under their own sheet (see silhouette note) while the torso is only ~9% under it (delivered denim body half ~0.392 at z 1.40 against the script's own traced 0.43), so the mass distribution is wrong in a way no single AUTO metric catches: a comparatively boxy trunk on thin pipes. At the ankle the connection is not a form at all, it is a 49% diameter step in 5 pixels from cuff lip to sock. At the shoulder, cropping gizmo-runtime-swing.png at (380,330,260x200) 4x shows the near deltoid as a discrete pale-blue BALL with its own outline, butt-joined to an orange cylinder upper arm — a doll ball-joint, not a deltoid rolling into the arm (3.11 EYES). The forearms are uniform tapered tubes with no elbow mass in either the A-pose board or the swing still. The crotch yoke does close (no gap) and the neck-to-shoulder junction is fine.

hairMass.label: hair mass
hairMass.note: Measured with measure:strands at three bands, because the default 5-45% reaches onto his forehead — the delivered forehead skin starts at ~40% of head height and the concept's at ~36%, so 5-45% counts brow and skin edges as false creases. Tightening it does not rescue him: 5-45% -> 18% of the concept's strand count at 299% of its prominence; 5-35% -> 23% at 347%; 8-30% -> 26% at 375%. The band choice moves the number by 8 points and the verdict not at all. What the crops show is exactly what those numbers describe: a SMOOTH, featureless dome carrying five isolated cone spikes along the crown ridge. The prominence is 3.5x over because the only creases present are the deep slots between those cones; everywhere else the mass is undifferentiated. The concept (c-head crop at 4x) is a tousled swept mop — a dozen overlapping locks, a fringe curving down across the forehead and past the temples, and a broken outline all round. The delivered fringe is an unbroken smooth helmet edge and the crest reads as a stegosaurus plate row rather than bed-head. Silhouette-wise this is not the same hairstyle from the front, and rubric 3.3 caps a smooth featureless mass at 4 before the shape error is even counted. It does cover the skull from every angle (no bare-skull read) and the hairline is legible from the front, which is why it is not a 1. The back of the mass is additionally faceted (p-hairback crop at 6x: five or six straight chords with visible corners).

clothingConstruction.label: clothing construction
clothingConstruction.note: There is real construction here and I want to credit it: the bib and straps are proud geometry rather than a colour wedge, the rolled cuff is a separate proud band with a dark underside lip, the tee has sleeve caps, the chest pocket is a raised patch, and the shoe has a sole ledge, a vamp panel and three lace stripes. That is a 4-shaped garment set. It is dragged down by one error that changes what he is wearing: the hem lands mid-shin. Measured on gizmo-front-review.png the pant/cuff column is 53px wide at y560, 27px at y590, and the shoe does not begin until y600 — a 34-row bare cream sock column, 5.9% of figure height, on both legs. The concept (c-legs crop at 4x) has ZERO exposed ankle: the rolled cuff sits directly on the sneaker collar and flares WIDER than the leg above it, and the per-leg width never falls below 67px between hem and sole. On the board and in gizmo-runtime-run.png the exposed socks read as bright white leg-warmers and are the first thing the eye lands on below the waist. Second: the shoe drops the concept's construction — the drawing has cream laces through visible eyelets, a cream toe cap, a striped sole band and a side button; the delivered shoe has painted stripes and no eyelets, laces or toe cap. I am NOT scoring the shoe's colour split, because measure:fidelity covers it and passes it (dominant tone 82.1 vs 84.6, second tone 17.9 vs 13.1, saturation 19.5 vs 21.7, all ok) and my own crude blue/cream classifier over the shoe bboxes was not trustworthy enough to override a passing detector. Third, unauthored: a strong vertical light-to-dark gradient runs down the denim (near-white at the bib top to navy at the hips) that the concept, which is uniform mid-denim with faint knee fading, does not have — it makes bib and pants read as two different garments. The chest TEAM_MASK patch is judged on extent only, and its extent is fine (a bib-pocket-sized rectangle, matching where the concept's pocket sits).

faceExpressionRead.label: face/expression read
faceExpressionRead.note: This is the one that should stop the character, and it is not a colour complaint — it is a geometry one. BOTH LENSES ARE OPAQUE. build_glasses authors a filled LENS disc (#E8EFEA) at plane_y + 0.012, i.e. 0.012 in FRONT of the ring plane, and it completely occludes the eye sockets and the face atlas's eye cells. Measured over the lens interiors: delivered left sd(luma) 18.3 with 25 distinct 16-level tone buckets, right sd 30.3 with 19 buckets; the concept's same regions are sd 65.5 with 133 buckets and sd 75.8 with 143. The concept has white sclera, a brown iris, a black pupil and a specular dot in each lens (c-head at 4x, f-lensbox at 10x); the delivered has flat grey. He has no eyes in the front board, no eyes in the hero still, and no eyes in ANY of the four runtime expression frames. I checked all four: grin, cheer, tongue and angry differ ONLY in the mouth cell — the mouth channel genuinely works (grin shows a tooth row, tongue opens with a pink tongue, so 3.14's mouth half passes), but half the expression channel is simply not rendered, at every angle and in every clip. Second defect at the same place: the rings collide. Measured centre-to-centre spacing is 60px on a 63.5px outer ring diameter (0.95 diameters); the concept's is 83.75px on 61px (1.37 diameters), so the rings sit ~30% too close and their rims MERGE — at the eye midline (y217-222) a single shared 5px dark run at x268-272 serves as both the left ring's inner rim and the right ring's inner rim. The authored bridge tube spans x -0.013 to +0.013 and is entirely buried inside that merge, so there is no bridge and no daylight: it reads as a figure-8 goggle, not as two round spectacles joined by a bar. Verifying the known glasses checks: frames ARE two cyclic wire tubes at 0.030 proud of the cheek (correct, not 0.050, and no see-through profile pocket); frames ARE on material index 2 (M_Hair) NOT slot 3, so they are not team-tinted — the blue-grey edge on them in the runtime stills is the scene's navy toon outline, visible identically on the shoulder, arm and shoe, and is a false finding I am explicitly not filing. The eye-landmark refusal is expected and fine. The temple arms DO bow outboard (0.357 -> 0.450 -> 0.485) but they do NOT reach the ear root: cropping (248,212,48x40) at 16x, the arm stops with a blunt cut end on the CHEEK forward of the ear, and a separate dark chip re-emerges INSIDE the ear's concha — the arm is buried through the ear rather than hooking over it. The ear itself (3.10) is constructed — outer rim, inner hollow — but it is a pointed crescent with a sharp tip at BOTH ends and no lobe; it reads as a fin. The concept's ear (c-profile at 6x) is a full shell with helix, concha, tragus and a rounded fleshy lobe, plainly traceable in the profile view, which contradicts the script's 'ears hide behind the mop, not-traceable' provenance comment. Finally, no nose: the profile skin contour is x=223 constant from y190 to y245, so nothing breaks the silhouette — rubric 3.5's 5/5 explicitly wants a real nose to break the profile, and here there is not even a bump. Rim thickness is 4px on a 52px ring vs the concept's 3px on 61px scale-corrected to 2.5px, so the wire is ~1.6x too fat as well. Score 1: features are not legible at hero scale because half of them are painted over.

heroAndFieldScale.label: hero and field scale
heroAndFieldScale.note: The one category he genuinely earns. I built the 40px read myself by extracting the figure box (y73-647) from gizmo-front-review.png and resampling to 40px tall, then nearest-upscaling to look at it: the brown crest, the two big dark rings, the blue overall column and the cream shoes survive cleanly and he is unmistakably Gizmo at that size — nobody else on the roster has that spiky-crest-plus-round-goggles pair. The board's own 40px strip agrees. 3.9 passes convincingly. The hero end is where it splits: at close-up the opaque lenses invert the identity. The concept's hook is a curious kid with enormous warm brown eyes behind clear glass; the delivered hero still is a kid with two blank white discs for a face, which reads as swim goggles or a welding mask and is faintly unsettling on a draft card. The bare white shins are also the loudest thing on the figure at mid-distance in the run still. So: field scale 4-5, hero scale 1-2, and 3 is the honest average of a read that works at 40px precisely BECAUSE the thing that ruins it at 400px (two big blank circles) is a strong low-frequency shape.
