polishFindings: BLOCKER — the lenses are opaque and the eyes are never visible. build_glasses fills each ring with a solid LENS (#E8EFEA) disc at plane_y + 0.012, i.e. IN FRONT of the ring plane, which paints over the face atlas's eye cells in every view and every clip (measured: lens interior sd(luma) 18.3/30.3 and 25/19 distinct tone buckets vs the concept's 65.5/75.8 and 133/143). The script's own comment defends this as 'what the drawing shows' — the drawing shows clear glass over huge brown eyes with a small crescent highlight. Fix: either delete the disc entirely and let the atlas eyes read through an open wire ring, or shrink it to a crescent highlight occupying the upper-outer ~20% of each lens. Whatever the isSkin detector scores, a kid with no eyes cannot ship.

BLOCKER — the two lens rings collide and there is no bridge. GLASSES_LENS_X 0.180 with GLASSES_RADIUS 0.177 leaves 0.006 between the ring centrelines' inner edges, so the two 0.022 wire tubes overlap: at the eye midline one shared 5px dark run serves as both inner rims and the authored bridge tube (x -0.013 to +0.013) is entirely buried inside it. Measured centre spacing 0.95 lens diameters against the concept's 1.37. Push GLASSES_LENS_X out to about 0.24 (or pull GLASSES_RADIUS in) so a real bridge bar and a strip of nose skin show between the rings, as they do on the sheet.

The legs are cricket's, and it is measurable on the board, not just in the source: delivered pair-outer halfWidths 0.4025 / 0.3956 at z 1.10 / 0.80 against gizmo's own sheet's 0.5007 / 0.5210 (tol 0.03) — 3.3x and 4.2x over tolerance, 20% and 24% narrow. The taper direction is also inverted: the sheet flares toward the cuff, the shipped table tapers. Re-solve LEG_STATIONS from gizmo's provenance rows and delete the copied comment block that quotes cricket's pixel runs ('denim 134-204 at z 1.10'), which is what let the transplant survive review.

The pant hem lands mid-shin and exposes a bare sock column the concept does not have: 34 rows tall (5.9% of figure height) with a -49% diameter step in 5 rows, on both legs, glaring in the run still as white leg-warmers. Drop the CUFF stations (0.740/0.640) and the PANTS_DARK lip (0.600) down so the cuff underside meets the shoe collar near z 0.50, and widen the cuff so it flares past the leg above it as the drawing does.

The hair is a smooth dome plus five isolated cones: 23-26% of the concept's strand count at 347-375% of its prominence, band-independent. The creases that exist are far too deep and there are four times too few of them, which is the roster-wide Nyquist finding. Trade crown ROWS for COLUMNS in build_hair at constant triangle cost (the grizz trade) and, more importantly, replace the party-hat cone crest with grouped swept LOCKS carrying a fringe across the forehead — the current crest reads as a different hairstyle from the front, not merely a simplified one.

The ear is a pointed crescent with a sharp tip at both ends and no lobe, and the temple arm dies on the cheek forward of it, re-emerging as a dark chip inside the concha (crop (248,212,48x40) at 16x). The concept's profile shows a full shell with helix, concha, tragus and a rounded lobe, plainly traceable — so the EAR_SPEC provenance comment 'his ears hide behind the mop and the temple arms / not-traceable' is wrong and should be re-derived off the profile view. Extend the temple arm's last station up and back to the ear ROOT (z near 3.06, y past the ear's rear) so it hooks over the helix instead of through it.

No nose in the profile: the skin contour is x=223 constant from y190 to y245 and never bulges forward. nose_push builds a 0.086 tip but the glasses plate sits 0.030 proud of the same face and the tip does not clear it. Increase the tip reach or move the lens plane back so the nose is the frontmost point of the head between the lenses, which is what 3.5's 5/5 asks for.

The shoulder reads as a detached ball-joint in swing: a discrete pale-blue sphere with its own outline butt-joined to a plain orange cylinder (crop (380,330,260x200) of gizmo-runtime-swing.png at 4x). 3.11 EYES fails. Blend the tee sleeve cap into the upper arm so the deltoid rolls into the limb instead of capping it.

The back of the hair mass is visibly faceted — five or six straight chords with hard corners from crown to nape at 6x. That is 3.1's 'butt-joined primitives' read and it is visible at 1x on the profile board. More columns in the nape rings, or a smoothed shading normal, would settle it.

An unauthored vertical light-to-dark gradient runs the length of the denim (near-white at the bib top to navy at the hips) that the concept does not have; it makes bib and pants read as two garments. Worth checking whether it is vertex colour or the review-page lighting before touching the palette.

The shoe drops the concept's construction: no eyelets, no laces as geometry, no cream toe cap, no striped sole band, no side button. measure:fidelity's shoe-band colour metrics all pass, so this is a geometry note only and I did not score the colour split on it.

NOT A DEFECT, recorded so nobody re-files it: the blue-grey edge on the frames in the runtime stills is the scene's navy toon outline (identical on shoulder, forearm and shoe), not a team tint — build_glasses correctly uses material index 2 (M_Hair), never slot 3. Frames are two cyclic wire tubes at 0.030 proud, temple arms do bow outboard, the eye-landmark refusal is expected, and 3.12 leg daylight passes at 34.1% vs 27.9%.

The recorded 4/4/4/4/4/4 on the board is not defensible on this evidence and should be replaced. Every category re-scores at or below 3, and faceExpressionRead is a 1 for a reason no reviewer can miss once they crop the eyes at 10x.

frontProfileSilhouette.label: front/profile silhouette
frontProfileSilhouette.note: He is THE CAP-OVER-CURLS KID by his own script header, and neither half of that reads. The cap's bill contributes ZERO pixels to the front outline: I read the geometry out of sculpt-dex-source.py myself — brim max half-width 0.340 against a crown half-width of 0.4934 at the brim's own z (interpolated from CAP_LEVELS at BRIM_Z_TOP=3.575), so the bill is 69% of the crown and lives entirely inside it. On the runtime grin still at 5x the bill is a 2-3px bright line under the dome that reads as a specular highlight; he is wearing a beanie. In profile the bill is a razor blade: 0.035ft thick over a 0.320ft reach, and the top surface drops 0.010ft across that reach = 1.8 degrees of droop, against a concept bill that is a thick, deeply curved, tapered form arcing down over the brow (cropped both at 4x-5x, /tmp/c_cap_prof.png vs /tmp/d_cap_prof.png). Second silhouette loss: the concept profile's single largest garment shape is a big DRAPED HOOD swelling behind the neck and covering the upper back — build_hoodie_details does author one, but at 5x on the delivered profile (/tmp/d_hood.png) the back of the neck runs straight into a smooth narrow collar cone with no roll at all, and my back-edge measurement against a mid-torso datum has the concept projecting +0.138ft at z=2.90 and +0.078ft at z=2.80 where the delivered gives +0.078 and -0.023. Third: the hair mass balloons WIDER than the cap it is supposed to sit under, so the head reads as a small hat perched on two earmuff lobes. Torso is a smooth trapezoidal slab; the hoodie hem is a flat horizontal shelf with two jean cylinders butt-jointed under it. Strip the colour and this is 'a kid in a hat', not Dex.

headBodyProportions.label: head/body proportions
headBodyProportions.note: The measured half is genuinely fine and I am not going to argue with it: `npm run measure:fidelity -- dex` gives head height 32.6% of figure against the concept's 33.7% (delta -1.10, ok) and head width:height 1.00 against 0.96 (delta +0.04, ok), so 3.13 passes and this is a child, not the proxy. What fails is the second clause — 'joints read as connected forms'. Every junction on him is a butt joint between primitives. The shoulders are square corners where a sleeve tube meets a flat torso plane (visible in the runtime hero and swing stills, and in the front board at 4x): no deltoid, no round mass, the arm just starts. The elbow has no form at all — in the run still the near arm is one unbroken straight cylinder from shoulder to hand. The neck is a bare skin cylinder plugged into a collar cone with a visible ring seam. The hoodie hem is a flat shelf and the thighs emerge from under it as separate tubes with a hard-edged cast shadow (/tmp/d_zip.png at 12x shows the shelf and the step). Proportion 4, construction 2, and the category asks for both, so 3.

hairMass.label: hair mass
hairMass.note: `npm run measure:strands -- dex` at the tool's only working band (default 5-45% of head height; I tried --band 15-40 / 20-45 / 10-35 and all three return 0 rows, so the flag is not supported and 5-45% is the number I have): concept 7.09 strand minima per row at mean prominence 16.2 over 94 rows, delivered 2.18 at 18.9 over 73 rows — he carries 31% of the concept's strand count. I take the band caveat seriously, but the crops settle it independently of any detector: at 5x (/tmp/d_cap.png, /tmp/r_head.png) and on the swing still the hair is ONE smooth glossy blob with a single broad specular sweep and not a single clump boundary anywhere, while the concept at the same 4x (/tmp/c_cap.png) is roughly thirty discrete ringlets each with its own rim light. CURL_LEVELS is a clump-modulated ring band in the source and the modulation is not surviving to the render. Rubric 3.3 says a smooth featureless blob caps at 4 'however correct its silhouette' — and here the silhouette is wrong too: the mass sits as two round lobes at ear height with almost nothing above, reading as earmuffs or headphones rather than a curl ball, and it swells wider than the cap. The hairline is a hard painted contour cutting a deep M into a large bare forehead, which reads as a receding hairline rather than the concept's curls dropping to the brow, and both brows run straight into the hair mass with no skin gap on either side. Blob plus wrong mass shape plus a bad hairline is a 2.

clothingConstruction.label: clothing construction
clothingConstruction.note: The hood, the pocket, the zip and the ribbing all have builders (I grepped build_hoodie_details before writing a word of this) and none of them read. The draped hood is invisible in the delivered profile — see the silhouette note for the numbers. The kangaroo pocket is two FLAT RECTANGULAR PLATES with hard 90-degree corners butt-joined to the torso; in the A-pose profile one of them sticks out from the hip as a bare slab with a visible gap under its edge, against a concept pocket that is a soft welted pouch with curved openings sweeping inward. The zipper is a flat cream stripe with no pull tab and no teeth (concept: a moulded metal zip with a pull). The ribbed hem is a ~2px dark line, not the thick vertically-ribbed band that occupies about a tenth of the concept figure; the ribbed sleeve cuffs are authored as SHIRT_DARK but do not read at any scale. The jeans have no fly seam, no gold topstitch, no yoke pockets, no belt line. The rolled cuff IS present and is the right height, but it is badly overcooked: I column-scanned both figures and the concept's cuff/thigh luminance ratio is 102/58 = 1.71 while the delivered is 148/52 = 2.85, so it renders 67% higher-contrast and reads as a white sock cuff rather than pale rolled denim (authored CUFF #96A4BA against a sheet cuff I sampled at #5F6670). Same class of drift on the body: delivered hoodie chest L=98.6 against the concept's L=57.2 — 1.72x too light — and this is not a lighting difference, because the jean thigh matches at 52.0 vs 54.4 (0.96x) under the same two renders. The authored SHIRT swatch is #5C6577 while dex.spec.json's own traced hoodie cluster is #4C5563 at toneDistance 0. The shoes are the one honestly constructed garment on him: cream cupsole, toe bumper and laces all read at hero and even survive to the run still.

faceExpressionRead.label: face/expression read
faceExpressionRead.note: 3.14 passes and I want that on the record: across the four runtime stills the grin opens with teeth, the tongue cell opens with a red tongue, cheer and angry both change the mouth shape, and all of it survives at draft-card distance — no stroke collapsing to a line. Measured face visibility is also fine: 24.7% of head width per side against a concept 20.5/22.8, left/right asymmetry 0.00. What holds it at 3 is that the face is a sticker, not a form. There is no nose. In the front board and the grin still the nose is a faint smudge of shading with no volume, and in the 3/4 runtime hero at 5x (/tmp/r_hero_head.png) the brow-to-lip contour is one smooth unbroken curve — the nose does not break the profile anywhere, which is exactly the failure 3.5 names. nose_push exists in the source and is doing almost nothing. There is a visible tonal seam where the face plane meets the cheek, so the features read as a decal island rather than integrated with the skull's planes. The brows are two flat black wedges that merge directly into the hair on both sides with no skin gap, so they read as part of the hairline. Legible: yes. A form: no.

heroAndFieldScale.label: hero and field scale
heroAndFieldScale.note: Both ends fail. At 40px on the board's zoom strip he is a dark cap over a dark blob over a grey body — the pale cuffs are about 2px, the team badge about 1px, the curls are one silhouette lump, and nothing on him separates from any other dark-capped kid in the roster. His one memorable read in the concept is curls bursting out from under a curved bill; the curls have no clumps and the bill has no silhouette, so 3.9 has nothing left to show. At hero the failures are the loud ones: the bill is a razor blade sticking sideways out of a smooth dome, the face is a flat orange plate with a sticker on it and no nose, the shoulders are square corners, and the hoodie is a featureless windbreaker. On 3.11 specifically — run and swing both show the arm as one straight rigid cylinder from a corner shoulder to the hand with no deltoid mass and no elbow break, which is the 'stiff hinged cylinder' read the item exists to catch.

measuredFidelity.result:
TOOLS I RAN. `npm run measure:fidelity -- dex`: head height 33.7 concept / 32.6 delivered (-1.10, ok); head width:height 0.96 / 1.00 (+0.04, ok); shoe band dominant tone 47.7 / 51.7 (+3.91, ok); shoe band second tone 49.9 / 48.3 (-1.53, ok); shoe band mean saturation 24.9 / 21.1 (-3.79, ok); visible face left of centre 20.5 / 24.7 (+4.19, ok); visible face right of centre 22.8 / 24.7 (+1.96, ok); face left/right asymmetry 0.00 / 0.00 (ok); daylight between the ankles 0.00 / 14.3 (+14.3, OFF against tol 12) — 1 of 9 outside tolerance. `npm run measure:strands -- dex`, BAND 5-45% of head height (the default and the only one that works — I tried --band 15-40, --band 20-45 and --band 10-35 and every one returns '0.00 strand minima/row (0 rows)' for both figures, so the flag is not implemented): concept 7.09 minima/row at mean prominence 16.2 over 94 rows, delivered 2.18 at 18.9 over 73 rows => 31% of the concept's strand count at 116% of its prominence. I accept the caveat that 5-45% can reach onto forehead and brow edges, but the same band is applied to both figures and the 4x crops agree with the direction.

LEG-TABLE PROVENANCE, verified independently as asked. sculpt-dex-source.py's LEG_STATIONS (lines 518-532) is BYTE-IDENTICAL to sculpt-lefty-source.py's (lines 531-545) — `diff` of the two extracted blocks returns nothing, comments included. sculpt-sniffles-source.py carries the same thirteen rows differing only in two colour tokens (CUFF->TEAM_MASK). Hashing the block across all 27 scripts that define one: dex and lefty share a hash exactly; clover/peaches share one; cricket/gizmo share one. The `# measured:` lines above the identical tables disagree — dex 0.6167 at z=1.25 and 0.4467 at z=0.80, lefty 0.4441 and 0.5136 — i.e. dex's provenance says the legs taper downward and lefty's says they flare, which one table cannot do.

SO I MEASURED BOTH SHEETS MYSELF, off each spec's own front box and ftPerPx (dex box [89,315,146,839] ftpp 0.005764; lefty box [73,284,177,838] ftpp 0.006042), taking the two widest silhouette runs per row as the legs and comparing mean per-leg half-width against the shared table interpolated at the same z:
  z=1.20  dex sheet 0.2032 vs table 0.1915 = +6.1%   | lefty sheet 0.1873 vs 0.1915 = -2.2%
  z=1.10  dex 0.1974 vs 0.1882 = +4.9%              | lefty 0.1813 vs 0.1882 = -3.7%
  z=1.00  dex 0.1917 vs 0.1847 = +3.8%              | lefty 0.1873 vs 0.1847 = +1.4%
  z=0.90  dex 0.1888 vs 0.1817 = +3.9%              | lefty 0.1707 vs 0.1817 = -6.1%
  z=0.80  dex 0.1888 vs 0.1794 = +5.2%              | lefty 0.1813 vs 0.1794 = +1.0%
  z=0.70  dex 0.1888 vs 0.1780 = +6.1%              | lefty 0.1782 vs 0.1780 = +0.1%
  MEAN ABSOLUTE ERROR: dex 5.0% ALL ONE SIGN (systematic, the table is uniformly too thin for him); lefty 2.4% with the sign alternating (noise around a fit).
The shared comment 'per-leg halves come from the central jeans runs (139-268 at z 1.40 across both)' matches NEITHER sheet: dex at z=1.40 is a single merged run [91,271]; lefty at z=1.40 is [107,174],[182,258]. And dex's own recorded 0.6167 at z=1.25 is not a leg measurement at all — his front figure at that row has four runs, [93,113] and [289,309] being the HANDS, so the number is the arm-inclusive span; the legs there are [122,199],[204,280].
PLAIN ANSWER: Dex's legs are NOT traced from his drawing. The table fits Lefty's front figure and misses Dex's by a uniform ~5% at every station below the hip, the pixel-run comment traces to neither sheet, and Dex's recorded provenance number measures his arms.

CAP GEOMETRY, read out of sculpt-dex-source.py and computed by me. Brim half-widths 0.340 (root) / 0.320 / 0.255 (tip); crown half-width at BRIM_Z_TOP=3.575, interpolated between CAP_LEVELS (3.620, 0.485) and (3.540, 0.500), is 0.4934. Brim/crown = 0.689, so the bill is entirely inside the crown's own half-width and contributes ZERO pixels to the front silhouette — confirming the still-open finding. Brim reach 0.320ft forward of the dome front; slab thickness 0.035ft; top-surface drop 0.010ft over the reach = 1.8 degrees of droop. It is a flat blade — confirming the second still-open finding.

LUMINANCE, sampled by column scan (Rec.709 luma) on the concept front figure and dex-front-review.png. Jean thigh: concept 58, delivered 52 (0.90x — the two renders are comparably lit). Rolled cuff: concept peak 106 / mean 99, delivered 156/150/139 mean 148. Cuff-to-thigh contrast ratio concept 1.71, delivered 2.85 = +67% — the cuff renders far lighter than the concept's, confirming the third still-open finding. Hoodie chest: concept L=57.2, delivered L=98.6 = 1.72x too light; authored SHIRT swatch #5C6577 vs dex.spec.json's traced hoodie cluster #4C5563 (toneDistance 0). Hoodie pocket: concept 66.8 (+9.6 over chest), delivered 102.6 (+4.0 over chest).

HOOD PROJECTION, profile back-edge measured against a mid-torso datum (mean of z=2.00..2.20): z=2.90 concept +0.138ft, delivered +0.078ft; z=2.80 concept +0.078ft, delivered -0.023ft. Rows below z=2.75 are contaminated by the A-pose arm blob so I discard them.

CAP SILHOUETTE ROW SCAN. Concept front, crown widens monotonically 12px (y=146) to 181px (y=230) then steps to 195/212/215px at y=236/242/248 — I checked the 4x crop and that step is the CURLS emerging, not the bill, so I am NOT claiming the concept's bill flares beyond the crown. Delivered front, top row 90, max width 182px at y=186-192 then narrowing — no bill step anywhere.

RETRACTED, because I cropped it. I first read a cream line running from the hoodie collar down through the crotch and inseam to the ankles in /tmp/d_torso.png. Scanning the centre columns x=255..285 of dex-front-review.png: the cream ZIP (L~200, rgb 202,200,196) runs y=302 to y=434 and stops at the hem; y=446-542 the brightest centre pixel is L=47-59, plain dark denim. The line below the hem is background daylight between the legs, plus specular edges on the inner leg cylinders. No zip on the jeans. Recording it so nobody re-files it.

NOT FILED. Legs (3.12) — I did not re-open it and I found nothing new; the ankle-daylight metric above is OFF in the MORE-daylight direction (14.3 delivered vs 0.00 concept, whose drawing has the feet together), which is the direction 3.12 wants, and per 6b.4 that is a stance question, never a tolerance to widen. Ears (3.10) — EAR_SPEC exists at (0.020, 3.150) radii (0.1300, 0.1600) and build_ear is called for both sides; I cropped the delivered profile ear at 8x (/tmp/d_ear.png) and it has an outer rim, an inner shadow and a lobe against the skull. Constructed. Passes. Team accent (3.7/2.3) — the TEAM_MASK panel is a badge-sized 0.105-half-width patch on the cap front, grey on the board and gold at runtime; extent is correct and I judged nothing by its colour. Holes (3.7) — none found in either board view.
measuredFidelity.note: His ear line is refused (curls and ears merge in every width metric); featurelatitude gates brow 49.0 vs traced 49.0, eye 67.6 vs 67.6, mouth 82.4 vs 82.3 through his 3.99-2.65 span. His lit skin never gets a cluster on the sheet (folded into the shadow tone) - the recipe records the refusal and the swatch is a direct cheek sample. alignOpenMouth is set: at mouthY 70 the unaligned open cells paint the under-chin (Gizmo's lesson).

polishFindings: BLOCKER, provenance: sculpt-dex-source.py's LEG_STATIONS is byte-identical to sculpt-lefty-source.py's, comments included (verified by diff; sniffles carries the same rows with two colour tokens swapped). The shared table fits LEFTY's front figure to 2.4% mean absolute error with an alternating sign, and misses DEX's by +3.8% to +6.1% at EVERY station from z=1.20 to z=0.70 — one sign, a systematic bias, his jeans are drawn ~5% too thin. BLOCKER, 3.1/3.6: the cap bill has no silhouette. SWEEP (not dex-only): the identical-leg-table defect is a class. Hashing every LEG_STATIONS block across the 27 scripts that define one finds three collision pairs — dex/lefty (identical), clover/peaches (identical), cricket/gizmo (identical). Each pair should be checked the way I checked dex: fit the shared table against BOTH sheets and see which one it was actually traced from. Better, add a lint that refuses two characters sharing a LEG_STATIONS hash, since the existing gates check spec-vs-sheet and sculpt-vs-spec but nothing checks that one kid's numbers are not another kid's.

CREDIT: the shoes are the one honestly constructed garment — cream cupsole, toe bumper and laces all read at hero and survive to the run still, and the shoe-band tone and saturation metrics are all inside tolerance. The four expression cells also genuinely work (3.14 passes): grin opens with teeth, tongue opens with a tongue, and both read at draft-card distance.

frontProfileSilhouette.label: front/profile silhouette
frontProfileSilhouette.note: The front large read survives colourless - pigtailed girl, A-line green dress, chunky hi-tops - but the forms that make it are butt-joined primitives, which is the exact 5/5 disqualifier and here it drags below 4. At 8x (front-review 300,150 100x100) each pigtail is a hard hexagonal SLAB with knife-edge corners and flat facets, not a tapered bunch; the concept's tail is a strand mass cinched by a green elastic. The profile is worse: clover-profile-review and -profile-apose-review both show a faceted BOB HELMET with a straight-line diagonal off the crown and no pigtail read at all, while the concept's profile shows a tail sweeping clearly behind the skull with a visible green tie - the delivered tails project straight sideways (+/-x) so they vanish into the head in orthographic profile. And her namesake form is gone: I measured the hem's petal amplitude at 7px over a 180px hem (3.9%) against the concept's 29px over a 205px hem (14.1%), so the petal silhouette carries 28% of the drawing's depth and reads as a plain flared cone with a ringer stripe. Limbs are straight tapered dowels against the concept's toddler chub - no calf swell, no knee. NOT a finding: the disc on the chest in clover-profile-review is the T-pose hand plus its cream cuff seen end-on in a true 90-degree orthographic profile (rubric trap 4), not a hole; and the legs are two legs with wide daylight (3.12 clean).

headBodyProportions.label: head/body proportions
headBodyProportions.note: The measured half is genuinely good and I re-took it: head height 28.8% of figure vs concept 29.9% (delta -1.04, ok) and head width:height 1.45 vs 1.45 (delta -0.00, ok), so 3.13's aspect check passes exactly and this is child proportion, not the proxy. What holds it off 4 is the rubric's second clause - 'joints read as connected forms.' The shoulder does not. In clover-front-apose-review at 14x (185,275 65x55) the sleeve's inboard-upper corner folds into a hard dark-green triangular wedge with a knife crease and a navy notch bitten out of the sleeve/torso junction, on BOTH sides. The elbow and knee are not forms at all - the arm is a smooth taper from sleeve hem to wrist and the leg is a dowel from hem to sock. Ankle daylight measured 34.0 vs concept 0.00 (OFF, tol 12): per 6b.4 that is a stance read, and the delivered stance is materially wider than the drawn feet-together pose, which changes the child read at 40px.

hairMass.label: hair mass
hairMass.note: I ran measure:strands myself on three bands and state them all. Default 5-45%: 0.97 minima/row delivered vs 10.86 concept = 9% of the concept's strand count at 254% prominence - but on this kid that band's foot lands on the brow line (delivered head 93-277, so 5-45% = rows 102-176, and her brows sit at y~172-175 from my own scanline), so brow and eyelid edges are counted as FALSE creases and 9% is INFLATED. On the safe crown-and-fringe band 5-32%, which cannot reach the brows, it collapses to 0.08 minima/row vs 10.89 = 1% of the concept's count at 22% prominence; 10-40% gives 3%. That is not 'a smooth blob capped at 4' - there is essentially no strand grouping in the crown at all. Second failure, and the one the record's own note flags as legal: the hair does not separate from skin. At the fringe/forehead boundary (face-grin, x=535) hair is rgb(139,100,14) L=102 and forehead skin rgb(188,135,61) L=141 - delta L 39/255 = 15%, in the SAME hue family, both passing isSkin(r>g+12). At the hero camera the head is one undifferentiated gold-tan mass. Third: the green tie (TIE #6E7A24, authored as TIE_SPINE/TIE_RADII, so it exists - I grepped) is not visible in clover-front-review, -front-apose-review, -runtime-hero, -run or -swing; her one hair accent never reaches the player. Fourth: the crown carries 5-6 large flat polygon facets with hard shading breaks at hero scale.

clothingConstruction.label: clothing construction
clothingConstruction.note: Some things do read as constructed: cream ringer collar, cream sleeve trim rolls, socks, and green hi-tops with a cream toe cap and cupsole. But the two signature constructions are both under-built. (1) The petal hem is present as geometry - I grepped build_petal_hem before saying anything - yet I measured its bottom-edge amplitude at 7px over 180px of hem (3.9%) against the concept's 29px over 205px (14.1%): 28% of the drawn scallop. Above it the 'petal stitch' is a DEAD-STRAIGHT horizontal cream ringer band at constant z (STITCH_RING 1.235-1.275), where the concept runs the topstitch around each petal's own outline; and the concept's gold topstitch SWIRL seam sweeping the bodice from shoulder to hem is entirely absent. (2) The sneaker: the concept has threaded cream laces crossing through eyelets, a padded tongue, a padded ankle collar and a dark foxing stripe on the cupsole; the delivered shoe has three parallel PAINTED white strokes, no eyelets, no tongue, no collar, no foxing. Code-level contradiction worth fixing at source: build_petal_hem uses cos(6*theta) and its own docstring insists on an EVEN count because 'five does not survive theta->pi-theta - the Penny/Clover mirror lessons', while dress_color right below it shades the skirt with sin(2.5*theta) and its comment says 'Five petal scallops'. The painted scallops are therefore at a different count AND a non-mirror-safe phase from the sculpted dips, so shading and geometry do not line up and the two sides of the skirt are not mirror-consistent. Measured shoe split is fine: dominant tone 33.5 vs 33.1 (ok), second tone 43.3 vs 50.9 (ok), band saturation 36.7 vs 35.5 (ok).

faceExpressionRead.label: face/expression read
faceExpressionRead.note: 3.14 passes on evidence, checked properly. All four -runtime-face-*.png are genuinely painted, not empty: angry 285,900 / cheer 286,363 / grin 287,929 / tongue 286,423 bytes - all within 0.7% of each other, none near the ~29% signature of a blank. Cropped at 5x they are four distinct mouths: grin a closed smile over a tooth strip, cheer an open shout with white teeth over a red interior, tongue a pink tongue sitting on the mouth line, angry a downturned closed frown. I also diffed grin against angry over the face (490,230 105x90): 745 px change, clustered in exactly two bands - rows 243-249 (two symmetric brow clusters, so the brows DO angle, the record's claim holds) and rows 285-296 (the mouth). Freckles and the hazel-green iris survive to card distance. Held to 3 because the head the face is painted on does not support it: no nose form breaks the profile (visible in both profile boards - the face is a decal on a smooth skull, which the record itself concedes), and the fringe descends to the brow so there is NO forehead and the hair curtains clamp the outer corner of both eyes with zero temple margin - on my own eye-level scanline (front-review, y=180) the hair ends at x=234 and the sclera begins at x=236. That, plus hair and skin sharing a hue, is why the hero still reads as a tan mass with one eye in it rather than a face.

heroAndFieldScale.label: hero and field scale
heroAndFieldScale.note: Split, and the hero half fails. The 40px strip on the board does keep a memorable read - a blonde bloom over a green dress, findable in a lineup - though it reads as a mushroom/bob rather than two pigtails, and at that size the hair and skin fuse into a single blonde disc with no face. The hero is the problem: at the review page's own idle camera (clover-runtime-hero, cropped 4x at 440,170) the head is one continuous gold-tan field. I sampled it - crown rgb(151,109,10), hair beside the jaw rgb(161,115,43), cheek rgb(175,129,68) - the same hue at three lightnesses, and every one of them passes isSkin, so nothing chromatic separates hair from face. On top of that the crown breaks into 5-6 large flat polygon facets with hard shading steps, and the pigtail beside the jaw is a faceted plate. Rubric 3.6 asks identity to survive BOTH reads; it survives 40px and does not survive the close-up that ships on the draft card.

frontProfileSilhouette.label: front/profile silhouette
frontProfileSilhouette.note: Boomer is THE big kid and the delivered silhouette is not a big kid. Normalising each figure to its own head-box width (concept ear span 1.153ft, delivered 1.238ft) the outer silhouette at z=0.8ft is 1.084 head-widths on the concept and 0.616 on the delivered — 57%. Raw ink at the same heights: 1.250 vs 0.655ft (52%) at 0.8ft, 1.445 vs 0.797 (55%) at 1.0ft, 1.742 vs 0.918 (53%) at 1.2ft. The belly recovers to 78% (1.353 vs 1.052 head-widths at z=2.0ft), so the torso is only modestly slimmed while the limbs are halved — the drawing's tree-trunk legs are pencils. The second identity, the mohawk, is a different FORM: the concept fan is one continuous forward-swept fin with feathered tips and no daylight in it; delivered is nine separate hard-faceted cones radiating like a stegosaurus frill with clean background between them (profile-review at 8x). Shoulders are a flat horizontal shelf with sleeve cylinders butt-joined onto it, their shaded end caps showing as dark notches inboard (front-apose at 8x) — the rubric's named 5/5 disqualifier, and here it costs more than the 5. Colourless, this silhouette reads as an average-build kid with a spiky crest, not as Boomer.

headBodyProportions.label: head/body proportions
headBodyProportions.note: Head size is broadly right and its two OFF metrics have recorded causes I am not re-litigating (34.9% of figure height against 37.3%; w:h 0.87 against 0.77; the T-pose arm band at z 2.56 blocks the instrument's centre run). The A-pose board measures 33.6%, so the head is a little small but inside a fair reading. What fails is the second half of the category — 'joints read as connected forms'. The shoulder is a flat shelf, not a deltoid: in swing_contact at 10x the sleeve cap is a separate faceted ball with a hard silhouette break against the torso cone. The elbow (swing_contact, 5x) is a hinge between two straight tubes with no elbow volume and a visible crease facet. The knees have no form at all — the legs are smooth tapered cylinders from shorts hem to sock. And the limb-mass gap above (52-57% of the concept) sits against a nearly correct head, which is exactly the proportion error that makes him read as a normal kid with a slightly big head instead of the drawing's low, wide, heavy child. The neck is also longer and thinner than the concept's near-absent neck.

hairMass.label: hair mass
hairMass.note: Strands, my own runs: default 5-45% band gives 89% of the concept's minima count at 305% of its prominence. I re-ran on a tightened 5-25% band, chosen to stay off the forehead and brows where skin/hair and brow edges register as FALSE creases — 103% count, 224% prominence (2-30%: 91%/244%; 10-40%: 90%/351%). So grouping is not the shortfall; the over-deep prominence is the spike GAPS being counted as creases, which is the honest reading of a crest built from separate cones. Two real failures. (1) The shaved fade stops at the temples. The concept carries dark shaved sides from the temple down past the ear on both front and profile; delivered has a thin brown band across the forehead and bare skin below it, so from the front and from any three-quarter angle the sides of the skull are naked — 3.3's 'no bare-skull read from any gameplay angle'. Measured, hair covers 33.3% of the delivered head box against the concept's 41.5% (80%), and it is 10-18% narrower relative to head height through its lower half (width/headH at t=20/25/30% down: concept 40.4/44.5/49.4%, delivered 36.0/36.0/41.3%). (2) The stubble/skin boundary is a stair-stepped zigzag at loft-ring resolution — visible without magnification in boomer-profile-review and violently so in swing_contact, where it also carries an isolated skin-coloured island inside the dark field. That is a torn edge, not a fade line. The mohawk itself is not one designed mass, it is nine cones on a cap.

clothingConstruction.label: clothing construction
clothingConstruction.note: Real construction is present and I credit it: a cream sleeve cuff, a shorts hem, and a genuine shoe with a cream cupsole, a ground-line welt and a toe cap. Against that: no laces — the delivered shoe has one dark V notch where the concept has cream flat laces criss-crossed through eyelets over a navy tongue (12x, both); two cream side stripes that are not in the drawing at all; and a ragged, mottled toe-cap boundary against the navy. The socks are smooth tubes; the concept's crew socks are heavily ribbed with a rolled top, and none of that ribbing survived. The sleeve is a cylinder butt-joined to the shoulder shelf with its end cap visible. And the garment that IS his identity is washed out: measured over the shirt rows, concept gold rgb(235,160,46) sat 80.6% and cream rgb(251,230,192) sat 23.3%; delivered gold rgb(209,171,116) sat 44.3% and cream rgb(208,203,194) sat 6.4% — the cream stripe has gone neutral grey. Gold-to-cream luminance contrast, which is lighting-robust because both are read inside one image, is 28.3 against the concept's 63.6 — 44%. (Lighting is still a partial confound between a render and a drawing, so treat the ratio, not the absolutes.) TEAM_MASK extent on the sock roll-top looks correct; I am judging extent, not colour.

faceExpressionRead.label: face/expression read
faceExpressionRead.note: The four expression cells are the best thing on this asset and I am scoring them up: grin, cheer, tongue and angry all read at draft-card distance with real lips, an upper tooth band, a red tongue and brows that genuinely change — 3.14 passes cleanly on the fresh stills. Three things hold it under 4. (1) There is no nose from the front. nose_push exists in the sculpt source (line 122) so it is built, but head-on it produces no shading break whatever, and the face plate between the eyes and mouth is blank orange at hero zoom (cheer, 4x). In profile it is the wrong shape too: measured, the delivered face edge advances 17px — 9.0% of its 189px head height — over only ~10 rows, where the concept advances ~10px (4.1% of its 245px head) spread over ~45 rows. A soft button became a thin beak, 2.2x as proud and ~3.5x as narrow. (2) It is a sticker on a sphere: no jaw, no chin, no cheek planes, and the mouth decal's lower lip overruns the chin line onto the jaw. (3) It does not survive yaw. In the FRESH hero (idle f52) and run stills the head is turned ~60-70 degrees and the flat atlas leaves one eyebrow plus a hooked white crescent of sclera pinned to the silhouette edge, with the far eye and the entire mouth off-model. faceAsymmetry measures 0.00 both sides, so the spike/lean x offsets do sum to zero as the record requires; the visible-face-left OFF is the sheet's own 8.4 lighting split and I am not re-litigating it.

heroAndFieldScale.label: hero and field scale
heroAndFieldScale.note: Both ends fail on evidence that post-dates the model (GLB 18:44:27, stills 19:00:33-19:00:55). HERO: boomer-runtime-hero is the designated close-up and it has no readable face — the head is yawed away, and at 5x the read is a blank orange ball with one dark brow bar and a white hook of sclera jammed on the right silhouette edge, no mouth anywhere. The run still repeats it. The clip is shared, so the yaw is not Boomer's invention, but the flat face island on this skull is what fails to survive it, and this is the hero evidence on disk. What DOES survive at hero is the crest — but as a lizard frill of separate cones with a torn stubble edge under it, not as the drawing's fan. 40 PX: the mohawk collapses to a rounded dark cap, so the tall blade that is his entire silhouette memory is gone, and the shirt flattens to one pale cream mass because the delivered stripe contrast is 44% of the drawing's. At 40px he is a generic brown-haired kid in a cream shirt and navy shorts — 3.9's 'one memorable read' does not survive. Fielder-vs-grass separation is fine; that is not the problem here.

frontProfileSilhouette.label: front/profile silhouette
frontProfileSilhouette.note: Front reads acceptably and the measured head metrics are in tolerance (head 30.4% vs concept 31.0%; head w:h 1.01 vs 0.99). The profile does not. The sheet's profile is a skull-hugging high fade with a clean nasal break and a lip line; the delivered profile is a squared black helmet that overhangs the skull and cuts a hard horizontal line at the nape, and the face plane from brow to chin is nearly flat. I measured the front-edge of the profile silhouette per row: delivered brow x=214 (y188-193) to nose apex x=208 (y202-204) = 6px projection on a 168px head = 3.6% of head height; the concept's same measurement is nasal root x=816 to tip x=831 = 15px on a 183px head = 8.2%. The delivered nose projects 44% of the concept's. Worse, the 4-vs-5 discriminator (butt-joined primitives) fails outright at the shoulder: at 5x-8x the T-pose sleeve is a plain cylinder butt-joined to the torso with a hard vertical seam and a 32px-wide wedge of true background between sleeve and torso (front-review y311-312, confirmed by alpha scan and by an 8x crop of x180-360/y268-328), and the collar is a jagged sawtooth rather than a band. No row of pure background crosses the body in any of the four boards — nothing is severed.

headBodyProportions.label: head/body proportions
headBodyProportions.note: The size relationships pass by measurement (head height 30.4% of figure vs 31.0%, delta -0.62, ok; head width:height +0.01, ok). The criterion's other half — 'joints read as connected forms' — fails hard. The neck is a long exposed cylinder; the concept sets the head almost directly on the shoulders. The arm is a uniform noodle from shoulder to wrist with no deltoid ball, no elbow swell and a small flat paddle hand, against the sheet's chunky toddler forearm. The shoulder is not a form at all: it is a butt joint plus a sheared triangular flap. I read the sculpt script and the cause is in code, not in the eye — ARM_STATIONS carries rings at x=0.335 and x=0.400 (ARM_SHOULDER_X), SHOULDER_BLEND has keys {0.215, 0.300, 0.345, 0.420}, and sculptlib/arm.py:130 does `spec.shoulder_blend.get(round(x, 3))` — an exact-key lookup that returns None for 0.335 and 0.400, so both rings weight 100% to the Arm bone, while the 0.345 and 0.420 entries match no station and never fire. Two of four blend entries are dead and the two rings closest to the joint are unblended. This is the recorded ARM SHOULDER_BLEND lesson reproduced verbatim.

hairMass.label: hair mass
hairMass.note: One designed mass, no bare-skull read from any angle, and it is the wrong mass. The sheet is a tight high fade: the scalp is a finely stippled curl texture, the sides taper to skin above the ear, and the hairline is a clean sharp line high on the forehead. Delivered is a smooth featureless black shell that reads as a bowl cut — the script's own BUZZ comment records that 'two critics read the fuller shell as a bowl cut', and it still does. Numbers I took: at a 5-25% head-height band (the default 5-45% reaches down to the brows, which sit at 47.5%, so it counts brow edges as false creases) the concept carries 5.00 strand minima/row at mean prominence 10.8, the delivered 1.63 at 27.1 — 33% of the concept's strand count at 251% of its prominence, i.e. facet creases standing in for strands. At 2-30% it is 37% / 234%. And the fringe swallows the forehead: scanning the centre column, the concept's hairline sits at y275 on a head spanning 228-410 = 25.8% down, the delivered's at y159 on a head spanning 92-260 = 39.9% down (the script's BUZZ_FRINGE z=3.500 predicts 39.7%, so the scan is right). With brows at 47.0-47.5% in both, the concept's forehead is 21.7% of head height and the delivered's is 7.1% — one third. At 8x the fringe's lower edge is a hard aliased quad staircase that overlaps the outer end of both eyebrows.

clothingConstruction.label: clothing construction
clothingConstruction.note: The best-served category and still mixed. Genuinely constructed: the sneaker is a real shoe — cupsole, black toe wrap, cream quarter panels, lace and midsole trim, all reading at hero and at 40px; the crew sock has a proud rolled top (which is also the declared TEAM_MASK accent, judged on extent only — the roll-top's extent matches the sheet's sock cuff); the tee has a proud sleeve hem roll at station 0.660 that reads as a rolled cuff. Primitive: the shorts are a bare tapered tube with no hem, no side seam and no waistband, where the sheet shows a hemmed leg opening and a seam; the tee hem is a plain cut; and the collar is not a band at all but a dentate sawtooth where the neck cylinder punches through the chest shell (visible at 8x on the front board). The measured shoe split is in tolerance both ways (dominant tone 46.3 vs 52.4, second 53.7 vs 45.8, saturation 28.9 vs 26.8).

faceExpressionRead.label: face/expression read
faceExpressionRead.note: The four runtime-face stills are the strongest evidence on this character and 3.14 clearly passes: all four are distinct files (md5s all differ, 276-279KB, none is a ~29%-size empty) and all four are genuinely painted with real mouth interiors — grin shows a full tooth row, cheer opens onto teeth and a dark red throat, tongue drops a pink tongue past the lower lip, angry slants both brows and turns the mouth down. Readable at draft-card distance. Everything else in the category fails. There is no nose form: profile projection is 3.6% of head height against the concept's 8.2% (measured above), and from the front the nose is a flat triangular facet with no nostril and no tip. The face atlas reads as a decal island, not integrated with the skull — at 5x on the hero still there is a hard polygonal seam running temple-to-jaw with a visible skin-tone step across it, which 3.5's own 5-criterion names as disqualifying. At the 3/4 gameplay camera (hero, run) the island only covers the front plane, so the near half of the face is blank skin and only one eye reads. Measured faceSkin is out of tolerance on both sides — visible face left 37.1 vs concept 29.7 (+7.39, tol 6), right 37.1 vs 27.5 (+9.59, tol 6). The delivered face is also perfectly symmetric (asymmetry 0.00) where the sheet's whole attitude is one cocked brow; that read is gone. Ears are constructed, not bare bumps — the profile 4x crop shows outer rim, inner concha shadow and a lobe against the skull, so 3.10 passes; they flare more and sit lower than the sheet's tucked ears, but ear size is within the measured head-width tolerance so I am not scoring it.

heroAndFieldScale.label: hero and field scale
heroAndFieldScale.note: The 40px strip survives: red torso, charcoal shorts, dark cap and cream soles all separate, and he is not confusable with the grass or dirt. The hero close-up is where he loses. At hero the three defects that dominate the frame are the shoulder fin (a dark triangular shard tearing out of the red sleeve, visible in the idle hero, in the run at the far shoulder, and at both shoulders in the swing back view), the decal-island seam across the cheek, and the flat noseless profile of the skull. frontProfileSilhouette.label: front/profile silhouette
frontProfileSilhouette.note: The large read survives — mop-haired kid, light-blue hoodie, cuffed jeans, low-top sneakers — and I confirm 3.12 PASSES on the regenerated board: the legs are two legs with visible daylight in bind, A-pose and run, and I did not re-file the closed-leg finding. What caps this at 3 is that almost every transition is a butt-joined primitive rather than an organic form. The five crown tufts are literal cones (`builder.tube([...], [rr, 0.015], 2, HAIR, ...)`, 4 radial segments) stuck into a smooth dome; at 10x they read as thorns, not locks. Per trap 2 I cropped the dark wedges at their bases at 10x (/tmp/sn/prof-spikes.png): the interior is warm shaded HAIR_DARK, NOT the navy backdrop — these are NOT holes, and I do not file a 3.7 failure. The hood is a bare `builder.ellipsoid((0.0, 0.350, 2.470), (0.280, 0.170, 0.230), ...)` — in the A-pose profile it reads as a detached ball parked behind the neck with a hard intersection seam, not a draped cowl, and from the front it appears only as two lumps flanking the neck where the concept shows a soft collar roll wrapping onto the chest. The kangaroo pocket is a square-cornered flat slab. The ear breaks the head silhouette as a pointed leaf (see faceExpressionRead). The profile back of the hair is a flat faceted wall with a straight-cut nape line where the drawing tapers.

headBodyProportions.label: head/body proportions
headBodyProportions.note: The numbers I took are green and I will not argue with them: head height 33.3% of figure vs the concept's 34.5% (delta -1.20, ok) and head width:height 1.05 vs 1.02 (delta +0.03, ok), so 3.13 passes and this is not a narrow-head kid. Limb masses are childlike and the shoulder stays a rounded deltoid when the arm drops in the A-pose — 3.11 reads fine in A-pose, run and swing_contact, with no hinged-cylinder elbow and no popped seam. What holds it at 3 is the second half of the category, 'joints read as connected forms', which fails in three places. (1) The neck: I measured a continuous central skin column from row 261 to row 283 on the front board — 23px on a 563px figure, 4.1% of figure height — where the concept front figure has the chin sitting essentially on the hoodie collar with no visible neck column; the head reads pinned on a post. (2) The hoodie hem is a ruler-straight dark line clean across the body at row ~431 with the jeans starting as a separate cylinder below it — a hard butt joint, not a garment sitting over a hip. (3) The hood ellipsoid meets the back with a visible intersection crease rather than a blend.

hairMass.label: hair mass
hairMass.note: The weakest thing on the model after the hankie, and every part of the known finding checks out when I run it myself. `npm run measure:strands -- sniffles` at the default 5-45% band: concept 9.03 strand minima/row at mean prominence 24.2 over 97 rows; delivered 1.25 minima/row at mean prominence 48.5 over 76 rows — 14% of the concept's strand COUNT at 200% of its prominence. I state my band explicitly: 5-45% of head height, the default. That band does reach onto the brow, and I checked that the brow bars are not being counted as creases — they are dark ATLAS marks, not depth minima, and excluding them does not move a 1.25 that is already near the floor, so the reading stands. The cause is in the builder and I read it: `segments = 18` at detail>=2 against `clump = 1.0 + 0.06 * cos(6 * theta)` — 6 lobes over 18 columns is 3.0 columns per lobe, below the ~4 a crease needs to resolve, and the modulation amplitude is only 6%. So the mass is a smooth featureless blob, which caps at 4 by rule 3.3 before anything else is considered. But the silhouette is wrong too, so it goes below 4. The concept's signature is a SWEPT, layered fringe that crosses the brow hard toward his right; delivered is a symmetric mushroom. That is not an opinion — `measure:fidelity` reports visible face left of centre 31.6% delivered against the concept's 43.3% (OFF, tol 6) and visible face right 31.6% against 13.1% (OFF, tol 6). The source comment is candid about why: CURL_SWEEP's asymmetry is deliberately confined ABOVE z=3.20 'so the measured row remains symmetric', which keeps the asymmetry gate green while the sweep does not reach the row a viewer reads. Finally, at 8x the fringe's lower boundary is a jagged rectangular staircase of raw ring polygons (/tmp/sn/grin.png), so the hairline does not read as a hairline from the front.

clothingConstruction.label: clothing construction
clothingConstruction.note: SNIFFLES IS WEARING ANOTHER KID'S BODY, AND I DIFFED IT MYSELF RATHER THAN TAKING THE CLAIM. Hashing the tables in scripts/v2/blender: ARM_STATIONS is byte-identical across sculpt-sniffles/dex/lefty-source.py (md5 fc89871bf82d12c098f8fdc69673a3c5), CROTCH_LEVELS is byte-identical (742c07abddd1660ce29ac0bd7bcc5d15), and SHOULDER_BLEND, SHOE_STATIONS and SHOE_SECTION are byte-identical too. The full ArmSpec block — stations, cap_x, ring_squash, HandSpec tip_x, finger_root, finger_offsets, finger_lengths, finger_widths, the whole thumb_spine — diffs against dex's and lefty's at exactly ONE line: the variable name (`SNIFFLES_ARM` vs `DEX_ARM` / `LEFTY_ARM`). LEG_STATIONS diffs at two lines, and both are a colour token only (TEAM_MASK vs CUFF) — and TEAM_MASK is defined as rgba('96A4BA'), the same hex as CUFF, so the geometry is identical as well. SHOE_BANDS diffs at one value (quarter 0.345 vs 0.200). So: his HEAD (HEAD_RADII), TORSO_LEVELS and NECK_LEVELS are genuinely his own; his arms, hands, legs, feet and shoes are another kid's, copy-pasted. Stated plainly: sniffles does not have his own body below the collar. On the garments themselves. THE HANKIE — the identity detail this character is named for — is a flat 17 x 16 px 2x2 checker tile on the 563px front board, 3.02% of figure height wide by 2.84% tall, against the concept hankie's ~49 x 55 px on a 699px figure (~7.0% x 7.9%): under a fifth of the drawn area. Worse, it is the wrong OBJECT. The drawing has a long folded gingham cloth hanging OUT of the pocket mouth and draping down past the pocket's bottom third with a folded corner; the build is three coplanar `surface_patch` rectangles pasted ON the hoodie face, straddling the pocket's top edge, with no drape and no thickness. Its peak luminance is 202.8 against the hoodie's 185.7 — 17 levels, ~9% — so it also has almost no contrast to fall back on. The ribbed sleeve cuff and ribbed hem ARE authored (ARM_STATIONS has a proud SHIRT_DARK station at SLEEVE_HEM_X; TORSO_LEVELS has hem rows at 1.470/1.505) — per trap 1 I grepped before judging — but SHIRT_DARK #8AAEC8 against SHIRT #A5C8E0 is invisible at board lighting: at 8x the wrist is a smooth uniform blue tube with no cuff band at all (/tmp/sn/front-hand.png), where the concept shows a clearly darker, wider, vertically ribbed cuff and hem. The kangaroo pocket is a square-cornered rectangle where the drawing has a curved pouch with angled hand openings both sides and topstitching. Per trap 3 I judged the TEAM_MASK cuff on extent, not colour: the rolled jean cuff band is the declared accent surface, its extent matches the drawing's roll, and I file nothing against it.

faceExpressionRead.label: face/expression read
faceExpressionRead.note: 3.14 passes and I want to say so first: across the four runtime cells the mouth is a real opening, not a stroke — grin gives a wide dark interior with a visible cream tooth strip, angry a distinct down-turned frown with a shadowed underlip, and both read at draft-card size. The eyes are large, well-placed and legible, and the brow bars do change shape between grin and angry, so the expression channel is live. 3.10 passes as well: per trap 1 I grepped and found `EAR_SPEC = EarSpec(center=(0.020, 3.100), radii=(0.1250, 0.1550))` and `build_ear(...)` from sculptlib, and at 10x the ear has a genuine outer rim, a darker inner concha and a lobe against the skull — not a bare bump. Three things hold this at 3. (1) There is NO NOSE FRONT-ON. At 8x on the runtime grin and on the front board there is only a faint diagonal shading crease down the centre of the face — no tip, no nostrils, no cast shadow — where the concept has a distinct round button nose with a highlight. In profile the nose is a thin flat wedge that sits at eye level, barely breaking the silhouette; per trap 4 I am NOT counting the foreshortened near eye against it, only the nose. Rubric 3.5's five requires a real nose that breaks the profile, so five is off the table and the front absence pulls it below four. (2) The brows collide with the hairline. Measured on the front board: the topmost brow row is 179; the first face-skin row (fringe bottom) is 200 at x=209 and 189 at x=239 — i.e. over the outer half of each brow the hair fringe hangs BELOW the top of the brow, and at centre (x=269) only 6px of forehead skin survives on a 198px head, ~3%. The brows read as notches in the hair rather than features on a forehead. (3) The concept's freckles across the nose and cheeks — a real part of this kid's face — are absent in all four cells. Also worth recording against 6b.3: `measure:fidelity` puts visible face left/right at 31.6/31.6 against the concept's 43.3/13.1, both OFF at tol 6.

heroAndFieldScale.label: hero and field scale
heroAndFieldScale.note: The runtime page reports `model model` at 26.0k tris, so 4.1 is satisfied and this is real fidelity evidence. But the identity does not survive either end of the scale. At the 40px board strip the read is 'brown mop over pale blue over navy over cream soles' — true of the model, but it is also true of half the hoodie kids on this roster, and the one thing that would separate him is gone: I cropped the hero chest at 6x (/tmp/sn/hero-chest.png) and the hankie is COMPLETELY INVISIBLE at hero distance — the pocket survives as a faint darker rectangle and the checker tile does not survive at all. At 17px on a 563px board figure it is 1.2px at the 40px field sprite, i.e. below one pixel of real signal. So 3.9 fails: the 40px strip does not show this character's one memorable read, because his one memorable read has been shrunk to a fleck. What IS most distinctive at hero is the ear, and it is distinctive for the wrong reason — at 6x on the hero head it reads as a pointed elf leaf whose tip rises above the eye line and past the hair edge, where the concept ear is small, rounded and tucked. Deformation is otherwise clean: run and swing_contact hold at 42 and 44 fps with the elbow line continuous and no tearing, feet planted, and the CONTACT@7 marker landing on the visible bat/ball instant.

measuredFidelity.note: His ear line is refused (mop-poisoned); featurelatitude gates brow 49.4 vs traced 49.6, eye 66.3 vs 66.3, mouth 78.0 vs bounded 78.0 through his 3.99-2.62 span. The mouth trace is bounded (skin-adjacent pout below the scanned rows) and the recipe records his fringe swallowing the brows' outer halves. An authored asymmetric sweep is the known faceAsymmetry failure class (Flash/Penny), so the symmetric build is deliberate. The fringe SHAPE carries the sheet's sweep with the asymmetry strictly above the faceSkin sample row, so the measured row stays symmetric while the brow band reads swept.

polishFindings: THE HANKIE IS NOT A HANKIE. It is three coplanar surface_patch rectangles (0.120 x 0.120 units) pasted ON the hoodie face straddling the pocket's top edge — 17 x 16 px on the 563px board, 3.0% x 2.8% of figure height against the concept's ~7.0% x 7.9%, under a fifth of the drawn area. It is invisible at hero (cropped at 6x, confirmed absent) and sub-pixel at the 40px field read. Rebuild it as an actual hanging cloth: a draped strip issuing from the pocket MOUTH, at least 2x taller than wide, falling past the pocket's lower third with a folded corner, and give the plaid enough check pitch to survive downscale. This is the one detail the character is named for.

SNIFFLES HAS NO BODY OF HIS OWN BELOW THE COLLAR. ARM_STATIONS, CROTCH_LEVELS, SHOULDER_BLEND, SHOE_STATIONS and SHOE_SECTION are md5-identical to both dex's and lefty's; the entire ArmSpec (hand, fingers, thumb spine) diffs at one line — the variable name; LEG_STATIONS diffs only at a colour token that resolves to the same hex. Only HEAD_RADII, TORSO_LEVELS and NECK_LEVELS are authored for him. He needs arm, leg and shoe stations measured against HIS turnaround, not inherited.

The hair cannot express a crease it has no columns for: 18 columns against cos(6*theta) is 3.0 columns per lobe, and it measures 1.25 minima/row = 14% of the concept's 9.03. Trade rows for columns at constant triangle cost (the roster-wide lesson in measure-strands.mjs's header) — CURL_LEVELS has 10 rows; 8 rows x 24 columns costs less than 10 x 18 and would put the lobes above Nyquist.

The signature swept fringe does not reach the row anyone reads. CURL_SWEEP's asymmetry is deliberately confined above z=3.20 to keep the measured row symmetric, and the result is measured dead-on symmetric (31.6/31.6) against a concept that is 43.3/13.1. Let the sweep cross the brow band as the drawing does and accept what the asymmetry gate then reports, rather than authoring above it.

The five crown tufts are 4-segment cones butt-joined into a smooth dome and read as thorns at every scale, including 40px. Either blend them into the mass as raised lobes of the ring itself, or delete them — the concept's tousle is a scalloped silhouette edge, not spikes.

The fringe's lower boundary is the raw ring polygon edge and staircases visibly at hero (8x crop of the grin cell). It needs either more columns or a dedicated hairline row that follows fringe_z_at smoothly.

No forehead. Measured, the brow top is row 179 while the fringe bottom is row 189-200 over the outer half of each brow, leaving 0-6px of skin on a 198px head. Raise fringe_z_at by roughly one brow-height, or drop the FACE_ROWS brow band, so the brows sit on skin the way the drawing has them.

No nose front-on — only a shading crease. The profile nose is a thin flat wedge sitting at eye level that barely breaks the silhouette. The concept's round button nose with a highlight is a top-three identity feature on this kid and it is missing from the geometry, not just the atlas.
The concept's freckles across the nose and cheeks are absent from all four expression cells.

The ear reads as a pointed elf leaf whose tip rises above the eye line and past the hair edge — the most distinctive thing about him at hero, for the wrong reason. EAR_SPEC radii (0.1250, 0.1550) give a tall narrow oval; the drawing's ear is small, rounded and mostly tucked under the mop.

The hood is a bare ellipsoid ball at (0, 0.350, 2.470). In the A-pose profile it reads as a detached knapsack with a hard intersection seam, and from the front it is two lumps flanking the neck instead of the concept's soft collar roll wrapping onto the chest. It needs to open toward the front and blend into the shoulders.

The ribbed sleeve cuff and ribbed hem are authored but do not read: SHIRT_DARK #8AAEC8 against SHIRT #A5C8E0 is ~9% luminance apart and the wrist renders as a smooth uniform tube at 8x. Either widen the value gap or give the ribbing actual relief.
The kangaroo pocket is a square-cornered rectangular slab. The drawing's pouch has a curved lower edge, angled hand openings on both sides and topstitching — none of which survives.
23px of exposed neck (4.1% of figure height) where the concept has the chin essentially on the collar. Raise NECK_LEVELS' collar or lower the jaw so the head stops reading as pinned on a post.
The hoodie hem is a ruler-straight dark line clean across the body with the jeans starting as a separate cylinder below it — a visible butt joint at the hip in both board views.
The back of the hair is a flat faceted wall with a straight-cut nape line (clearest in the profile board and swing_contact), where the drawing tapers into the neck.

frontProfileSilhouette.label: front/profile silhouette
frontProfileSilhouette.note: DECAPITATED. I re-measured every board view myself: figure spans rows 73-647 (h=575px = 4.0ft) and rows 261-265 contain ZERO figure pixels in cricket-front-review, profile-review, front-apose-review and profile-apose-review alike — 5 rows, 0.035ft, at 32.7% of figure height. Row counts run 54,50,44,40,34,28,22,10,0,0,0,0,0,40,42,40 (front): the jaw tapers to a point, five rows of pure background, then the torso starts at a constant 40px. I cropped rows 215-295 at 6x with a magenta backdrop and the background is visibly straight through: the head FLOATS above a flat-topped neck stub. Root cause found in the sculpt source and it is arithmetic, not a posing artifact — HEAD_CENTER z 3.220 with HEAD_RADII z 0.460 puts the skull's bottom pole at z 2.760, while NECK_LEVELS tops out at z 2.720. 0.040ft of the boy has no geometry. Rubric 3.7 forbids holes and gaps outright and this is the worst shape on that list; silhouette.lint cannot see it because a gap open at both sides is never an enclosed pocket. Beyond the severance the large read still misses the sheet: the concept's profile is a radiating spiked mop over a clear cheek, jaw and ear, while the delivered profile is a smooth motorcycle-helmet shell with a hard flat-cut vertical back plane and an angular bevelled corner (a butt-joined primitive, which 3.1's 5/5 explicitly excludes), the torso is one bell-shaped apron slab from chest to hip ending in a hard hem ledge, and the sleeve meets the bare forearm at a visible diameter step with no transition. The one metric measure:fidelity puts outside tolerance is silhouette too: daylight between the ankles 26.7 delivered vs 0.00 concept (tol 12) — the bind stance is planted far wider than the sheet's feet-together stand. LEGS ARE NOT FUSED (3.12 is fine: clear daylight between thighs and calves in bind, A-pose and the run still) — if anything they are too far apart.

headBodyProportions.label: head/body proportions
headBodyProportions.note: The RATIOS are fine and I took them myself with measure:fidelity: head height 32.7% of figure vs the concept's 34.2% (delta -1.48, ok) and head width:height 0.93 vs 0.87 (delta +0.05, ok), so 3.13's aspect check passes and this is not a bobblehead. What fails is the other half of the category — 'joints read as connected forms.' The head is not connected to the body AT ALL (see 3.1: 0.040ft of missing geometry between skull pole z 2.760 and neck top z 2.720), which is the most extreme possible failure of a joint reading as a connected form. It is not an isolated slip either: in the A-pose front board the shoulder is a square-cornered block with no deltoid — the tee sleeve is a fat cylinder that simply stops, and the bare forearm emerges from it a full step narrower with a visible flat ring at the junction. The hand is a paddle mitt. The neck itself is a bare flat-topped cylinder butt-joined to a flat-cut head underside, with no sternocleidomastoid, no trapezius sweep and no jaw shadow to bed it in. Ratios that measure correct on a figure that comes apart at the neck cannot score 4.

hairMass.label: hair mass
hairMass.note: I ran measure:strands myself at three bands, and the default 5-45% is not the culprit — the result is the same everywhere. 5-45%: concept 10.19 strand minima/row at prominence 24.4 over 98 rows, delivered 3.19 at prominence 72.2 over 70 rows = 31% of the concept's strand count at 296% of its prominence. Tightening to 5-30% to stay off the forehead and brows (where skin/hair and brow edges could count as false creases) gives concept 8.98 vs delivered 3.59 = 40% at 278%; 5-35% gives 9.34 vs 3.75 = 40% at 295%. The band choice moves the number by nine points and the verdict not at all. That count/prominence signature is diagnostic: the delivered mass has almost no creases, and the few it has are enormous — they are the facets of an 18-gon and the bases of the spike cones, not strands. I confirmed the mechanism in the sculpt source rather than inferring it: ring_loft_cap builds `segments = 18` columns and modulates them with `clump = 1.0 + 0.055 * cos(6 * theta)` — six lobes across eighteen columns is 3.0 columns per lobe, below the ~4 a crease needs to read, and the amplitude is 5.5% of half-width. That clump can never produce a groove; the code's own comment says it exists so 'the mop's back is not a featureless helmet,' and the board shows it failed at exactly that. What ships is a smooth glossy bowl with fourteen discrete cone spikes stuck on the crown, which reads as horns, not hair. Rubric 3.3 caps a smooth featureless blob at 4 'however correct its silhouette' — and this silhouette is NOT correct either. The concept mop radiates pointed locks in every direction, all round the sides and back; the delivered mass is a bare rounded shell everywhere except the crown mohawk. THE HAIR ALSO SWALLOWS FACE THE SHEET KEEPS CLEAR: CAP_FRINGE drops the lower edge to z 3.000 at |x| 0.44, and the profile crop shows two claw-shaped hair lobes hanging over the cheekbone down to mouth level with the near ear buried and the eye reduced to a sliver, where the sheet's profile keeps the whole eye, cheek, jaw and a fully drawn ear clear. I also cropped the profile hair at 12x around the temple and there is a genuine 4-5px dark pinhole notch in the otherwise unbroken shell.

clothingConstruction.label: clothing construction
clothingConstruction.note: The most defensible category, and it still does not reach 4. Real construction IS present and I verified it by cropping rather than asserting: the shoes carry a cream cupsole band, a toe cap, a lit collar and two-to-three lace stripes; there is a ringer collar at the neck; the ankle carries a rolled cuff ring; the bib carries a pocket badge. Measured shoe split is honest too — measure:fidelity reads the concept's shoe tones as #fbeedc and #7b644b and reports dominant 49.8 vs 54.9, second 50.2 vs 44.0, saturation 24.5 vs 27.4, all inside tolerance. But the PRIMARY garment is a primitive. Cropping the torso at 4x, the overalls read as a single bell-shaped apron flaring from the chest and terminating in a hard horizontal hem ledge at the hip — no side seam, no leg-opening construction, and the two straps are flat plates butt-joined onto a flat bib with no buckle, no button and no topstitch, where the concept shows brass buttons on both straps, a bib pocket with a lip and a hip patch pocket. The team-accent badge (TEAM_MASK, raw grey on the board, so I judge EXTENT not colour) is proportionate and correctly confined to the bib pocket — that part is right — but it is a flat rectangle with no pocket lip, so it reads as a sticker. In profile the shoe is a bar of soap: a rounded rectangular loaf with no heel counter, no tongue, no toe upturn and a flat untreaded sole. Two fidelity misses I checked against a 4x crop of the concept's feet: the concept's rolled cuff is clearly light DENIM with orange topstitching, while CUFF is authored #D5CDBE and renders near-cream; and the concept ankle is BARE SKIN between cuff and shoe, while the delivered adds a prominent white tube-sock column that is not in the sheet at all.

faceExpressionRead.label: face/expression read
faceExpressionRead.note: Genuinely mixed, and it lands at 3. The strengths are real: the eyes are the best-sculpted thing on the model, with a proper iris, pupil, highlight and lash line that read at hero scale; the freckles are present and placed as the sheet places them; and 3.14 passes cleanly. I checked all four -runtime-face-*.png stills and they are ALL genuinely painted, not stubs — bytes 275741 / 273942 / 274270 / 273929 for grin / cheer / tongue / angry, within 0.7% of each other, nowhere near the ~29% signature of an empty one — and I cropped and composited the four faces at 4x: grin is a closed curved smile, cheer opens to a red mouth interior with teeth, tongue puts a pink tongue out over the lower lip, angry drops the corners and angles the brows. Four distinct, readable emotions with lips, teeth and tongue, none collapsing to a stroke. The failures are structural. At 9x the face is unmistakably a DECAL ISLAND: a hard-edged, stair-stepped skin-tone patch pasted onto the skull, with the boundary visible as right-angle staircases across the forehead and down the right cheek and a tonal step between the decal skin and the sculpted skin below it. Rubric 3.5 names 'no visible decal-island seam' as a 5/5 requirement, and this is the seam the clause is about. The brows are flat dark quadrilaterals, not brow forms. And the nose does not read: nose_push IS authored (an upturned button, max 0.086 push at |nx|<0.18 around nz -0.44 — I grepped it rather than calling it absent), but at board scale the front view shows only the faintest shading between the eyes where the concept has a distinct round button nose with nostrils. 3.5's 5/5 asks for 'a real nose that breaks the profile' and 'a form, not a sticker'; this is a sticker with an invisible nose.

heroAndFieldScale.label: hero and field scale
heroAndFieldScale.note: The review page reports 'model model', so 4.1 is satisfied and this is fidelity evidence, not proxy evidence. At hero scale the character reads: the expressions land, the eyes carry, the palette (brown mop, green tee, blue overalls, taupe canvas shoes) is legibly Cricket, and the run and swing_contact stills show two clear legs, a bent elbow and planted feet with no visible tearing. I cropped the runtime hero head at 6x and the neck DOES read as connected once the skinning closes it, so the severance is a board defect rather than a gameplay one — but 3.7 is a board check and the board is the delivered evidence. At the board's 40-pixel strip the read degrades to 'brown bowl, green top, blue bottom.' The one memorable thing about this kid on the sheet is a wild spiked mop radiating in every direction, and the delivered bowl-with-a-crown-mohawk keeps only a fuzzy crown fringe of that at 40px — the sides and back go smooth and the read becomes generic against a roster of brown-haired boys. Add the sticker seam and the fringe overhang, both visible at hero scale, and this cannot be called 4.
