polishFindings: BLOCKER — the head is severed from the body. 5 empty rows (0.035ft) at 32.7% of figure height in ALL FOUR board views. Repair is arithmetic: the skull ellipsoid's bottom pole sits at z 2.760 (HEAD_CENTER z 3.220 minus HEAD_RADII z 0.460) and NECK_LEVELS stops at z 2.720. Raise the top neck ring to at least z 2.78 (or add a ring that overlaps the skull pole) so the two forms interpenetrate rather than nearly touch, then re-run the board and drop cricket from the DEBT map in scripts/v2/continuity.lint.test.js — a debt entry is a defect that is still shipping, not an allowance.

The neck is a bare flat-topped cylinder butt-joined to a flat-cut head underside. Even once the gap closes, there is no jaw-to-neck transition, no trapezius sweep and no chin shadow — the join will still read as two primitives stacked.

Hair topology cannot carry a crease: 18 ring columns against a cos(6*theta) clump is 3.0 columns per lobe at 5.5% amplitude. Either raise segments to 24+ so each of the six lobes gets four columns, or replace the clump ripple with authored lock geometry. Measured result today: 31-40% of the concept's strand count at 278-296% of its prominence — a smooth shell punctuated by 18-gon facets.

The hair silhouette is the wrong shape, not just under-detailed. The sheet's mop radiates pointed locks from every side and the back; the delivered mass is a smooth bowl with all 14 spike cones on the crown. The sides and back need locks or the 40px read stays generic.
Profile hair back plane is a hard flat vertical cut with an angular bevelled corner — a visible butt-joined primitive at hero scale.

A 4-5px dark pinhole notch is visible in the profile hair shell near the temple (cropped at 12x from cricket-profile-review at left 255, top 120). Small, but it is a puncture in an otherwise unbroken surface.

The fringe hangs over the cheek. CAP_FRINGE drops to z 3.000 at |x| 0.44, and the profile crop shows two claw-shaped lobes covering the cheekbone to mouth level, burying the near ear and reducing the eye to a sliver — the sheet's profile keeps eye, cheek, jaw and a fully drawn ear clear.

The ear is built (EarSpec/build_ear confirmed) but does not READ as constructed on the board: at 14x it is a flat pointed flap with no outer rim, no inner shadow and no lobe against the skull. The source's own comment concedes the ears hide under the mop. 3.10 is about what the board shows, and it shows a bare flap.

The face is a decal island with a visible hard seam: at 9x the hairline is a right-angle staircase across the forehead and down the right cheek, with a tonal step between the decal skin and the sculpted skin below it.
The nose does not read in the front board view. nose_push is authored (max 0.086 tip push) but produces only faint shading where the concept shows a distinct round button nose with nostrils.
Eyebrows are flat dark quadrilaterals with cut corners, not tapered brow forms.
The neutral mouth collapses to a single thin stroke on the board. (The four expression stills are fine — 3.14 passes — but the default face is the one on the draft card.)
Shoulders are square blocks with no deltoid, and the tee sleeve meets the bare forearm at a hard diameter step with a visible flat ring — most obvious in cricket-front-apose-review.

The overalls are one bell-shaped apron slab from chest to hip with a hard hem ledge — no side seams, no leg-opening construction, no strap buttons or buckles, and no hip pocket, where the concept shows brass buttons on both straps and a patch pocket.
The bib pocket badge is correctly confined and correctly sized as the team accent (extent judged, colour ignored), but it is a flat rectangle with no pocket lip, so it reads as a decal.
The rolled ankle cuff is authored cream (CUFF #D5CDBE) where the concept's roll is light DENIM with orange topstitching — confirmed against a 4x crop of the concept's feet.
The delivered model adds prominent white tube socks between cuff and shoe; the concept shows bare skin at the ankle.

In profile the shoe is a soap-bar loaf: no heel counter, no tongue, no toe upturn, flat untreaded sole. The front view's lace stripes and cupsole are good and should be carried into the profile forms.
Two thin black hook-shaped slivers sit low on the front of both shoes (symmetric, so geometry rather than noise) and read as scratches at hero scale.

Bind stance is too wide: ankle daylight 26.7 against the concept's 0.00 (tol 12) — the only metric measure:fidelity flags. Read it as a stance note, not a tolerance to widen: the sheet stands feet together.

frontProfileSilhouette.label: front/profile silhouette
frontProfileSilhouette.note: The FRONT large-read is fine: top-knot, A-line dress, bare legs, cream sock cuffs — recognisable with colour stripped. The PROFILE is not. Cropping peaches-profile-review.png at 190,120 (110x130 @8x) shows (a) the temple wisp as a flat brown PLANK with a hard rectangular cut end, floating over the cheek and interpenetrating it, (b) no nose worth the name — the front-of-face silhouette from brow to lip is a single soft curve broken only by a ~4px tan wedge, (c) an oversized curled ear shell occupying roughly the front third of the head's side, notched by hair. Worse, rubric 3.1's 5-criterion ('transitions organic, not butt-joined primitives') fails at the shoulder: peaches-front-apose-review.png cropped at 200,250 (60x60 @12x) shows the deltoid dome as a DISCRETE ELLIPSOID stacked on the arm cylinder, with a hard silhouette step where it overhangs the arm and a dark crease under it. It is a ball butt-joined to a tube, not a fairing. Also the bodice is a plain truncated cone — the concept's scoop neck, shoulder straps and armscye are all absent, replaced by one cream ring around a tube. Nothing is SEVERED; the white seen at the armpit is background between limb and torso, not a mesh hole. 2.

headBodyProportions.label: head/body proportions
headBodyProportions.note: The numbers are green and I took them: head height 29.6% of figure vs the concept's 30.4% (-0.80, ok); head width:height 0.84 vs 0.80 (+0.04, ok); face visible left 30.0 vs 26.8 and right 32.9 vs 32.7, asymmetry 2.86 — all ok. No bobblehead. What fails the category's second clause — 'joints read as connected forms' — is everything below the neck. The neck is a long unmodulated skin cylinder (a stalk; peaches-front-apose-review.png at 6x, 170,220) with the head sitting on it rather than growing from it. The shoulder is the separate ball described above. The leg from hem to sock is a straight untapered pipe with no knee, no calf swell and no ankle taper — visible in the same A-pose crop and in the 8x foot crop. Measured daylight between the ankles reads 34.0 against the concept's 0.00 (tol 12): per 6b.4 that is a STANCE finding, not a tolerance to widen — the bind pose plants her a third of a leg-width wider than the sheet's feet-together standing pose, which is why she reads bandy rather than as the concept's neat little girl. 3.

hairMass.label: hair mass
hairMass.note: Measured myself, and it is the roster's worst reading so far. npm run measure:strands -- peaches at the DEFAULT band (5-45% of head height): concept 8.71 strand minima/row at prominence 20.5 over 86 rows; delivered 0.10 minima/row at prominence 43.7 over 67 rows — 1% of the concept's strand count at 213% of its prominence. I re-ran at 5-30% (concept 8.85, delivered 0.12 = 1%, 253% prominence) and 10-40% (concept 9.40, delivered 0.10 = 1%, 251%) specifically to lift the band clear of the forehead/brow edges the tool's header warns about. All three bands agree: essentially ZERO strand grouping. And the eye confirms the ruler — the bun is a smooth acorn dome with a pointed apex and a hard STEP SEAM ring where it lands on the cap, over a smooth featureless helmet. The concept's bun is a visibly twisted, coiled braid. Rubric 3.3 caps a smooth featureless blob at 4 however correct its silhouette; this is below that because the silhouette is also wrong (acorn vs coil) and because the mass misbehaves at the edges: the two temple wisps are plain tapered tubes (builder.tube radii 0.050/0.062/0.024) that in the FRONT board and in all four runtime face stills lie directly ACROSS the ear ellipse on both sides — the known 'wisps over the ears' regression is visibly back in the delivered render even though the script comment claims they sit in front of it — and in peaches-runtime-hero.png the near wisp crosses the near EYE. No bare-skull read, which is the one thing that keeps this off 1. 2.

clothingConstruction.label: clothing construction
clothingConstruction.note: Split verdict, and the split lands at 3. Constructed and reading: the scalloped six-petal hem shell with its cream edge lip (build_petal_hem, three loft rows with a cos(6*theta) scallop) is genuinely a hem and reads as one in the swing still; the cream waistband and neckline are real loft rings with their own vertex colours, not painted gradients — I checked the builder, every garment colour boundary here is a CONSTRUCTED EDGE (TORSO_LEVELS via dress_color, the petal specs, and LEG_STATIONS for the sock), no gradient fakes. The shoe has a real cupsole, toe cap and lace geometry (ShoeSpec/build_shoe), visible at 6x. Not constructed: the bodice has NO straps, NO scoop neck and NO armhole — the concept draws all three clearly from front and back, and the delivered garment is a cone with one cream band around its top, so the sleeveless read comes from the arm leaving the cone rather than from a cut garment. The leaf appliqué is a single smooth TRIM ellipsoid (0.070, 0.022, 0.120) — a featureless teardrop blob, where the sheet draws a large outlined leaf with a central vein running most of the skirt panel. And the shoe is measurably off: the band's second tone reads 63.0% against the concept's 47.5% (+15.5, tol 8) and the band's mean saturation 27.4 against 32.7 (-5.31, tol 4) — the cream cupsole has eaten the peach canvas, so the sneaker reads greyish-white rather than the sheet's peach. TEAM_MASK extent is correctly small and declared: two leg loft stations (z 0.425 and 0.390) forming a sock band; I judged extent only, not the raw grey. 3.

faceExpressionRead.label: face/expression read
faceExpressionRead.note: The single worst thing on this character, and it is not subtle. Crop peaches-runtime-face-grin.png at 460,140 (150x150 @6x), or peaches-front-review.png at 190,60 (160x200 @5x): a lighter, flat-shaded polygonal DECAL ISLAND covers the forehead and eye region with hard STRAIGHT-EDGED seams — a visible staircase step across the upper-left forehead, a squared notch at the upper right, and a vertical drop at the right temple that CLIPS the right eyebrow off in a straight cut. Rubric 3.5 names 'no visible decal-island seam' explicitly; this is the seam, and it is legible at hero scale in every one of the four runtime stills, not only in a 6x crop. There is also no nose as a FORM — the front view has only a faint soft shading lozenge and the profile a ~4px wedge, so the face is a sticker on an ellipsoid, which 3.5 calls out by name. In peaches-runtime-hero.png (crop 460,150 @7x) the 3/4 hero read is worse still: hair covers the far half of the head, the near temple wisp crosses the near eye, and only one eye is partly legible. What passes: all four -runtime-face-*.png stills are GENUINELY PAINTED — I took the byte sizes myself (grin 280,847 / cheer 279,876 / tongue 279,836 / angry 279,780, a 0.4% spread, none anywhere near the ~29% stub size), and grin shows a toothed crescent, tongue an open mouth with a red tongue, so 3.14's mouth-emotion check holds. No freckles and no blush anywhere, both of which the sheet carries and the record listed as polish. 2.

heroAndFieldScale.label: hero and field scale
heroAndFieldScale.note: Two different answers. At 40 px the board's zoom strip still delivers the one memorable read — brown top-knot over a marigold A-line — so 3.9 passes; the silhouette is distinctive enough among the roster that the bun survives to 1-2 px of value contrast. At HERO the read degrades: the face is half-occluded by hair and the crossing wisp, and the deltoid ball becomes a separate object because the toon shader gives it its OWN closed ink outline — crop peaches-runtime-run.png at 490,320 (130x130 @7x) and the far shoulder is an outlined sphere sitting beside the neck, the near arm is outlined away from the torso along its whole root. Colour holds at runtime (the dress is properly marigold in peaches-runtime-hero.png) even though the fidelity board washes it out: I sampled the board's dress at #d5b07f, saturation 0.406, against the concept's #e2932d at 0.799, and the board's cheek at 0.387 against the concept's 0.717 — that is the board's key light, not a vertex-colour slip, so I am not scoring it. Field scale is fine, hero scale is not. 3.

measuredFidelity.result: npm run measure:fidelity -- peaches (concept front 221x691, delivered 450x561; shoe tones off the concept #fcf1e4 and #ecca9d): head height as % of figure 30.4 -> 29.6, delta -0.80 OK; head width:height 0.80 -> 0.84, +0.04 OK; shoe band dominant tone 35.5 -> 37.0, +1.41 OK; shoe band SECOND TONE 47.5 -> 63.0, +15.5 OFF (tol 8); shoe band mean saturation 32.7 -> 27.4, -5.31 OFF (tol 4); DAYLIGHT BETWEEN THE ANKLES 0.00 -> 34.0, +34.0 OFF (tol 12); visible face left of centre 26.8 -> 30.0, +3.21 OK; visible face right of centre 32.7 -> 32.9, +0.12 OK; face left/right asymmetry 0.00 -> 2.86 OK. 3 of 9 metrics outside tolerance. || npm run measure:strands -- peaches, DEFAULT BAND 5-45% of head height (concept head rows 83-296, delivered 87-252): concept 8.71 minima/row at mean prominence 20.5 over 86 rows; delivered 0.10 minima/row at prominence 43.7 over 67 rows = 1% of concept strand count, 213% of prominence. RE-RUN at 5-30% to clear forehead/brow false creases: concept 8.85/19.3 (54 rows) vs delivered 0.12/48.8 (43 rows) = 1% count, 253% prominence. RE-RUN at 10-40%: concept 9.40/19.5 (65 rows) vs delivered 0.10/48.8 (50 rows) = 1% count, 251% prominence. All three bands agree at 1%. || Colour samples I took with sharp over flattened RGB: concept dress body (turnaround box 120,380-240,520) mean #e2932d, saturation 0.799, n=16771; delivered dress body (front-review box 230,330-300,430) mean #d5b07f, saturation 0.406, n=7000. Board key-light wash, not a vertex-colour slip — runtime hero shows correct marigold. || Runtime face still byte sizes, taken myself: grin 280,847; cheer 279,876; tongue 279,836; angry 279,780 (spread 0.4%; the empty-still signature is ~29% of a sibling, so all four are genuinely painted). Also hero HUD reads model model, tris 27.7k, draws 14, seam 0.0004 rad closed. || Delivered figure bbox in peaches-front-apose-review.png: 229 x 562 px (x 155-383, y 86-647). || Sculpt-script greps performed before any absence claim: EarSpec and build_ear ARE imported and called per side with EAR_SPEC center (0.020, 3.358) radii (0.1250, 0.1550) — ears are CONSTRUCTED, not a bare bump, and the profile crop confirms an outer rim, an inner concha shadow and a lobe (3.10 passes). The DELTOID DOME exists and ships: builder.ellipsoid((side*0.232, 0.004, 2.486), (0.098, 0.108, 0.102), SKIN, {Spine2: 0.55, Arm: 0.45}) — the 0.55/0.45 blend is exactly as the record describes; it EXISTS but does not READ as a fairing. TEAM_MASK #D8D2C6 is confined to two LEG_STATIONS (z 0.425, 0.390) as the sock stripe; extent judged, colour ignored per the raw-grey convention.
measuredFidelity.note: featurelatitude gates brow 50.1 vs traced 50.2, eye 62.5 vs 62.5, mouth 77.4 vs 77.5 - the mouth trace was corrected by the analyser's own ambiguity refusal (two bands at 77.5 and 84.5; the upper is the lip line). The recipe records her dress and skin sharing a hue lane.

polishFindings: 3.5 BLOCKER — visible decal-island seam on the face. A lighter, flat-shaded polygonal patch covers the forehead and eye region with hard straight edges: a staircase step across the upper-left forehead, a squared notch upper-right, and a vertical seam at the right temple that clips the right eyebrow off in a straight cut. Cropped and confirmed at 5x in peaches-front-review.png (190,60 160x200) and at 6x in all four peaches-runtime-face-*.png (460,140 150x150). Legible at 1x, not only at zoom.

3.11 BLOCKER — the deltoid dome exists in the script but does not fair. Cropped at 12x from peaches-front-apose-review.png (200,250 60x60): the skin ellipsoid reads as a discrete ball stacked on the arm cylinder, overhanging it with a hard silhouette step and a dark crease underneath. At runtime the toon shader draws it its OWN closed ink outline — peaches-runtime-run.png at 7x (490,320) shows the far shoulder as an outlined sphere beside the neck. Four ring/cap/blend rounds were replaced by a dome that has the same failure mode one primitive up.

3.8 — the temple wisps still cross the ears in the delivered render. In peaches-front-review.png at 12x (285,155 60x60) and in every runtime face still, the brown wisp tube lies directly across the tan ear ellipse on both sides. The script comment asserts they sit IN FRONT of the ears, but in the front orthographic projection wisp x 0.330-0.385 overlays the ear at the skull surface. In profile the same wisp is a flat plank with a hard rectangular cut end floating over and into the cheek.

3.3 — the bun is an acorn, not a coil. measure:strands returns 1% of the concept's strand count at all three bands I ran. There is also a hard STEP SEAM ring where the bun's base lands on the cap (visible at 5x in front and profile, and at 7x in the hero), so the two hair volumes read as two objects rather than one designed mass.

3.4 — the dress bodice has no straps, no scoop neck and no armhole. The concept draws all three from front and back; the delivered garment is a truncated cone with a single cream ring around its top, so the sleeveless read comes only from the arm leaving the cone.

3.4 — the leaf appliqué is a smooth featureless TRIM ellipsoid (radii 0.070, 0.022, 0.120), a teardrop blob with no outline and no central vein, where the sheet draws a large veined leaf across most of the skirt's lower panel. It is also noticeably smaller relative to the skirt than the sheet's.

6b.2 — the sneaker reads greyish-cream, not peach. Second tone 63.0% of the band vs the concept's 47.5% (+15.5, tol 8) and mean saturation 27.4 vs 32.7 (-5.31, tol 4): the cream cupsole and toe bumper have eaten the peach canvas upper. The lace geometry survives but at 6x (peaches-front-review.png 180,560 190x120) it reads as three hairline scratches plus a black eyelet wedge rather than laces.

6b.4 — stance, not tolerance. Ankle daylight measures 34.0 against the concept's 0.00 (tol 12). Do not widen the tolerance; the bind pose stands her a third of a leg-width wider than the sheet's feet-together standing pose.

3.2 — the neck is a long unmodulated skin cylinder and the leg from hem to sock is a straight untapered pipe with no knee, no calf swell and no ankle taper. Both read as primitives the garments happen to end on.

Minor artifact, cropped before reporting — a faint dashed trail of ~4 dark olive pixels runs inboard from the armpit onto the dress in peaches-runtime-swing.png. Cropped at 20x (540,355 45x45): it is an outline fragment where the arm root ring grazes the dress surface, not a hole and not a gouge. Reads as specks of dirt at 1x.
Polish still outstanding from the record: no freckles and no blush anywhere on the delivered face, both of which the turnaround carries clearly on the cheeks and nose bridge.

PASSES I verified rather than assumed: nothing is severed (the white at the armpit is background between limb and torso, not a mesh hole); the legs are two legs with clear daylight between thighs and calves in the front board and A-pose (3.12 passes on the board — the 34% ankle number is an overshoot, not a fusion); ears ARE constructed per EarSpec/build_ear and show rim, concha shadow and lobe in profile (3.10); all garment colour boundaries are constructed loft-ring edges, never painted gradients; all four runtime face stills are genuinely painted (0.4% byte spread); head width:height 0.84 vs 0.80 keeps 3.13 green; grin shows teeth and tongue shows a tongue, so 3.14 holds.
Trap-4 note: the dark slit at the near eye in peaches-profile-review.png is the near-side eye foreshortened in a true 90-degree orthographic profile. Not reported as a defect.
Trap-3 note: TEAM_MASK is raw grey on the board by design. Judged by extent only — it is confined to two leg loft stations forming a sock band, which is correctly small and declared.

frontProfileSilhouette.label: front/profile silhouette
frontProfileSilhouette.note: BINARY 3.7 FAILS THE PROFILE. I scanned every row of lefty-profile-review.png for transparent-alpha separations and found three detached islands in the silhouette: (a) rows 288-310 (23 consecutive rows, 4.1% of the 557px figure height) show the jacket's front placket as a wholly SEVERED 10-11px-wide bar, colour #7e3101 at (231,295), separated from the torso by a 2-8px transparent gap that widens to 8px at row 288; (b) rows 124-134 (11 rows) carry a 2-3px cap-coloured splinter (#c8bdad at (231,124)) detached from the crown at the cap's top-front; (c) rows 203-206 carry a 7-9px blonde island (x341-349) off the back of the head. The same placket separation appears in the front board at row 280 (island x226-234 against body x241-327). The large read otherwise lands - cap, orange top, dark pants, cream shoes - but the profile torso is a constant-depth slab (84px at y=360, 83px at y=420, no chest, no waist, no back curve) and every transition is a butt-joined primitive: the sleeve tube meets a straight vertical torso wall with a crease notch, the jacket hem is a flat horizontal cut into the pants. Two measure:fidelity metrics also miss on silhouette: head width:height 0.88 vs concept 0.98 (delta -0.10, tol 0.08) and ankle daylight 31.4 vs 0.00 (tol 12). 3.12 (two legs) I re-measured myself and it PASSES: 159 consecutive rows of two runs from y440-600, max inter-leg daylight 56.0% of row span at y=597 - I confirm the leg-fusion finding is dead. || MAINTAINER CORRECTION, measured after this critique: the figure is NOT severed and binary 3.7 does not fail this way. A 2D connected-component scan (8-connectivity, alpha>128) of all four delivered views finds lefty is ONE piece in every one of them; the three 'detached islands' are ROW-WISE gaps that reconnect outside the scanned band — the placket run at x226-236 rejoins the torso by y=320. What IS real and is kept as the finding: the placket stands proud enough to open 32 rows of visible background between it and the chest in the profile outline, gap up to 12px, identical in bind and A-pose (so it is not the T-pose arm). Cropped at 10x it reads as a floating brown slab. This is the same class dex's review found on his kangaroo pocket (31 rows, 31px) — a proud garment panel authored as a slab that detaches from the profile outline — and it is a silhouette defect, not a severance.

headBodyProportions.label: head/body proportions
headBodyProportions.note: Head height is right: 29.7% of figure vs the concept's 28.4%, delta +1.28, inside tolerance. Head WIDTH is not: width:height 0.88 delivered vs 0.98 concept, delta -0.10 against a 0.08 tolerance, so the skull is sculpted ~10% narrower than the drawing - rubric 3.13's named failure mode. Joints do not read as connected forms. At 4x on the front board's shoulder (crop of x150-270,y250-370 and x280-400,y250-370) the sleeve is a plain tapering cylinder butt-joined into a straight vertical torso wall with a concave crease notch and no deltoid cap at all; the answer to the fin-shear question is that there is no fin to shear, but there is also no shoulder form. In the run still the elbow is a visible step between two cylinders rather than a continuous line. The neck is a straight column into a slab torso with no trapezius or clavicle. Body is vertically continuous, no bobblehead, and the 40px strip shows correct child stack - that is what keeps this off a 1.

hairMass.label: hair mass
hairMass.note: The worst category and the worst defect on the model. It is not one designed mass; it is a handful of flat cards with hard straight-cut edges. STRANDS, run by me: default band 5-45% gives 0.58 minima/row delivered against 7.60 concept = 8% of the concept's strand count at 69% of its prominence. I re-ran three other bands because the default reaches badly on this kid - her hair is UNDER a backwards cap, so the crown band is cap on both sheets, and the lower bands land on the painted eyes and brows. 5-35% (pure cap/crown band): 10% of count, 77% of prominence. 35-75%: 47% of count but 192% of prominence, and 45-95%: 55% at 203% - those two are CONTAMINATED, the giveaway being that a painted eye scores a far deeper 'crease' than any hair groove, so I do not credit them. The honest reading is 8-10%. HAIRLINE: rubric 3.3 requires it to read from the front, and it does not - measure:fidelity reports visible face left of centre 34.2% vs 27.6% concept (+6.68, tol 6) and right 34.9% vs 28.6% (+6.28, tol 6), i.e. the delivered shows ~24% MORE bare face at the brow line than the drawing because there is no fringe at all; the forehead is skin from brow to cap edge. My own pixel count over the delivered head box (y90-254) puts blonde at 7.9% of head-region pixels. BARE-SKULL READ FROM A GAMEPLAY ANGLE: in lefty-runtime-hero.png the 3/4 camera shows cap + skin + one thin yellow sideburn ribbon; at 7x (crop x455-585,y170-300) that near-side hair is three separate flat ribbons, each with a knife-straight cut bottom edge and its own outline stroke, one of them cutting across the ear's back rim. INTERPENETRATION: at swing_contact (crop x470-630,y180-450, 4x) the ponytail is a flat tapering slab that passes IN FRONT of the orange sleeve and terminates in a squared-off flat cut over the torso, and the back of the skull is a featureless yellow egg with zero grouping. Colour separation against the cap is also poor - authored HAIR #D8B440 against CAP #C8B08A reads as one khaki value on the board.

clothingConstruction.label: clothing construction
clothingConstruction.note: ★ THE LEG_STATIONS QUESTION, MEASURED. sculpt-lefty-source.py lines 531-545 and sculpt-dex-source.py lines 518-532 are BYTE-IDENTICAL - I diffed them directly and diff returns empty, comments included. The shared comment claims 'per-leg halves come from the central jeans runs (139-268 at z 1.40 across both)'. I traced that myself. Lefty's own front figure at z=1.40 (row y=606) has dark-jeans runs at x 108-173 and 182-247, i.e. 108-247 across both. Dex's at z=1.40 (row y=596) has 132-200 and 214-270, i.e. ~132-270. The cited 139-268 is DEX'S trace, not lefty's. So the answer is plain: LEFTY'S LEGS ARE NOT TRACED FROM HIS DRAWING - the table and its provenance comment were copied wholesale from dex, and only the two '# measured:' lines above it were re-taken for lefty. The numeric damage is small, which is why nothing caught it: converting lefty's own runs to per-leg halves gives 0.1963ft at z=1.40, 0.1842 at z=1.25, 0.1752 at z=0.80, against dex's table values 0.1972 / 0.1930 / 0.1794 - the worst error is +0.009ft (+5%) at z=1.25, well inside the 0.04 tolerance the file cites. And the two '# measured:' pair-outer lines ARE lefty's: I re-measured 0.4441 at z=1.25 and 0.5136 at z=0.80 exactly, and the delivered board reads 0.4381 and 0.4811 at the same heights, both inside tol - the delivered pair silhouette tracks because the bind pose splays the legs (gap grows 12px at z=1.25 to 32px at z=0.80) even though each leg tapers. So: a provenance forgery, not a visible silhouette defect. It must still be re-traced, because the file asserts a trace it did not perform. GARMENTS. Real construction exists: the shoe has a distinct cupsole band, a dark outsole edge, a toe bumper and three lace grooves (4x crop x160-380,y560-660); the sleeve ends in a proud ribbed cuff ring; a hood and a placket were authored. But the placket is the detached bar described under silhouette - in lefty-runtime-run.png it reads as two loose vertical straps standing proud of the chest with daylight behind them, not as a jacket front. There is no zipper, no pocket, no hem band and none of the concept's white piping on sleeve or body. The jogger's rolled cuff is authored CUFF #2E2F36 against PANTS - the two values are indistinguishable at render, so the concept's clearly banded ankle cuff reads as nothing. The navy hood, which is a defining front-of-figure feature in the drawing (a dark collar V at the neck), is invisible in both front board views and shows only as a small dark patch behind the shoulder in profile. TEAM_MASK extent only, no colour judgement: the declared accent is a single small rectangle on the cap crown, roughly a tenth of cap width, where the concept carries a full-width band across the cap's front closure - the accent surface is under-extended.

faceExpressionRead.label: face/expression read
faceExpressionRead.note: The strongest category and the only thing near passing. All four runtime-face stills are genuinely painted and genuinely distinct - I diffed them pairwise at raw-channel level and every pair differs (grin/tongue 2.83% of channels by >12, grin/angry 2.37%, grin/cheer 2.24%, cheer/tongue 1.61%, tongue/angry 1.49%, and the closest pair cheer/angry still 0.64%). 3.14 passes on the evidence: the grin opens with real teeth, tongue puts a modelled pink tongue over a lower lip, and both read at card distance. The nose is a real form that breaks the profile silhouette, not a sticker. The near-side eye in the true 90-degree profile is a foreshortened sliver, which is expected and which I am not filing. Ears are constructed - EarSpec/build_ear are in the script at lines 34/137-139 and the 8x profile crop shows outer rim, inner concha shadow and a lobe against the skull, so 3.10 passes. Against that: 3.13 FAILS on measurement, head width:height 0.88 vs 0.98 concept, delta -0.10 on a 0.08 tolerance, and the rubric says outright that a head sculpted narrower than its concept never reads as the same kid. There are visible atlas seam dashes on the neck below the jaw (8x crop x470-560,y290-350 of the grin still) and a tone step where the saturated face region meets the paler neck. The idle/neutral mouth reads as a downturned frown at the gameplay camera rather than the concept's soft confident smile. Face is a form, mostly - but a narrow one with a visible island boundary, so this is a 3, not a 4.

heroAndFieldScale.label: hero and field scale
heroAndFieldScale.note: The hero close-up is fine: at 1059x804 the face, cap and jacket all read and the review page reports 'model model' (4.1 satisfied, not proxy evidence). The 40px strip is where it collapses. What survives is orange top + tan cap + dark pants + pale shoes - a generic capped kid. Her one memorable read is blonde hair and a ponytail escaping a backwards cap, and at 40px the blonde is gone entirely; on the board's own 40px tile I can find no yellow pixels. Worse, it is nearly gone at the ACTUAL gameplay camera too - lefty-runtime-hero.png and lefty-runtime-run.png at the 3/4 field angle show a single thin yellow ribbon at the sideburn and a scrap at the cap's back edge; the ponytail is invisible in the run still. The pants also render near-black at the gameplay camera rather than the concept's navy, further flattening the read. And the one angle where the hair IS large - swing_contact - is the angle where it becomes a slab intersecting the jacket. 3.9 (the 40px zoom strip still shows the one memorable read) fails.

measuredFidelity.result: MEASURE:FIDELITY (run by me, 2026-08-16): concept front 211x662px, delivered 450x556px; shoe tones read off the concept #fbeddc and #947b5b. head height as % of figure 28.4 -> 29.7, delta +1.28 ok. head width:height 0.98 -> 0.88, delta -0.10 OFF (tol 0.08). shoe band dominant tone 72.8 -> 77.7 ok. shoe band second tone 26.4 -> 22.3 ok. shoe band mean saturation 21.9 -> 18.2 ok. daylight between the ankles 0.00 -> 31.4 OFF (tol 12). visible face left of centre 27.6 -> 34.2 OFF (+6.68, tol 6). visible face right of centre 28.6 -> 34.9 OFF (+6.28, tol 6). face left/right asymmetry 0.00 -> 0.68 ok. 4 of 9 metrics outside tolerance. MEASURE:STRANDS (four bands, all run by me): default 5-45% -> concept 7.60 minima/row at prominence 36.1 over 80 rows, delivered 0.58 at 24.7 over 67 rows = 8% of count, 69% of prominence. 5-35% (the pure crown/cap band; lefty's hair is under a backwards cap so the default band is cap on both sheets) -> 10% of count, 77% of prominence. 35-75% -> 47% of count but 192% of prominence, and 45-95% -> 55% at 203%; I DISCARD both lower bands as contaminated - they reach the painted eyes, brows and mouth, and a painted eye registers a far deeper minimum than any hair groove, which is exactly what the >190% prominence figures are telling us. Honest band reading: 8-10% of the concept's strand count. MY OWN MEASUREMENTS: (1) Profile silhouette severance - full row scan of lefty-profile-review.png at alpha>40: rows 288-310, 23 consecutive rows (4.1% of the 557px figure height), split into two runs, the left one a 10-11px placket bar at x226-237 with a transparent gap of 8px at row 288 narrowing to 2px at row 310; body run x238-337. Island colour sampled #7e3101 at (231,295) = jacket orange. Also rows 124-134, an 11-row 2-3px cap-coloured splinter (#c8bdad at (231,124)); also rows 203-206, a 7-9px blonde island at x341-349; also rows 329-330, a 1-3px island at x313-315. Front board carries the same placket separation at row 280 (island x226-234 vs body x241-327) and rows 228-229. (2) Leg daylight, my own scan of lefty-front-review.png y440-600: 159 consecutive rows with exactly two runs, max inter-leg daylight 56.0% of row span at y=597 - 3.12 PASSES, confirmed independently, gap grows monotonically 6px at z=1.40 to 50px at z=0.50. (3) LEG_STATIONS provenance: `diff` of sculpt-lefty-source.py:531-545 against sculpt-dex-source.py:518-532 returns EMPTY - byte-identical including comments. The shared comment's pixel citation '139-268 at z 1.40 across both' matches dex's traced jeans runs (132-200 and 214-270 at his row y=596) and does NOT match lefty's (108-173 and 182-247 at her row y=606). Lefty's own per-leg halves from her sheet: 0.1963ft at z=1.40, 0.1842 at z=1.25, 0.1752 at z=0.80; the copied table gives 0.1972 / 0.1930 / 0.1794 - max error +0.009ft (+5%) at z=1.25, inside the 0.04 tol. The two '# measured:' pair-outer lines above the table ARE lefty's own: I reproduced 0.4441 at z=1.25 (px 105-252) and 0.5136 at z=0.80 (px 96-266) exactly; delivered reads 0.4381 and 0.4811 at those heights, both inside tol, because the bind pose splays. Verdict: the table is COPIED FROM DEX, the provenance comment is dex's trace pasted verbatim, and the numeric consequence happens to be small. (4) Profile torso depth: 84px at y=360, 83px at y=420, 96px at y=300 - a constant-depth slab, ~0.60ft. (5) Blonde coverage of the delivered head box (x150-400, y90-254, hue 40-75 / sat>0.30): 1507 of 19008 figure pixels = 7.9%. (6) Face stills pairwise raw-channel diff (>12 on any channel): grin/cheer 2.238%, grin/tongue 2.827%, grin/angry 2.372%, cheer/tongue 1.605%, cheer/angry 0.636%, tongue/angry 1.494% - all four genuinely painted and distinct. (7) Builders grepped before any absence claim: EarSpec/build_ear present (lines 34, 137-139, 706), build_cap (221), build_side_hair (384), build_hood (407), shoe sole/toe-cap/lace profiles (589-683) - I filed no feature as absent that the script builds. (8) 4x/8x crops taken of every region cited: head front, head profile, both shoulder junctions, the placket, the cap splinter, the nape shard, the feet, the swing ponytail, the run torso, the face seams. The profile chest 'knob' I first suspected turned out to be the near HAND seen end-on in T-pose (it moves to the wrist in the A-pose profile) - NOT filed.
measuredFidelity.note: Her ear line gates at 67.0 (real, under the cap edge); featurelatitude gates brow 54.4 vs traced 54.3, eye 59.9 vs 59.9, mouth 79.1 vs bounded 79.0 through her 3.99-2.80 span. The backwards cap reverses BRIM_REACH (+0.78 rearward); the analyser refuses her brow and eye bands (cap shadow merges them) and the recipe records the tee living in the backdrop's cream cluster. The tail is TWO tubes after a first critic rejected the all-deep compromise as a 'dark strap': a thin deep-tone gather crosses the faceSkin sample band, and the full lit-blonde volume hangs entirely below the measured row - blonde and voluminous without falsifying the face metric. Its depth hugs the nape (Rocket's daylight lesson) and the backwards brim is held at 0.56 reach (a fuller sweep seals an enclosed window against the pony's crown in profile).

polishFindings: PROUD PANEL DETACHES IN PROFILE (re-characterised from a severance claim, which measurement disproved): the jacket placket opens 32 rows of background between itself and the chest in both profile views, up to 12px, reading as a floating slab at 10x. The figure is ONE connected component in all four views. Same class as dex's kangaroo pocket. Fix by blending the panel's edges into the torso rather than standing it off.

TWO MORE DETACHED ISLANDS in the profile silhouette: an 11-row 2-3px cap splinter at the crown front (y124-134) and a 7-9px blonde island off the back of the head (y203-206), plus a 1-3px speck at y329-330. All are 3.7 violations.

NO HAIRLINE FROM THE FRONT (3.3): the forehead is bare skin from brow to cap edge. measure:fidelity puts visible face at 34.2%/34.9% against the concept's 27.6%/28.6%, both beyond the 6-point tolerance - the delivered shows ~24% more bare face than the drawing on both sides. Author a fringe under the cap's front edge.

HAIR IS FLAT CARDS WITH KNIFE-CUT EDGES, not a mass: at 7x the near-side hair is three separate ribbons with straight-cut bottoms and individual outline strokes, one cutting across the ear's back rim. 8-10% of the concept's strand count on the honest band.

PONYTAIL INTERPENETRATES THE JACKET at swing_contact: the ponytail card passes in front of the orange sleeve and ends in a squared-off flat cut over the torso (crop x470-630,y180-450 of lefty-runtime-swing.png). This is a shipped clip, not a bind-pose artefact.

BARE-SKULL READ AT THE GAMEPLAY CAMERA (3.3, 3.9): at the 3/4 field angle in the hero and run stills the blonde survives as one thin sideburn ribbon; the ponytail is not visible at all in the run still, and no blonde survives the 40px tile. Her one memorable feature does not reach the player.

LEG_STATIONS COPIED FROM DEX, not traced from lefty (proven): the table is byte-identical to sculpt-dex-source.py:518-532 and the comment's pixel citation '139-268 at z 1.40 across both' is dex's trace - lefty's own jeans runs at that height are 108-173 and 182-247. Re-trace from her sheet; the errors are small (max +5% at z=1.25) but the file asserts a measurement it did not take, and sculpt-provenance is a gate that is currently being satisfied by another kid's homework.
HEAD IS 10% TOO NARROW (3.13 board-vs-turnaround fail): width:height 0.88 delivered against 0.98 concept, tolerance 0.08.

NO DELTOID AT THE SLEEVE/TORSO JUNCTION: the sleeve cylinder butt-joins a straight vertical torso wall with a crease notch, both sides. No fin is being sheared, but no shoulder form exists either (3.11 risk).
PROFILE TORSO IS A CONSTANT-DEPTH SLAB: 84px at y=360, 83px at y=420 - no chest, no waist, no back curve.

THE JOGGER CUFF READS AS NOTHING: authored CUFF #2E2F36 is indistinguishable from PANTS at render, so the concept's clearly banded ribbed ankle cuff disappears. Lighten or darken the cuff swatch, or make it proud enough to catch a terminator.
THE NAVY HOOD IS INVISIBLE FROM THE FRONT where the concept makes it a defining dark collar V at the neck; it survives only as a small patch behind the shoulder in profile.

MISSING GARMENT DETAIL the concept carries: zipper and pull, two front pockets, white piping lines on sleeve and body, a ribbed jacket hem band. The hem is currently a flat horizontal cut into the pants.

TEAM_MASK EXTENT (extent only, no colour judgement): the declared accent is one small rectangle on the cap crown, roughly a tenth of cap width, where the concept carries a full-width band across the cap's front closure. Under-extended.
ANKLE DAYLIGHT 31.4 vs the concept's 0.00 (tol 12) - read this as a stance note, not a tolerance to widen: her drawn stance closes at the ankles and the bind pose splays.
FACE ATLAS SEAM DASHES visible on the neck below the jaw at hero scale, with a tone step where the saturated face region meets the paler neck (3.5's decal-island clause).

NOT A DEFECT, recorded so it is not re-filed: 3.12 passes - 159 rows of two legs, max daylight 56.0% of row span, measured by me. The profile chest 'knob' is the near hand seen end-on in T-pose. Ears are constructed (rim, concha, lobe). All four face stills are genuinely painted and distinct.
